Share ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Emmy Award winner Kristen Bell is under fire after Fox News announced she would be joining its expanding Christian content initiative , a decision that seemingly fractured part of her longtime fanbase. The announcement came as a surprise for her followers, especially since she previously described herself as non-religious and said she identifies as a humanist. Highlights Some fans blasted Kristen Bell for joining a Fox Christian project despite describing herself as non religious. Supporters argued she has the right to work on any production without being attacked for it. Others accused the post of turning a Jesus podcast into a political fight it never needed to be. Moreover, Bell has a history of supporting liberal-leaning causes, including campaigning for Barack Obama in 2008, backing the Writers Guild during the 2007 strike, and advocating for veganism. “Kristen Bell working for Fox News?” a fan asked on X. “Well, I guess everyone whose work I have loved since childhood, just wants to self-cancel this year, huh.” RELATED: Fans accused Kristen Bell of betraying her beliefs after it was announced that she had been hired for a Fox News Christian production Kristen Bell wearing a black off-shoulder top, looking at the camera with a neutral expression, joining Fox Faith Project. Image credits: Instagram/kristenanniebell ADVERTISEMENT The project at the center of the outrage is The Life of Jesus Podcast , a 52-episode production that Fox News Media is positioning as a cornerstone of its growing “Fox Faith” initiative. Bell was revealed as the voice of Mary Magdalene, acting alongside Sean Astin, Neal McDonough, Brian Cox, Malcolm McDowell, John Rhys-Davies, and Julia Ormond. To say the decision divided her fanbase would be an understatement. Couple sitting on outdoor steps with Kristen Bell, highlighting outrage after joining Fox Faith Project in media news. Image credits: Netflix The loudest group argued that Bell should never collaborate with Fox in any capacity, regardless of the project. These fans believe the network stands in direct opposition to Bell’s publicly stated values. “She has a net worth of 60M and a hit Netflix show,” a fan argued, questioning Bell’s decision to accept the job. “She needs neither money nor a job.” ADVERTISEMENT Kristen Bell smiling and seated during a talk show interview discussing Fox Faith Project and related controversy. Image credits: Getty/NBC Others defended the actress , dismissing the outrage entirely. They argued that an actor has the right to accept any role without being forced into an ideological battle. Moreover, they questioned why a depiction of Jesus should be treated as a political endorsement. “Since when are we canceling people for talking about the life of Jesus?” another asked. According to executives, religious content is among the most sought-after categories on their streaming service, Fox Nation Tweet on a social media platform expressing outrage over Kristen Bell joining Fox Faith project. Image credits: TVTweets2026 ADVERTISEMENT Kristen Bell in a red dress with fur trim, sparking outrage after joining Fox Faith Project, shown with two men in separate frames. Image credits: Instagram For Fox News Media , the decision is all about satisfying their viewers. The network believes religious programming is a high-growth area for its audience and its streaming service, Fox Nation. Kristen Bell speaking on Fox Faith Project, sparking outrage amid self-cancel discussions in a studio setting. Image credits: Getty/John Lamparski According to Jason Klarman, chief digital and marketing officer at Fox News Media, the network is trying to address what he called an “insatiable appetite” for this type of content from “a very passionate audience that is underserved.” ADVERTISEMENT Twitter post criticizing Kristen Bell's decision, mentioning self-cancel and Fox Faith project controversy. Image credits: X/effoff1988 ADVERTISEMENT He explained that Fox is simply following the data. Shows such as Ainsley’s Bible Study consistently spike during holiday seasons, and books from Fox News personalities who write about biblical themes perform strongly. Klarman said faith-based content delivers the best engagement and acquisition among Fox Nation’s offerings. Kristen Bell with long hair and brown top making a pouting face, sparking outrage over Fox Faith Project involvement Image credits: Instagram/kristenanniebell “I just am excited that more people are open to talking about faith ,” said Ainsley Earhardt, who introduces each episode of the Jesus podcast. She explained that, in today’s stressful media environment, she believes this type of content can help parents and believers find guidance. For some fans, the issue had more to do with her political beliefs than her spiritual ones Kristen Bell speaking with eyes closed and hand raised, sparking outrage over Fox Faith Project involvement. Image credits: Instagram/kristenanniebell The backlash against Bell continues to grow because fans view this as more than a single project. To them, it signals alignment with a political and cultural ecosystem they believe goes against her beliefs. Bell supported and campaigned for Barack Obama during the 2008 United States presidential election. Along with actress Rashida Jones, she visited college campuses in Missouri to encourage voter registration. Kristen Bell smiling with a man in a casual setting, sparking outrage after joining Fox Faith Project. Image credits: Instagram/kristenanniebell She has also been clear about her spiritual beliefs. Bell has said she is non-religious and identified herself as a humanist. So far, Bell has not addressed the controversy. Kristen Bell smiling in a black dress with layered necklaces and bracelets, standing against a beige curtain backdrop. Image credits: Instagram/kristenanniebell For Fox News, Bell’s participation is a calculated move. The company is betting that adding a recognizable mainstream actress will strengthen Fox Nation’s performance within its growing faith-focused audience. “If you are this upset over someone doing a podcast about faith, which they don’t control the distribution of, you should probably re-evaluate some things,” a user argued. “Major stars know what they sign for,” another replied. “Problematic.” Some netizens argued the move could negatively impact Bell’s career Screenshot of a tweet reacting to Kristen Bell sparking outrage after joining Fox Faith Project. Share ADVERTISEMENT Several well-known actors, including Kristen Bell , Malcolm McDowell , and John Rhys-Davies , have broken their silence amidst the controversy surrounding Fox News’ The Life of Jesus podcast. According to representatives of the stars, many performers had no knowledge that their voices were being used for the upcoming podcast, with some claiming that the recordings actually came from a separate biblical project that was completed 15 years ago. Netizens remain split on the matter. Highlights Multiple actors said they had no idea their voices would appear in a Fox News biblical podcast. Representatives claimed audio recorded 15 years ago was being reused without new consent. Fox News has stated that the project was licensed “with full cooperation and participation” from everyone involved. RELATED: As it turns out, Fox News ’ The Life of Jesus podcast uses repurposed audio from a biblical project way back in 2010 Kristen Bell smiling in a black sleeveless top, speaking out after backlash over Fox News religious podcast. Image credits: Instagram/kristenanniebell On Wednesday, Fox News promoted a star-studded voice cast, including Kristen Bell as Mary Magdalene, Malcolm McDowell as Caiaphas, Neal McDonough as Jesus, and Brian Cox as God, for a 52-episode biblical podcast series called The Life of Jesus . ADVERTISEMENT The podcast is produced by Gulfstream Studios, and it is expected to launch under the network’s Fox Faith vertical. Each episode of the series will be complete with introductions from Fox & Friends host Ainsley Earhardt. Kristen Bell and other actors pictured with stained glass windows, addressing backlash over Fox News religious podcast. Image credits: Fox News Social media erupted, with many critics slamming stars like Bell for participating in a religious project. Soon, representatives for multiple actors stepped forward with shocking messages: their clients didn’t even know about The Life of Jesus podcast. According to Entertainment Weekly , the actors involved said they “had no knowledge” of the podcast and only learned of it this week. Kristen Bell speaking on stage in a white suit addressing backlash after Fox News religious podcast controversy. Image credits: Getty/Michael Buckner ADVERTISEMENT Confusion deepened when it became clear that the project relied heavily on audio originally recorded for a completely different production, the 2010 Truth & Life Dramatized Audio Bible . Her representative stressed that Bell never granted permission for her old audio to be reused. “This is the actual and factual story,” Bell’s representatives told EW . Smiling man in black suit and glasses posing at an event related to Kristen Bell and Fox News religious podcast backlash. Season 2 holds the #1 spot on the platform's official Top 10 global TV shows. Even season 1 has found its way back on top, taking up the list's #7 spot. So, this rom-com isn't likely to go anywhere any time soon. The streaming platform is banking on viewership, and with both seasons sitting in the top 10, a new batch of episodes is a sound investment. Of course, it's possible that season 2's 56% Rotten Tomatoes score will come back to bite Netflix in the butt. Those viewers who found Nobody Wants This ' sophomore outing unfavorable may choose to skip over season 3, resulting in a drop in viewership. Kristen Bell , Josh Gad , and Idina Menzel reportedly have each secured huge salaries to return for Frozen 3 and Frozen 4, making it one of the richest payouts in animation history. Frozen 3’s Kristen Bell, Josh Gad and Idina Menzel secure massive paydays Kristen Bell, Josh Gad, and Idina Menzel, who voice Anna, Olaf, and Elsa, will reportedly receive a combination of upfront fees and box-office-based bonuses totaling more than $60 million across the two upcoming sequels. Each actor is expected to earn close to $20 million upfront per film, with the remainder tied to performance-based payouts. The new salaries represent a steep jump from their Frozen 2 earnings, which stood at around $15 million for each. An executive close to the negotiations told TheWrap that the payments will be made over several years and are not going to be given as a single lump sum. Disney hasn’t yet commented on the reported figures. The massive paydays are a reflection of the continued commercial strength of the Frozen brand. The first film earned $1.3 billion globally, while Frozen 2 surpassed that in 2019 with $1.4 billion. Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen’s The Snow Queen, the original 2013 film became a cultural phenomenon, winning Oscars for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Song for “Let It Go.” Its impact extended far beyond theaters as the franchise remains one of Disney’s most profitable. It is bolstered by worldwide merchandise sales, theme-park attractions, touring productions, cruise ship experiences, and global stage adaptations. Now, Jennifer Lee, who directed the first two films, is returning to direct Frozen 3, this time alongside Trent Correy, the filmmaker behind Disney’s 2023 short Once Upon a Studio. Longtime producer Peter Del Vecho and songwriters Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez will also return. Disney has slated Frozen 3 for a Thanksgiving 2027 release on November 24. Frozen 4 currently has no confirmed date but reportedly remains in active development. Originally reported by Devanshi Basu on ComingSoon . Ginnifer Goodwin and Jason Bateman ’s return as Officer Judy Hopps and Nick Wilde in ‘Zootopia 2’ has been much appreciated by the public. The first film was released all the way back in 2016 and managed to garner a lot of love and attention worldwide. In a recent interview, the star delved into recording for the hit animated film and why she wishes for the next film to come sooner. Ginnifer Goodwin shares how she and Jason Bateman had to be separated while recording Ginnifer Goodwin, who voices the main character Judy Hopps, recently revealed how it was to record for the second installment of the franchise. While talking about her co-star Bateman with The Hollywood Reporter, the actress hilariously confessed that the two were not allowed to record their lines together and had to be separated every time. She further provided context, adding that, “I get the giggles really, really, really badly. I waste everyone’s time. He can’t not make me laugh. They built these booths where they are going to be able to put us. If we can get a third one, they can put us in the same space, and I won’t ruin all the takes because if I’m laughing, they can isolate that sound out. We have to do this just so I can experience it and not just have to wonder what it is he did in his recording. ” Ginnifer Goodwin opens up about the film and expectations for the third installment The second installment of the film was released almost a decade after the first film, and Goodwin revealed during the interview that she had been itching to get back in the studio. “I would call them every year and I’d be like, ‘Is this the year?’ And they’d be like, ‘We’re really busy with a lot of things, just hold on tight.’ So I was waiting and waiting,” she further revealed. While talking about the next film, she shared that the wait time is not as long and that she is “trying to manifest a number three, after a much shorter break. Dallas, for his part, complemented his wife in a beige suit, while Oliver and Hugo twinned in black suits with respective square-shaped glasses. Dallas and Goodwin met on the set of ABC’s Once Upon a Time , where they played Prince Charming and Snow White. Soon after portraying an onscreen couple, the two actors sparked a real-life romance. It’s like, how could you not [fall in love]?” The Manifest alum and Goodwin got married in 2014, shortly before welcoming Oliver that same year. Hugo followed two years later in 2016. “Every day is a milestone,” Dallas told Us in 2015 after Oliver’s arrival . “He can climb the stairs like a ninja [and] hold his own bottle. Every day, there’s a milestone that amazes you as a parent. … Sleep is elusive — a slippery devil. I can’t seem to ever catch it. There’s somebody else that you have to take care of, you don’t think about yourself anymore. The team working behind the first Zootopia film ignored the directions they were given to add certain number of puns in the write up. In conversation with SFX magazine, he added that the first movie featured only five puns, but they have taken it to a whole new level for the second film. "I do love a pun. On the first film, we got a note that said, 'You can have a total of five puns in this movie”, added the writer. He continued, "This is absolutely true. It was early on. We disregarded that note and put a billion in there." In the new sequel featuring Jason Batman and Ginnifer Goodwin, besides the puns in character names and dialogues, audience will get to see signs reimagined versions of iconic brands. While talking about Zootopia 2 , Bush said, "You'll see a ton of advertisements and brand labels. It is aggressive and we love it." Without giving much spoilers, the screenwriter added that the most iconic pun appears when Nick is look on something called HuluZoo streaming service. Directed by Bush and Byron Howard, the upcoming animated includes voiceovers by Shakira Macaulay Culkin, Robert Irwin, Ke Huy Quan and many more. Zootopia 2 is slated to release on November 26. For those dreamers wishing for a sequel to 'Something Borrowed', it's time to temper those expectations. During their chat on the 'Sibling Revelry' podcast, both Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin delivered the bittersweet news: a sequel is nearly impossible. With Goodwin sharing that as she nears the big 5-0, the character's age dilemma hits closer to home than ever before. The duo Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin are best known for their 90s chick-flick film ‘Something Borrowed.’ In a season where old classics are getting remakes and prequels (‘Freakier Friday’ and ‘Practical Magic 2), fans had been wondering whether the two beloved stars would be open to reuniting for a sequel to ‘Something Borrowed’ or not. Recently in an interview, the two formally put all questions and rumors to rest. Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin share insights about ‘Something Borrowed’ sequel On November 24, Kate Hudson invited Goodwin on her and her brother, Oliver Hudson’s, podcast titled ‘Sibling Revelry’ in order to get candid and talk about her career as an actress. During one of the segments of the show, the conversation drifted to their 2011 release, ‘Something Borrowed.’ Hudson shared that she had mentioned the project on multiple occasions, but it never ended up happening. She added, “I was saying to Ollie that I get asked about [a sequel] on the [red] carpet all the time. I was on the carpet not that long ago, and they were like, ‘What’s the movie that you would want to do the sequel [to]? And I was like, ‘Well, Something Borrowed, we never got to do the sequel.” Ginnifer also added that she would no longer be open to a project like that anymore. She added, “I would not want to go back and do Something Blue at this point.” Kate ended up adding, “I mean, we’re kind of too old.” The two set the record straight during the podcast and shared how the project never happened, and they would no longer be interested in it as well. Goodwin even talked about how she had a monologue in the film about spiralling and turning 30, and that she would not feel okay with it as she is now turning 50. She further shared that, “My sons, their girlfriends at school, they’ve been learning the dance. I’ve got a bunch of 12 year olds… I show up, I’m the assistant librarian when I’m not doing other things. And I have shown up on campus and had the girls be like, Mrs. Dallas, look. ” About ‘Something Borrowed’ The film was originally based on a 2005 romantic comedy novel written by author Emily Griffin. A sequel book titled ‘Something Blue’ was also published, and a script was already in the works as per PopSugar; however, no updates have been shared about the sequel with the public, leading everyone to believe that the case is cold. Sarah, who played Shiv Roy in Succession, happily posed with Brian, who starred as her dad Logan on the smash hit series. Smith Cameron who played Gerri Kellman, Arian Moayed who starred at Stewy Hosseini, Cherry Jones who appeared as Nan Pearce, Berry Schneider actress Jihae and Dagmara Dominczyk, who played Head of PR Karolina on the show. Nicholas' public show of support for Sarah comes after he was court-ordered in September to cease using any drugs or alcohol in the wake of his DUI arrest in New Hampshire . Nicholas, 37, entered a plea of not guilty to a DUI-Impairment charge in the August 29 incident. He was also charged with operating his car without lights in the incident; due to police cameras malfunctioning, his mug shot was not snapped. While the actor is out on bail, the court has ordered him to cease 'any use of alcohol, and use of any narcotic drug or controlled substance,' People reported after reviewing court docs. In addition to his efforts in front of the camera, Nicholas is also a busy restaurateur as he owns a piece of a number of bars and restaurants. The actor was nominated for three Primetime Emmys for his work on the show as the Roy family cousin. Sarah meanwhile was also nominated for three Emmys during her time on the show, scooping the win in 2023 during the final season. In 2017, Zimbabwe’s 93-year-old president, Robert Mugabe, resigned; he was facing impeachment proceedings and had been placed under house arrest by the military. His resignation ended a 37-year rule beginning with Zimbabwe’s independence in 1980. In 2021, an SUV sped through barricades and into marchers in a Christmas parade in the Milwaukee suburb of Waukesha, killing six people and injuring several others. A judge the following year sentenced Darrell Brooks Jr. to life in prison without parole for his conviction on first-degree intentional homicide and other counts. In 2022, a powerful earthquake killed at least 162 people and injured hundreds on Indonesia’s main island of Java, sending terrified residents into streets covered with debris. Also in 2022, NASA’s uncrewed Orion capsule reached the moon, whipping around the far side and buzzing the lunar surface on an orbit that broke the record for distance traveled by a spacecraft designed to carry humans. (AP Photo/George Walker IV) NEW YORK (AP) -- The top prize of entertainer of the year at the 2025 Country Music Association Awards went to none other than Lainey Wilson, who hosted, performed and barely left the stage Wednesday night. "It takes a village," she said in her acceptance speech. "We about to party." She beat out Luke Combs, Cody Johnson, Chris Stapleton and Morgan Wallen, last year's winner in the category. Earlier in the night, she won album of the year for "Whirlwind" -- marking her second career win in the category -- and earned the trophy for female vocalist of the year. It was her fourth time winning that title. She celebrated other women in country music -- and had a few choice words for those who don't. "For the folks that are sitting at home, in your mama's basement, eating your Cheetos, trying to pit women against each other," she concluded her speech. "Y'all need to find something better to do." Collider praised it for being a "modern-day Columbo " and noted that Rian Johnson (the man behind the Knives Out films) had proven that "he's the maestro of modern mysteries." Poker Face set up a unique storytelling style , with famous guest stars popping up in every new episode. Everyone from Chloë Sevigny and Melanie Lynskey to Cherry Jones and Katie Holmes has made appearances. In its two seasons, Poker Face also managed to earn six Emmy nominations , with a win for Judith Light for Season 1. The show seemed to be a hit for the streamer until a surprising announcement last week changed Poker Face 's potential future. What Is 'Poker Face' About? Natasha Lyonne as Charlie Cale sitting in a car with her left leg up on the steering wheel in Poker Face Image via Peacock Poker Face follows an intriguing protagonist named Charlie Cale, played by Natasha Lyonne . The extraordinary thing about Charlie is that she's a human lie detector and can instantly tell when anyone on Earth is so much as fibbing. Of course, this gets Charlie in all kinds of trouble , because she's either seen as a weapon by dangerous people or as a threat. Charlie gets pursued by some pretty unsavory folks, but what results is a wild journey that is completely compelling to go on. Charlie's gift (and her wanderlust) allow her to travel around meeting all kinds of different people from various walks of life, but every episode she's sucked into a new mystery that she must solve. This also allows the show to traverse a wide variety of settings, from Vegas to the Big Apple. Whether Charlie's going head-to-head with a gangster played by Adrien Brody , or a gaggle of sisters all played by Cynthia Erivo , each episode brims with electric, suspenseful mysteries told in an incredibly inventive way. Posts By Rob London Nov 13, 2025 'Poker Face' Is Ending With Season 2 on Peacock, but There's a Twist Poker Face has been a critical hit for Peacock, so that made it all the more surprising when it was unceremoniously cancelled by the streamer . Although the ratings were down a bit from the first season, there weren't a lot of rumors about it getting the ax. Johnson is insisting that this isn't the end of the road for Charlie Cale, and it's been reported that the show will be shopped around to other networks/streamers to see if the series can be saved. However, Johnson's actual plan for future episodes is pretty shocking. Instead of Lyonne returning as Charlie, the role would be recast for Season 3 with Peter Dinklage taking over the character. It's unclear exactly how this would play out, but Johnson mentioned possibly recasting the lead character every two seasons to shake things up even further. There are examples of other shows that have done this, but it was more out of necessity than just a desperate move to regain viewer interest. The Crown took on this strategy, but this made sense because actors needed to switch up with the passage of time for these real-life characters. There have been notable recastings for shows like Bewitched , Fresh Prince of Bel-Air , and Roseanne , but this isn't actually a method that should be implemented unless absolutely necessary. Johnson stated that this plan is something the team has been thinking about, per an exclusive with Deadline , "We've been germinating this next move together since writing the Season 2 finale. We love our Poker Face and this is the perfect way to keep it rolling." Well, we'll have to disagree. 'Poker Face' Should End If Natasha Lyonne Leaves Natasha Lyonne as Charlie Cale leaning against her blue Barracuda in Poker Face Season 2 Image via Peacock It's likely that Lyonne would stay on as executive producer for future Poker Face episodes, but we're not entirely sold on the idea that a recasting would actually work . Johnson probably thinks that the plan to bring in a new leading actor would breathe fresh life into the show, or perhaps reel in more viewers who want to check out the new iteration. However, getting rid of Lyonne's version of Charlie would just completely change the magic of what made Poker Face special in the first place. This natural blend of comedy and drama allowed the series to capitalize on both its quirkiness and its fun sensibility, and Lyonne has a masterful ability to play off the multitude of incredible guest stars every episode. Saying goodbye to Lyonne's Charlie would be a total mistake. That's not to say that Dinklage isn't a fantastic actor. His recent turns in both Dexter: Resurrection and The Lowdown have demonstrated that the actor can take on a breadth of roles . He certainly proved his worth in his Emmy-winning part in Game of Thrones . Of course, Dinklage deserves to be a leading man. It's just that we're not sure that Poker Face is the vehicle to do it. Fans of the series are already connected to Lyonne's Charlie, and seeing the character reworked in this way would only ruin the vibe that the show has established. The time to make this switch, if any, would have been after the first season. If Poker Face had been billed more as an anthology series , with new leading actors after every season, this massive change might have been easier to swallow. Dinklage deserves his own series to lead, rather than being offered to replace another actor. It's a shame that Peacock has cancelled Poker Face , but at this point, fans will likely be happier just saying goodbye to the series for good, rather than adjusting to someone else in the role every two seasons. We applaud Johnson's creativity in coming up with a potential solution for the cancellation, but we'd rather leave Charlie Cale as she is than see her completely reworked . It's okay to let things end if it's truly their time, and the two seasons of Poker Face with Lyonne in the lead are a perfectly fine high note to go out on. There are 40 days left in the year. Today in history: On Nov. 21, 1980, 85 people died, most from smoke inhalation, after a fire broke out at the MGM Grand Hotel in Las Vegas, Nev. Also on this date: In 1920, on “Bloody Sunday,” the Irish Republican Army killed 14 suspected British intelligence officers in the Dublin area; British forces responded by raiding a soccer match, killing 14 civilians. In 1964, New York City's Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, at the time the longest suspension bridge in the world, was opened to traffic. In 1980, an estimated 83 million TV viewers tuned in to the CBS prime-time soap opera “Dallas” to find out “who shot J.R.” (The shooter turned out to be J.R. Ewing’s sister-in-law, Kristin Shepard.) In 1985, U.S. Navy intelligence analyst Jonathan Jay Pollard was arrested and accused of spying for Israel. (Pollard later pleaded guilty to espionage and was sentenced to life in prison, but was released in 2015.) In 1990, junk-bond financier Michael R. Milken, who had pleaded guilty to six felony counts related to violating U.S. securities laws by selling junk bonds, was sentenced by a federal judge in New York to 10 years in prison. (Milken served two.) In 1995, Balkan leaders meeting in Dayton, Ohio, initialed a peace plan to end 3 1/2 years of ethnic fighting in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In 2017, Zimbabwe’s 93-year-old president, Robert Mugabe, resigned; he was facing impeachment proceedings and had been placed under house arrest by the military. His resignation ended a 37-year rule beginning with Zimbabwe's independence in 1980. In 2021, an SUV sped through barricades and into marchers in a Christmas parade in the Milwaukee suburb of Waukesha, killing six people and injuring several others. A judge the following year sentenced Darrell Brooks Jr. to life in prison without parole for his conviction on first-degree intentional homicide and other counts. In 2022, a powerful earthquake killed at least 162 people and injured hundreds on Indonesia’s main island of Java, sending terrified residents into streets covered with debris. Also in 2022, NASA’s uncrewed Orion capsule reached the moon, whipping around the far side and buzzing the lunar surface on an orbit that broke the record for distance traveled by a spacecraft designed to carry humans. The mission marked the first time an American capsule visited the moon since NASA’s Apollo program ended a half-century earlier. Today’s Birthdays: Actor Marlo Thomas is 88. Arabia Awards 2025 red carpet on Saturday in Doha, Qatar. Styled by duo Brit and Kara Elkin, Roberts turned to Valentino ’s resort 2026 collection for her attire. The dress, crafted in a blush pink tone, featured a sheer neckline and long sleeves with a cutout above the bustline and a button at the base of the neckline. Emma Roberts at the Fashion Trust Arabia 2025 Awards Ceremony on Nov. 22, 2025 in Doha, Qatar. The “American Horror Story” actress also added a cocktail ring to her look. As for glam, Roberts’ chestnut hair featured a soft wave and was parted down the middle with makeup highlights including bold brows and a glossy lip. Emma Roberts wears Valentino at the Fashion Trust Arabia 2025 Awards Ceremony on Nov. 22, 2025 in Doha, Qatar. Getty Images Creative director Alessandro Michele showcased Valentino’s resort 2026 collection in a dreamscape that saw the Italian luxury fashion house models in various states of sleep on beds captured in a photo-scape. “The women’s offering was utterly feminine, with all its chiffon dresses; polka dot ruched gowns; bouclé sets in candy tones; bon-ton skirt suits, and girly A-line dresses with cutouts, as well as cute cropped cardigans with lace inserts paired with pencil skirts with feathery trims to create pastel colorblocking,” Sandra Saliban wrote in WWD’s review of the collection. Emma Roberts Getty Images “The collection charmingly ping-ponged between the ornamental and the streamlined, both lovely in their own way. The introduction of gobelin jackets added to the opulent velvet ones embroidered with sequins and beads and the strong graphism of the luxe outerwear pieces, which ranged from shearling trimmed coats to shorter options in animalier motifs.” The Fashion Trust Arabia Awards 2025 featured a series of high-profile designers, whose work was honored throughout the evening. Ziyad Albuainain, Youssef Drissi, Leila Roukni and Farah Radwan were among the evening’s honorees, while Miuccia Prada was honored with the Lifetime Achievement Award and Zuhair Murad won the Trailblazer Award. After recruiting Lady Gaga for Season 5 and Season 6, the popular FX show has added another major pop star to the crew. It has been announced that Ariana Grande has joined the cast of American Horror Story Season 13. She will be joined alongside a host of franchise regulars, including Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson , Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe and Leslie Grossman. Ryan Murphy Productions announced the cast of Season 13 on Instagram with a brief teaser, and although it doesn't reveal any plot details, the extensive cast list hints that this may be the most ambitious season yet. The last season, subtitled Delicate , followed Emma Roberts as Anna Victoria Alcott, a rising actress in pursuit of becoming a mother when a sinister force begins to haunt her. Reviews are a bit mixed , highlighting the slow-paced nature of the season and the inclusion of Kim Kardashian in a prominent role. The horror anthology series is not afraid to break formula and focus on unexpected storylines, but some fans suspect that Season 13 might be a follow-up to a previous season. Coven and Apocalypse are some of the most popular guesses, especially since a fan-favorite is finally making her grand return. Jessica Lange Coming Back for 'American Horror Story' Is a Big Deal While fans have long speculated that American Horror Story Season 13 might be the last one, the long-awaited return of franchise icon Jessica Lange may support that theory. The last time she showed up in the anthology series was when she reprised her role as Constance Langdon in Apocalypse , Season 8. Lange plainly dismissed a possible return earlier this year, but that has clearly changed. Getting the crew together for one massive cast seems like the recipe for a final hurrah, even if FX or co-creator Ryan Murphy has not revealed that to be the case. Still, fans will embrace Lange's return with open arms, especially alongside other regulars like Sarah Paulson and Emma Roberts. No matter the case, viewers will be treated to another batch of AHS episodes when the series returns on October 31, 2026 . Adding Ariana Grande will only add to the hype, who is expected to reemerge in the Oscar race when Wicked: For Good hits theaters in November. But the big draw for longtime fans is seeing the old faces together again, which seems to be the driving force behind Season 13. In late 2024, Murphy told Variety that he was formulating the next season alongside Paulson, who was keen on getting the previous cast back together. “I did have a wonderful conversation with Sarah Paulson the other day, and she was like, ‘Okay, I think it’s time we get the band back together, so let’s make some calls here.'" Grande is returning to the world of showrunners Ryan Murphy and Brad Falchuk after starring in their 2015 horror comedy "Scream Queens." She most recently received praise for her role as Glinda in the film adaptation of "Wicked," which is appropriate given the subject matter of her new project. American Horror Story is an anthology show, with each season focusing on a different supernatural drama. Actors often return in different roles each season because of the series' nature. Because of the anthology format, each season has a subtitle referencing its particular plot. Grande will be joined by an all-star lineup of AHS veterans, including Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe and Leslie Grossman. Roberts and Lourd previously shared the screen with Grande in Scream Queens. The casting announcement came via the Ryan Murphy Productions Instagram page , which posted a cryptic teaser — a black screen featuring the cast’s names in the show’s signature font, set to Vera Lynn’s haunting rendition of “I’ll Be Seeing You.” The return of Lange, Bassett, Bates and Sidibe is particularly noteworthy. None of the four have appeared in the series since "American Horror Story: Apocalypse," the show's eighth season, which aired in 2018. Peters and Paulson last starred in 2021’s season: Double Feature. The reunion of so many familiar faces has fueled fan speculation that Season 13 could revisit the world of Coven, the witch-themed third season from 2013. The anthology previously brought back earlier characters in Apocalypse, which served as a crossover between Coven, Murder House (Season 1) and Hotel (Season 5). American Horror Story October 31, 2025 Photo: FX Today, executive producer Ryan Murphy dropped a major Halloween surprise when it comes to American Horror Story season 13. After all, we now know the full cast! If you head over to the EP’s official Instagram today, you can see a video that confirms that for the first time in countless seasons, Jessica Lange is going to be a part of the next chapter. This comes on the heels of her previously downplaying the possibility of a return. We had heard for some tie that both Sarah Paulson and Evan Peters were likely to return, and that has been confirmed alongside a number of other franchise veterans including Kathy Bates, Leslie Grossman, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe, Emma Roberts, and Angela Bassett. There is also one newcomer to the franchise here in Ariana Grande, who worked with Murphy previously on Scream Queens. SUBSCRIBE to Matt & Jess on YouTube for more AMERICAN HORROR STORY videos! At the moment, there are not any further teases on the story of season 13 but at the same time, do we really need to share anything more to be grateful? Our feeling is that this season could be a culmination of a lot of what we’ve seen on the franchise over the years, whether it be shocking moments, great characters, and of course elaborate themes. Now, if there is one last question we have to wonder at present, it is whether or not season 13 is going to be the final one. For now, let’s just say that we wouldn’t be surprised given that this cast feels almost akin to a final curtain call. We personally think that this show really doesn’t ever have to end, though, depending on the story that is designed. Grande is returning to the world of showrunners Ryan Murphy and Brad Falchuk after starring in their 2015 horror comedy "Scream Queens." She most recently received praise for her role as Glinda in the film adaptation of "Wicked," which is appropriate given the subject matter of her new project. American Horror Story is an anthology show, with each season focusing on a different supernatural drama. Actors often return in different roles each season because of the series' nature. Because of the anthology format, each season has a subtitle referencing its particular plot. Grande will be joined by an all-star lineup of AHS veterans, including Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe and Leslie Grossman. Roberts and Lourd previously shared the screen with Grande in Scream Queens. The casting announcement came via the Ryan Murphy Productions Instagram page , which posted a cryptic teaser — a black screen featuring the cast’s names in the show’s signature font, set to Vera Lynn’s haunting rendition of “I’ll Be Seeing You.” The return of Lange, Bassett, Bates and Sidibe is particularly noteworthy. None of the four have appeared in the series since "American Horror Story: Apocalypse," the show's eighth season, which aired in 2018. Peters and Paulson last starred in 2021’s season: Double Feature. The reunion of so many familiar faces has fueled fan speculation that Season 13 could revisit the world of Coven, the witch-themed third season from 2013. The anthology previously brought back earlier characters in Apocalypse, which served as a crossover between Coven, Murder House (Season 1) and Hotel (Season 5). Season 12, titled Delicate, aired on FX from September 2023 to April 2024 and featured Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Leslie Grossman, Kim Kardashian and Matt Czuchry, among others. Although the cast announcement was dropped on Halloween, no details have been given about when the next season is set to air. None of the four have appeared in the series since "American Horror Story: Apocalypse," the show's eighth season, which aired in 2018. Peters and Paulson last starred in 2021’s season: Double Feature. The reunion of so many familiar faces has fueled fan speculation that Season 13 could revisit the world of Coven, the witch-themed third season from 2013. The anthology previously brought back earlier characters in Apocalypse, which served as a crossover between Coven, Murder House (Season 1) and Hotel (Season 5). Season 12, titled Delicate, aired on FX from September 2023 to April 2024 and featured Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Leslie Grossman, Kim Kardashian and Matt Czuchry, among others. Although the cast announcement was dropped on Halloween, no details have been given about when the next season is set to air. Premiering in 2003 and later revived by Netflix, the series’ unique blend of satire, absurdity, and dysfunction won Emmys but struggled with network ratings. Yet its streaming resurgence made the ensemble valuable long after cancellation. Still, the show’s niche audience meant smaller paychecks compared to traditional sitcom giants like Friends or Seinfeld . What’s fascinating is how differently the main players used the cult momentum. Some transformed their quirky roles into full-fledged Hollywood careers, while others focused on independent projects or consistent, low-profile work. The result: a cast whose net worths range from modest millions to comfortable eight-figure fortunes — proof that success in a “revived classic” doesn’t always equal massive bank accounts. Here’s how the cast stacks up today, from lowest to highest, a pattern critics often note ( ranked by critics approaches aren’t just for films). 7. Alia Shawkat Alia Shawkat ’s estimated net worth is around $4 million , representing steady growth rather than overnight riches. Her breakout as Maeby Fünke made her one of television’s most promising young stars, but she transitioned intentionally toward indie cinema, art-house projects, and production work rather than network paychecks. Roles in Search Party , Animals , and Transparent cemented her creative credibility more than financial dominance. She’s also dabbled in voice work — a lane many actors exploit to diversify earnings ( famous voices in franchises ). What makes Shawkat’s story compelling is how she built a sustainable Hollywood career without the trappings of mainstream fame. Instead of chasing high-budget comedies, she cultivated her niche — directing, producing, and starring in projects that give her both creative freedom and stable income. Her wealth is understated but self-made, built on artistic range and consistent reinvention, a path mirrored by other steady television stars ( mind-blowing net worths aren’t the only success metric). 6. Jessica Walter Jessica Walter , who passed away in 2021, left behind an estimated net worth of about $4 million — modest by Hollywood standards but reflective of a long, respected career. Her portrayal of Lucille Bluth became legendary, earning her critical praise and new audiences decades after her earlier film and TV successes. Before Arrested Development , Walter already had a distinguished résumé, from Play Misty for Me to her iconic voice work in Archer (voice roles can be lucrative; see actors with GTA voice credits ). Walter’s wealth came from consistency, not headline salaries. While she didn’t benefit from modern-era streaming pay scales, her late-career renaissance proved how talent longevity can convert into renewed demand. Her estate’s value shows that legacy and recognition often matter as much as raw numbers when measuring career success — a theme common across TV ensembles and their cast net worth rankings . 5. Tony Hale #image_title Tony Hale holds an estimated net worth of roughly $9 million , built through a combination of Arrested Development residuals, his award-winning turn on Veep , and voice roles in animation. His portrayal of Buster Bluth — anxious, awkward, and unforgettable — made him a comedy icon. After the show’s Netflix revival, Hale’s stock skyrocketed thanks to Veep , where he earned Emmy Awards and significantly higher pay per episode (proof that later pivots can rival even mega-ensemble earnings ). Unlike many sitcom actors who plateau after their breakout role, Hale diversified strategically. His appearances in family films like Toy Story 4 and Ralph Breaks the Internet expanded his audience and earning potential. Hale’s fortune illustrates how post-sitcom agility — balancing prestige TV, voice acting, and brand appeal — can quietly multiply wealth, echoing broader trends in award-courting careers . 4. David Cross David Cross has a reported net worth of about $12 million , built on a career spanning stand-up, writing, producing, and acting. His role as Tobias Fünke became instantly iconic — the oblivious, well-intentioned therapist-turned-actor who delivered some of television’s most quoted lines. Beyond Arrested Development , Cross has enjoyed success in stand-up specials, voice acting ( Kung Fu Panda ), and his sketch series Mr. Show with Bob Odenkirk (a reminder that multi-hyphenates often show up in cast net worth breakdowns across TV). What distinguishes Cross is his entrepreneurial mindset. He’s retained control over much of his comedy catalog, earning revenue through touring and digital distribution. While his net worth isn’t astronomical, it’s diversified — coming from writing royalties, production rights, and live performances. His model reflects the smart blend of artistry and ownership rare in comedy careers, similar to profiles featured in notable TV star net worths . 3. Michael Cera Michael Cera ’s net worth is estimated at around $20 million , largely fueled by his transition from Arrested Development to major film success. As George Michael Bluth, he embodied adolescent awkwardness perfectly — a persona he carried into box-office hits like Superbad , Juno , and Scott Pilgrim vs. the World . Those roles earned him millions per film and helped him carve out a lucrative niche as the indie-comedy everyman (a trajectory often contrasted with reality TV cast net worth rankings ). Cera’s fortune reflects strategic timing: he leveraged cult-series fame right when Hollywood was searching for “relatable” leads. He later pivoted toward theater, voice acting ( The Lego Batman Movie ), and music production, which diversified his earnings further. Cera may live quietly, but financially, he’s among the most successful alumni of the revival-era sitcom boom — a pattern common in broader TV wealth spotlights . 2. Will Arnett Will Arnett ’s estimated net worth of about $25 million cements him as one of the top financial beneficiaries of Arrested Development . His portrayal of Gob Bluth — the delusional magician and master of bad decisions — became his career cornerstone. Post-series, Arnett turned that comic persona into gold through BoJack Horseman , LEGO Batman , and numerous high-paying voice-over gigs (again underscoring the power of voice franchises ). His wealth reflects mastery of reinvention. Arnett transformed his distinctive voice and comedic range into a brand. Between Netflix productions, animation royalties, and endorsements, he built a steady income pipeline that rivals bigger sitcom stars. He represents the archetype of the late-career surge — someone who used a cult hit as a springboard into enduring financial relevance, much like names cited in TV net worth rundowns . 1. Jason Bateman Jason Bateman leads the cast financially, with an estimated net worth of around $30 million . Though already a known name before Arrested Development , the show resurrected his career, setting the stage for his later dominance in Ozark , Horrible Bosses , and Game Night . His combination of acting, directing, and producing has made him one of television’s most consistently profitable multi-hyphenates — a profile often compared across ensemble net worth lists . Bateman’s fortune stems from calculated evolution. He leveraged Arrested Development ’s revival fame to build serious drama credentials while maintaining his comedy audience. As an actor-producer, he commands back-end profits from streaming deals and production credits. More than anyone in the ensemble, Bateman exemplifies how turning critical acclaim into creative control leads to sustained — and scalable — wealth, a throughline visible in many TV wealth case studies . By Nate Freeman November 2, 2025 Alex Consani, Demna, Demi Moore, and Tallulah Willis attend the 2025 LACMA Art+Film Gala, Presented By Gucci at Los Angeles County Museum of Art on November 1, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story There are a lot of museum galas this time of year – all fabulous, all great causes, all of that – but there’s nothing like the LACMA Art + Film Gala . What’s do I mean exactly when I say there’s no gala like the LACMA Art + Film? Well, most of them are simply mechanisms to draw funds from donors into the coffers of the institution—and there’s nothing wrong with that whatsoever. It’s a miraculous, marvelous thing, raising money for a building dedicated to the arts and culture. But the LACMA gala is much more than that: it’s a social media hurricane that doubles as a runway show, coalescing into a cultural force that doesn’t really have an equivalent on this side of the American continent. Los Angeles has needed some hometown heroes to bring a victory. The fires in January put a damper on all things in the City of Angels. The town is recovering, but there remains uncertainty surrounding the film industry—whether it’s fear of consolidation, or AI, or diminishing ticket sales as people give up going to the movies. But that’s not at all how it felt on Saturday night. For reasons that will become evidently clear, Los Angeles is winning. Walking into the Los Angeles County Museum of Art on Saturday night, Kenny Scharf (in red sunglasses) next to Queen Latifah , as Dustin Hoffman sidled up to the bar when Emma Roberts was leaving, right as Alex Israel , who was peeling off from Finneas , and then went to fetch a drink with Gaia Repossi . Kaia Gerber and her mother Cindy Crawford posed next to Chris Burden’s Urban Light as LACMA CEO Michael Govan walked in with Marc Glimcher . Lorde was speaking with the artist Emma McIntyre , and then the singer went to say hello to Troye Sivan , and Disney CEO Bob Iger went to take his seat next to David Geffen . Cynthia Erivo and Thelma Golden Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images Claudia Sulewski, Finneas and Alex Israel Zach Hilty/BFA.com This mix of celebrity and art royalty aside, the gala is a bellwether for the world-conquering ambitions of LACMA, and raised close to $6.5 million to centralize film in the museum’s programming, and fund its mission at large. LACMA has long wanted to go toe-to-toe with its East Coast counterparts—namely the Metropolitan Museum of Art—and now it has a showstopper of a building, designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, set to open in April of next year. And LACMA, with this gala, has real showbiz leverage, the support of Hollywood power players. Just look at the host committee, comprised of co-chairs Eva Chow and Leonardo DiCaprio, who were joined by Gucci Artistic Director Demna and Gucci President and CEO Francesca Bellettini . But Demna is perhaps is most telling. One of the most influential and controversial fashion designers in the last decade, he reimagined the idea of zeitgeist while at Balenciaga. The Pinault family—who also own Christie’s, and CAA—moved him to Gucci, which is a genius move on a lot of levels but, for our specific purposes here, quite wonderful for this particular event. Demna really likes hanging out with artists. At one point, sculptor and photographer Paul Pfeiffer went over to say hello, and Demna cupped his hands over his heart and said to Pfeiffer: “I love your work.” Arrow Arrow Demna told me he’s restoring a historic architecturally significant home in Los Angeles to live in. He’s also been homing in on the conceptual ideal of Hollywood to situate the narrative of the new Gucci. In lieu of a runway show, he commissioned Spike Jones and Halina Reijn to make The Tiger , a short film starring Demi Moore , Edward Norton, Ed Harris, Elliot Page, Keke Palmer , Alia Shawkat, Julianne Nicholson, Heather Lawless, Ronny Chieng, Kendall Jenner and Alex Consani . The result brought the characters from his “La Famiglia” collection to life. And then, to ice that cake, Demna hosted the biggest art museum gala in Tinseltown. It honored Mary Corse , as legendary of the West Coast light and space artists as you can get. James Turrell introduced her—he referred to her as one of his heroes, along with Rothko and Georgia O’Keeffe. TheWrap served as a media partner for the 2025 festival, which crowned “Thirstygirl” and “My Kind of People” with the top honors. The festival’s biggest prize, the Grand Jury Award, went to “Thirstygirl,” directed by Alexandra Qin, earning the filmmaker two 4-Day Plus badges to the American Film Market and a $2,500 grant from the Proof Development Fund. The Audience Award went to “My Kind of People” from Joe Picozzi, accompanied by a $1,000 grant. “The Taking of Courtroom One Two Three,” from writer-director Bomani J. Story, earned the runner-up slot and a Jury Special Mention. In the competitive shorts categories, An Nguyen’s “We Used to Take the Long Way Home” received the Gold Award and a $1,000 grant. “Inner Demons,” directed by Jasmine J. Johnson, won the Silver Award and $750. The Bronze Award and a $500 grant went to “Love192” from Haydon Mayer. All three projects were funded through the Proof Development Fund. This year also marked a new partnership between Proof and Kodak, which presented its inaugural Kodak Excellence in Analog Film Award. The prize — $5,000 worth of film stock and processing — went to “Make Me a Pizza.” The film was among several projects earning Jury Special Mentions, along with “Miriam,” “Such Good Friends” and “Cacique del Monte.” Proof Film Festival 2025 (American Cinematheque) In the festival’s industry-focused Pitch Deck Show and Tell, “The Re-Education of Jane Brown” from MK McGehee won a $500 grant, while “When I Taste Blood,” from Caydon LiRocchi, was named runner-up. Judges for this year’s festival were Miranda Sarah Einy, Rachel Goldfinger, Sarah Marie Flores, Remy Solomon, Brett Robinson, Liz Sargent, Riley Chapman, Sara Koch, Kesila Childers, Aisling Scott Lynch, Reiko Napier Moreno and Yuky Shen. Filmmakers Reagan Yorke and Jillian Smith hosted. Proof also unveiled a new partnership with Souvenir Studios: the Souvenir Studios Development Award, which will give the company the opportunity to select one or more projects from the 2025 slate to develop and finance as feature films. “Our ethos has always been to support and elevate young creatives,” Souvenir CEO José Fernández-Velasco said in a statement. “We couldn’t be happier to partner with Proof.” Festival founder and American Cinematheque programmer Imani Davis said this year’s honorees embody Proof’s mission. “Proof is all about connection between filmmakers, collaborators and the opportunities that grow from these early visions,” Davis said. “We’re grateful to all of the partners that make this possible. Courtesy of Tokyo Film Festival Share on Facebook Share on X Google Preferred Share to Flipboard Show additional share options Share on LinkedIn Share on Pinterest Share on Reddit Share on Tumblr Share on Whats App Send an Email Print the Article Post a Comment Kicking off the year with a surprise Sundance win , Hailey Gates ’ debut feature Atropia is now lined up in competition at Tokyo International Film Festival. Satirizing the military, the media and the movie business, the film veers from the surreal to moments of slapstick as it portrays the world of a training facility to prepare troops for deployment to unfamiliar countries and cultures. “The initial idea came when I was trying to make a documentary,” Gates explains to The Hollywood Reporter in an interview during the festival. “I was spending time ingratiating myself with the Department of Defense — now the Department of War — but the way I wanted to film wasn’t going to be possible. So, I thought I’d make a MAS*H-style film instead.” Related Stories Movies 'Inconvenient Indian' Author Thomas King Reveals He Has No Cherokee Ancestry Movies 'Awards Chatter' Pod: 'Jay Kelly' Composer Nicholas Britell Discusses and Performs His Greatest Scores Gates, whose resume includes acting, modelling and journalism, feels the “9/11 generation” has been underserved in onscreen examination of its wars. “When you look at Vietnam, all the great directors made anti-war films. But when you look at the Iraq War, there’s a real dearth. You know, it’s sort of Bigelow, Eastwood, Bigelow,” she says. “And so many things made at that time were in cahoots with the government. I just felt like I wanted to fill a very strange hole there.” Gates’ film, which stars Alia Shawkat and Callum Turner, takes its title from the fictional country “Atropia,” a name the filmmaker unearthed during her research into U.S. military training sites. “They’re all called things like Fort Irwin, and they give them different town names,” she says. “The idea, I’ve heard, is from the Greek word atrophia, meaning to atrophy, so they’re always fighting atrophy to keep the military muscle strong. A little military poetry for you.” Shot in just 19 days on a California movie ranch, but Gates found the production less hectic and haphazard than making documentaries. “Everybody thought 19 days was crazy, but I thought it was thrilling to have a schedule with time. On the first morning, driving in and seeing 40 cars, I actually wept a little. I couldn’t believe all these people were here to make this stupid idea come to life,” she recounts. However, her acting background helped ready her for feature making, and shaped how she directs. “I like doing little parts in movies because it’s the best way to watch a director work. I worked with David Lynch on a few episodes of the Twin Peaks reboot, and he’s famous for using a megaphone, even if there are only three people in the room. I realized it’s not just about projection; it’s about getting the whole crew on the same emotional page. That really stayed with me,” she explains. The flashes of irreverent, even puerile, humor in Atropia can feel jarring in a piece that also points the finger at U.S. imperialism. But the effect is deliberate, according to Gates: “I studied experimental theater before I became a filmmaker. I studied a type of French clowning called bouffon, where you perform for the king and make him laugh at his atrocities. I really like the idea of Trojan-horse storytelling: reeling people in through comedy and then having that comedy curdle a bit, so when you’re walking home, you start rethinking what you were laughing at.” Gates avoids easy caricature and polemics, casting her critically humorous eye across the board. “I don’t like being taught a lesson when I watch films. I like being presented with moral quandaries and coming to conclusions on my own,” she says. Nevertheless, a satirical film about the U.S. military in a climate where dissent is being quashed isn’t without risks. “It’s definitely a film about the American empire and its follies. I just wanted to show that it was built with flimsy plywood,” says Gates. “I had a foreign festival invite the movie and then write back and say, ‘Actually, we think this might upset people.’ It hasn’t opened widely in America yet.” Despite the Sundance victory, Atropia ’s reviews have been mixed . But Gates says she’s unfazed. “It might be that it isn’t a typical Sundance film: it’s not a mood piece, it’s not very sentimental,” she says. “But I’d rather make something polarizing than something everybody loves. This year’s centerpiece program will feature the Los Angeles premiere of Atropia , winner of the 2025 Sundance U.S. Grand Jury Prize for Drama. Originally conceived as a short film, Atropia evolved into a full-length feature starring Alia Shawkat and Callum Turner, which was produced by acclaimed director Luca Guadagnino. The film reflects the festival’s core mission of nurturing bold, experimental storytelling that transitions from short to long form. Writer-director Hailey Gates and Shawkat will attend the screening and participate in a Q&A between showings of the short and feature versions. The festival’s centerpiece programming also includes Film Financing Today , a co-presentation with TheWrap featuring financiers and industry executives from Film Mode Entertainment, Pressman Films, and Unapologetic Projects. The discussion will explore how independent projects are getting funded amid changing market conditions. Another highlight, Next Steps: From a Short to a Feature , returns as a PROOF signature panel, spotlighting filmmakers who have successfully expanded their short works into features. Among the speakers are Jim Cummings ( Thunder Road ), Caroline Lindy ( Your Monster ), and Michael Vlamis ( Crossword ), who will share practical insights and creative advice for emerging filmmakers. The selected 8 pitches are as follows: Bee (Amy Omar & Pinar Binay) Written by Melis Aker, Bee tells the tale of a reclusive 10-year-old girl in Istanbul who suspects her neighbor’s role in her father’s disappearance, setting her on a path of revenge, friendship, and self-discovery. Cult Like Activity (Sam Schaefer) Two twenty-somethings, adrift after the dissolution of their cult, decide their only option is to start their own. It Revolves Around Tycho (Zoe Milenkovic & Elias Kyriakidis), Prague, 1601: The year leading up to Tycho Brahe’s mysterious death, as seen through the eyes of apprentice Johannes Kepler. Lucky Lenny (Jack Campise,) A gay wannabe actor’s big break spirals into a bittersweet road trip when his estranged daughter suddenly reappears. Paper Tiger (Don Ahmad) A Pakistani-American drug dealer scrambles to save his sister’s wedding while colliding with family, friends, and foes. Skylight (Adia Ivey) A daughter learns her grandmother’s stories of aliens, spirits, and cults may hold unsettling truths. The Re-Education of Jane Brown (MK McGehee) A young doctor imprisoned in a nightmarish facility for women who’ve had abortions must escape before she’s stripped of her identity. When I Taste Blood (Caydon LiRocchi, Jahziel Chu & Anoop Chaganty) Dog Day Afternoon with vampires: two eternal lovers trapped in a blood bank as a heist spirals into a hostage nightmare. The 2025 PROOF Film Festival jury brings together a diverse group of industry professionals, including Miranda Sarah Einy ( Happy Place ), Rachel Goldfinger (Playgrounds), Sarah Marie Flores (Anarchists United), Remy Solomon, Brett Robinson, Liz Sargent, Riley Chapman (New Line Cinema), Sara Koch, Kesila Childers, Aisling Scott Lynch (Fourth Wall), Reiko Napier Moreno, and Yuky Shen (Kindred Spirit). Their experience spans studio development, independent production, casting, and talent discovery. The festival will also host its popular Pitch Deck Show & Tell , offering eight selected filmmakers the opportunity to present their feature and series concepts to an audience of peers, producers, and executives. Each participant will have five minutes to showcase their materials and receive real-time feedback from industry veterans — a hallmark of the festival’s focus on mentorship and collaboration. Individual tickets to screenings, panels, and events are now available through the American Cinematheque website . Founded by the American Cinematheque, PROOF Film Festival is the only event dedicated to celebrating proof-of-concept storytelling. The festival serves as a launch platform for innovative filmmakers, spotlighting short films that demonstrate potential for expansion into full-length features. There’s been a lot of game-changing movies directed by women in recent years, but films helmed by women still continue to be much less common than male-directed features. That being said, there’s a lot of releases on the way over the next year that we wanted to bring attention to. It’s exciting to see more women filmmakers than ever with their name all across a variety of genres across the rest of 2025 and the 2026 movie release calendar . Let’s talk about them: (Image credit: Searchlight Pictures) Rental Family - Hikari (November 21, 2025) Hikari is a Japanese filmmaker who previously helmed a movie called 37 Seconds along with having her name on three episodes of Netflix hit Beef . Rental Family is her English-language feature directorial debut, which she co-wrote as well. The movie starring Brendan Fraser is about an American actor living in Tokyo, who begins working for a rental family service. Hamnet - Chloé Zhao (November 26, 2025) Chloé Zhao is one of three women to win the Oscar for Best Director for her work in 2020’s Nomadland – which earned Best Picture as well. The Chinese-born filmmaker is also behind the Marvel movie Eternals . Hamnet is her fifth feature directorial effort. It’s a book-to-screen adaptation of a novel that tells the story of William Shakespeare and his wife Agnes after their 11-year-old son tragically died. And, we can’t wait to see what she does with the video game property next. There’s not enough women behind big horror movies, so it’s great to see Tammi breakout here. (Image credit: IFC Films) 100 Nights Of Hero - Julia Jackson (December 5, 2025) Back in 2016, a graphic novel titled The One Hundred Nights Of Hero offered a retelling of One Thousand And One Nights from a female perspective. Now, it’s been adapted by writer/director Julia Jackman with an all-star cast. Starring Emma Corrin, Maika Monroe, Charli XCX and more, this fantastical romance seems like it will provide a fresh take on the Middle Eastern folktale. Merv - Jessica Swale (December 10, 2025) Rom-coms may often be called “chick flicks”, but not enough women direct them. If you have an Amazon Prime subscription , you can look forward to Merv from Jessica Swale. She is an acclaimed British theatre playwright and director. The movie stars Zooey Deschanel and Charlie Cox as a recently broken up couple who go on a vacation together to cheer up their shared dog. Atropia - Hailey Gates (December 12, 2025) Hailey Gates’ feature directorial debut, Atropia , is on the way to theaters this December after it premiered at Sundance, and won its Grand Jury Prize. Also written by Gates, the movie stars Alia Shawkat and Callum Turner and is a war satire about an aspiring actress in a military role-playing facility. It’s a musical led by Amanda Seyfried about the founding leader of the Shakers religious sect in the 18th century. SOULM8TE - Kate Dolan (January 9, 2026) There’s a M3GAN spinoff movie coming early this year called SOULM8TE . It will give Kate Dolan (who previously helmed You Are Not My Mother ) the opportuinty to do her biggest genre movie to date. Backed by James Wan and Jason Blum , the film is about a man who buys an android to cope with the death of his wife. 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple - Nia DaCosta (January 16, 2026) Nia DaCosta has been making her name as one of the most exciting filmmakers making movies in recent years, and that continues with her fifth directorial effort, 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple . Wuthering Heights - Emerald Fennell (February 13, 2026) From Promising Young Woman to Saltburn , Emerald Fennell has shown she likes to make movies that start conversation, and can be a little controversial. This continues with her peculiar adaptation of Wuthering Heights , which promises to be erotic, and quite different from the source material . The Bride! - Maggie Gyllenhaal (March 6, 2026) After Maggie Gyllenhaal stunned in 2021 with her directorial debut, The Lost Daughter , she’s back in the director’s chair for The Bride! It’s another take on Frankenstein that takes a lot of inspiration from the 1935 movie, Bride of Frankenstein . It stars Jessie Buckley and Christian Bale. Reminders Of Him - Vanessa Caswill (March 14, 2026) There’s been a couple of Colleen Hoover movie adaptations so far, but Reminders Of Him will be the first from a woman director. Vanessa Caswill, who also made the solid Netflix rom-com Love At First Sight in 2023, is behind the movie about a woman who returns to her hometown seven years after being sent to prison. (Image credit: SME) Italianna - Kat Coiro (April 10, 2026) Another female-helmed romantic comedy to look forward to is this spring’s Italianna starring Halle Bailey and Regé-Jean Page. The movie will be directed by Kat Coiro, who also did Marry Me , A Case Of You and many She-Hulk episodes. It's about a whirlwind romance that takes place during a destination wedding in Italy. 4 Kids Walk Into A Bank - Frankie Shaw (April 17, 2026) We’ll get the chance to see the directorial debut of Frankie Shaw, who has been an actor for the past twenty years. 4 Kids Walk Into A Bank is a black comedy heist movie starring the likes of Liam Neeson , Talia Ryder, Whitney Peak, Jack Dylan Grazer, Spike Fearn and Jim Sturgess. Is God Is - Aleshea Harris (May 15, 2026) It’s rather rare to hear the original playwright behind their own play is helming a movie based on their work, but that’s the case for Aleshea Harris’s Is God Is . The thriller will be Harris’s first time directing a movie, and boasts a cast including Sterling K. Brown , Vivica A. Fox and Janelle Monáe. It’s about twin sisters who are ordered by their mother to kill their abusive father. (Image credit: TIFF) Poetic License - Maude Apatow (May 15, 2026) Maude Apatow, the daughter of Judd Apatow and Leslie Mann, has made her first movie called Poetic License . It stars her mom as a former therapist and empty nester who gets in the middle of two best friends / college seniors (played by Cooper Hoffman and Andrew Barth Feldman). It premiered already to positive thoughts from critics. Practical Magic 2 - Susanne Bier (September 18, 2026) Almost two decades after Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman played witches in Practical Magic , they’ll continue the story, this time with a female director behind it. Suzanne Bier has made a lot of movies over the years, but has notably already directed Practical Magic 2 ’s stars before – Bullock in Bird Box and Kidman in The Perfect Couple . The Legend Of Aang - Lauren Montgomery (October 9, 2026) The last movie we'll highlight for now (though there's more to come from women directors) is the animated Avatar: The Last Airbender movie, The Legend of Aang . Director Lauren Montgomery has a massive resume of being a storyboard artist and director in the animated space for 20 years primarily on DC animated projects, but this is her highest-profile movie to date. We'll keep you updated as this list continues to change. Go out and support these women-fronted projects!
