Black Doves Season 2 Adds 7 New Cast Members Including Neve Campbell and Ambika Mod ☰ × New on Netflix Coming Soon Leaving Soon News & Previews K-Dramas Anime Games What to Watch Top 10s Netflix Top 10 Reports Top 10 Data Search Engagement Report Search Top 10 Country Search Top 10 Weekly Rank List Library Netflix Roulette About Us Home Netflix News Black Doves Black Doves Season 2 Adds 7 New Cast Members Including Neve Campbell and Ambika Mod The series is filming its second season in the United Kingdom as we speak. By Jacob Robinson • @JRobinsonWoN November 18th, 2025 - 10:00 am Copy to clipboard Comments Picture left to right: Ambika Mod, Babou Cessay, Sam Riley, and Neve Campbell have been cast in Black Doves season 2. Netflix has finally confirmed that Black Doves season 2 filming is underway and rounded out the cast as it continues production in the United Kingdom, having begun in September. Ambika Mod, Babou Cessay, Sam Riley, Neve Campbell, Sylvia Hoeks, Goran Kostic, and Samuel Bennett have all been cast in Black Doves season 2. Here’s everything we know about the new cast members and their roles. One of the best new shows from 2024, Black Doves is a British crime-thriller series created by Joe Barton. It stars Keira Knightley as Helen Webb, a spy from a mysterious shadow organisation, who is publicly married to the British Defence Secretary. After the death of her lover, her secret identity as a spy is at risk, so the Black Doves send Sam, played by Ben Wishaw, to protect her. 7 New Cast Members for Black Doves Season 2 Picture: 7 new cast members for Black Doves season 2 Starting with Ambika Mod , she will play Laila, described as “an acerbic and anarchic Black Doves agent who is sent to help Helen on a mission.” The actress previously starred in the Netflix adaptation of One Day as Emma. Read Next Black Doves Season 2: Now In Production And Everything We Know So Far Babou Ceesay plays Mr. Conteh, one of the Black Doves executives with “suspicious motivations.” A new ally for Helen and Sam or a new antagonist? He recently starred in the Disney+ series Alien: Earth . Sam Riley will play the role of Patrick, “an emissary from a mysterious organisation, who offers Sam a lifeline.” Riley is best known for his roles as Diaval in Maleficent and Mr. Darcy in Pride and Prejudice and Zombies . Neve Campbell has joined the cast as Cecile Mason, who, interestingly, hasn’t been given any form of character description. Advisary or ally? We can’t wait to find out. Campbell is most well-known for starring as Sidney in the Scream franchise. Three further cast members have been revealed: Sylvia Hoeks (Blade Runner 2049) as Katie Chernov, Goran Kostic (Ant-Man and The Wasp) as Alexi Chernov, and Samuel Barnett (Penny Dreadful) as Jerry. Keira Knightley , Ben Whishaw , and Sarah Lancashire have already been confirmed to be reprising their roles as Helen Webb, Sam Young, and Reed. Picture: Ben Wishaw (left) and Keira Knightley (right in Black Doves Other confirmed cast members returning for season 2 are: Andrew Buchan as Wallace Webb, Kathryn Hunter as Lenny Lines, Ella Lily Hyland as Williams, Gabrielle Creevy as Eleanor, Agnes O’Casey as Dani, and Molly Chesworth as Marie. Production Underway on Black Doves Season 2 Alongside the casting news, Netflix confirmed that production on season 2 is underway, as it has been since late September 2025, with a planned wrap sometime in February 2026. Joe Barton, the series creator, had the following to say: “I couldn’t be more excited to delve back into the world of our murderous little spy family. To have so many of our amazing cast returning and also being able to add some of my absolute favourite actors into the mix is such a great joy. Downing Street will never be the same again…” The Vice President of Content for Netflix UK, Anne Mensah, shared her excitement Netflix has for the series return: “To say we are over excited about welcoming the Black Doves team back to Netflix would be an understatement. This is what happens when best in class writing meets best in class directing and extraordinary acting in a dark alley with guns and champagne. We couldn’t be more thrilled and we know the Black Doves fandom is waiting!” What is the Plot of Season 2? Netflix has provided an updated logline for Black Doves season 2: “Helen (Keira Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organisation she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever. As Helen’s enigmatic handler Mrs Reed (Sarah Lancashire) is ensnared in a ruthless plot to undermine her position in the Black Doves, Helen is reunited with her best friend Sam (Ben Whishaw). The once high-end triggerman is now reduced to lonely drinks in Soho bars and low-rate hits. As they search for answers, loyalties are weaponised, trust is shattered, and the fight to protect the people they love could cost everything. With all the explosive wit of Series 1, Helen and Sam’s mission leads them back to old friends and enemies, through the dark decisions and painful sacrifices of their pasts, and right to the heart of the Black Doves.” For more information on the second season, you can find our ongoing preview here : Are you excited for Black Doves season 2 on Netflix? Keira Knightley thinks she's been fortunate in her career The 40-year-old actress has enjoyed a hugely successful career in the film industry, having starred in Bend It Like Beckham back in 2002 - but Keira acknowledges that her life and her career could've easily gone in another direction. Speaking to The Independent, Keira explained: "The adult me is very aware that people can go through very difficult periods in their life, and they do not come out of it with a very successful career and a very healthy bank balance. I feel incredibly fortunate." Keira acknowledged that she's now achieved a level of respect from the public that didn't exist during her teenage years. The brunette beauty said: "I think being a 40-year-old woman, people have a different response to you than when you’re 18. That’s just the way the world is. "When you’re 18, you haven’t got much work, you’re all image. When you have a career that’s 25 years long, and you’ve got enough stuff to be like, ‘Well, that’s a body of work; some worked, some didn’t’ – people can look, and go, ‘That’s a career.’" Meanwhile, Keira previously claimed that there's "an inherent rage to actors". The movie star has observed that some actors and actresses, including herself, often lean into their anger in order to inspire their on-screen performances. Keira told the Guardian newspaper: "I think there’s an inherent rage to actors. I see that quite a lot. Masked brilliantly but easy to access. "Not that people behave badly, because generally they don’t. But there’s a well of anger that opens very quickly. "It comes from this being such a subjective industry where it is very public when things go wrong. And it’s an industry of people searching for a truth that by its very nature they can’t find because it’s fiction. Maybe that creates the coiled spring, which is where some performances come from." Heart This Christmas’ on Hallmark, In Which A Glassblower Tries Sell Her Work At A Famous Holiday Fair, And Falls For Its Organizer In The Process After premiering on Freeform in 2019, Ghosting: The Spirit of Christmas is now available on Netflix. This fantasy romantic comedy film stars Aisha Dee as a young woman who ends up literally ghosting a new man (Kendrick Sampson) in her life after an untimely demise. With the help of her supportive best friend (Kimiko Glenn), she tries to resolve anything holding her back in hopes of moving on to the afterlife. It’s a little silly, but it also has a lot of heart, and is definitely an original premise as far as the typical holiday fare goes. GHOSTING: THE SPIRIT OF CHRISTMAS : STREAM IT OR SKIP IT? The Gist: Jess is a Los Angeles-based young woman who’s always flitting from one thing to the next. She loves trying new things, but easily grows bored once the initial shine wears off, leaving her feeling stuck in life. Luckily, her longtime best friend, on-call energy healer and tea brewer extraordinaire Kara (Kimiko Glenn), is always at her side, supporting Jess through it all, including her recent firing from a bakery job. When sparks fly on a successful first date with artist Ben (Kendrick Sampson), Jess’s luck seems to finally turn around, as she sees in him something worth committing to. But tragically, on her way home from the date, Jess gets killed in a car accident, cutting the budding relationship off before it can really bloom, and leaving Ben thinking he’s been ghosted. In a way, he’s not wrong, because Jess is now a ghost stuck between the land of the living and the afterlife, with only Kara apparently able to see her. Kara and Jess hypothesize that Jess has unfinished business on Earth, so they do everything they can to get her unstuck. Following the advice of Kara’s energy healer, Chrissy (Missi Pyle), the best friends believe that “one big love” will help Jess ascend, leading her to once again pursue Ben, who’s miraculously able to see her ghostly form too. As Ben struggles with this seemingly ill-fated relationship while still working through long-lasting grief and hangups from when his mother died when he was just 13, Ben is supported by his younger sister, psychology master’s student Mae (Jazz Raycole). The more that Ben and Jess get together, the harder they fall, pushing them both to change. At the same time, Kara and Mae also start falling for each other, as Kara confides in Mae about her situation with Jess, and Mae pushes Kara to stop holding herself back for a ghost’s sake to pursue her own dreams. But as Christmas draws near and the lines between ghost and living worlds blur, tensions reach a boiling point as Jess discovers that Kara has been keeping secrets about a big career opportunity. With Jess fearing failure and Kara fearing change, the two are forced to confront hard truths and old resentments to achieve their happy endings. Photo: Everett Collection What Movies Will It Remind You Of?: While the movie makes some references to It’s a Wonderful Life , the most direct comparison to Ghosting: The Spirit of Christmas might actually be ghost and friendship-centric TV series like Boo, Bitch and School Spirits . Performance Worth Watching: Honestly, all four of the main actors are great, but Kimiko Glenn and Jazz Raycole especially pop as supporting characters who are more complex, fleshed-out, and engaging than you see in your typical holiday rom-com. Memorable Dialogue: This exchange between Jess and Kara, which showcases how self-aware the writers were about this film’s kind of random rules of ghosthood: “You have to learn to ride a bike.” “I can’t.” “You can!” “No, I mean, like I literally, I can’t grab onto the handles or pedal the pedals.” “Then how are you sitting on it? Your tangibility is so confusing.” Sex and Skin: There’s a bit of hanky panky, but it happens off-screen, so there’s no actual sex or skin to be seen. Our Take: Ghosting: The Spirit of Christmas has a unique storyline, good pacing, and strong acting performances that come together to create a movie full of genuine humanity and heart. While the romances between Ben and Jess, as well as Kara and Mae, are charming and definitely ones that you root for, the friendship between Jess and Kara is the real love story that will hit you in the feels. I mean, all of the actors in this have great chemistry, but Aisha Dee and Kimiko Glenn really do carry and sell this as best friends trying to be there for one another, all while struggling to say goodbye, and it’s hard not to be moved while watching them onscreen together. Ghosting: The Spirit of Christmas is more of a movie that happens to be set around the holidays than one about the holidays. It doesn’t always make sense, namely with the logic (or lack thereof) of Jess’s tangibility. Even so, neither of these things detracts from this being an engaging and evocative film. Sure, there could be more holiday stuff, but ultimately, the core of this movie is friendship, and at the end of the day, what’s more Christmasy than love and warmth in all its forms? Our Call: If you want a strictly light-hearted, mindless watch, this isn’t exactly it, but if you’re willing to embrace the full spectrum of human emotion for a bittersweet little story about love and soul mates in all their forms, then Ghosting: The Spirit of Christmas is the movie for you. After more than a decade at R&CPMK, Lauren Stillman is striking out on her own with Stillman+Co, opening offices simultaneously in New York and Los Angeles. The agency will focus on talent and influencer alignment for fashion, luxury, lifestyle and beauty clients, as well as VIP dressing and gifting, leveraging long-standing relationships to create culturally resonant red carpet moments. You May Also Like Operating bicoastally, Stillman+Co will have a West Coast dressing and gifting showroom through a partnership with SHO+Co, with LA operations overseen by Katsya Brito. The agency’s name was chosen to reflect the core values of community, collaboration and commitment, which Stillman says are essential in today’s industry. The launch comes as R&CPMK undergoes a structural overhaul, rebranding as PMK Entertainment under Michael Nyman’s Acceleration Community of Companies. While celebrity and corporate clients transitioned to the rebranded firm, Stillman is taking her fashion clients independent. “One of the things I’m most excited about with the decision to go independent is the ability to truly collaborate with my clients as partners,” Stillman told WWD. She said independence allows the firm to leverage its network to encourage clients to take strategic risks on emerging talent and buzzworthy projects. Stillman emphasizes that red carpet dressing is increasingly strategic, driven by ambassadorships and major houses’ investment in global events like Cannes and the Met Gala. Smaller brands can compete by offering consistent support and community to talent and stylists year-round. “You need to know how to speak the language and understand the customs so you don’t get taken advantage of. Clients come to us because they see the value in working with a small, independent operation,” she said. Stillman also stresses the necessity of a global, bicoastal presence and participation in international hubs such as Cannes, where she has over eight years of experience running a pop-up showroom. On Saturday, Lori Harvey and Shanina Shaik wore Zuhair Murad to the Fashion Trust Arabia Prize Ceremony, in Doha, Qatar, where Murad was honored with the Trailblazer Award. Kerry Washington appeared in Zuhair Murad Couture at the Los Angeles premiere of “Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery” and later wore Murad ready-to-wear to the Elle Women in Hollywood Awards. Actress Ali Larter wore Teresa Helbig at the same event. “Community and collaboration are the key to our business,” Stillman added, noting that independence allows for deeper involvement throughout the dressing process. Stillman began her career at Film Fashion in 2001 and has worked across Rogers & Cowan, ITB Worldwide, and R&CPMK, navigating mergers and restructurings under Interpublic Group. IPG recently sunset Rogers & Cowan as part of its relaunch into PMK Entertainment, marketing agency ACC Advisory, and corporate branding agency DKC. However, this past year proved one of the most important in the organization’s history. “This year, Baby2Baby provided essentials to the one million children relying on them in foster care, homeless and domestic violence shelters, schools and more in all 50 states and 300 cities,” began presenter Olivia Munn from the stage of the Pacific Design Center on Saturday, Nov. 8 at the 2025 Baby2Baby Gala presented by Paul Mitchell. Jessica Alba, Kelly Sawyer Patricof, Co-CEO, Baby2Baby, Serena Williams, Norah Weinstein, Co-CEO, Baby2Baby and Olivia Munn Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby “I think that it might be hard for many of us in this room to comprehend the fact that 1 in 2 families in this country cannot afford diapers for their babies,” added Kerry Washington, who accompanied Munn to the podium. “And consider the ripple effect: If a mom doesn’t have enough diapers to drop her baby off at daycare, she can’t go to work. And so, the cycle of difficulty continues.” Olivia Munn and Kerry Washington Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Washington noted how Baby2Baby built its own diaper manufacturing system, making diapers for 80 percent less than retail cost and distributing over 250 million. “They’ve even successfully advocated to remove sales tax from diapers here in California,” she added, “and since then, 13 more states have followed suit.” Paris Hilton, Lizzo and Meghan Trainor Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Baby2Baby’s fastest-growing program is helping families in the wake of disasters. The organization’s work in this area began with Hurricane Harvey in 2017, when the team realized disaster relief areas did not have items to accommodate babies and children. Since then, Baby2Baby has responded to 100 disasters — from hurricanes in Florida to wildfires in Maui. But this year brought unforeseen challenges. The organization supplied gear to 100 additional fire relief events; sent diapers to the city, state and FEMA; and opened a storefront in Pasadena. “In total, so far, we have distributed 31 million emergency supplies to families,” Patricof said to applause. Read more about Weinstein and Patricof’s fire relief efforts in our March L.A. Woman issue . Orlando Bloom, Jessica Alba and Danny Ramirez Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Next up, they’re building a new national headquarters and warehouse in Santa Monica that will serve as Baby2Baby’s permanent home in 2027. This new 47,000-square-foot facility will triple its warehouse capacity and double its volunteer space, allowing it to help even more children. “This year, Baby2Baby served one million children around the country in all 50 states,” said Patricof. “We gave out our 500 millionth item, our 270 millionth diaper and our 10 millionth backpack and school supplies.” But they aspire to help the 10 million children still on their waitlist. Prior to sitting for the program, over 800 guests — including executives, business leaders, philanthropists and famous supporters, such as Adam Scott, Anna Kendrick, Ayesha Curry, Camila Alves McConaughey, Charlie Puth, Demi Lovato, Erin Foster, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Jenna Dewan, Judd Apatow, Julianne Hough, Kaley Cuoco, Katherine LaNasa, Lake Bell, Leslie Mann, Lizzo, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Trainor, Miranda Kerr, Missy Elliott, Molly Sims, Monique Lhuillier, Nicole Richie, Orlando Bloom, Paris Hilton, Rachel Zoe, Sara Foster, Swizz Beatz, Tyler Perry, Vanessa Bryant and Will Ferrell — mingled during a cocktail hour. They sipped Avaline wine and Casamigos, Johnnie Walker and Ketel One cocktails, and snacked on passed bites curated by Jon Shook & Vinny Dotolo. Then, the real eating began. Credit: Author A restaurant area offered dinner stations, featuring dishes by beloved eateries including Funke, Holy Basil, Kato, Kazunori by Sushi Nozawa, Burger She Wrote, The Benjamin Hollywood, Beethoven Market, 88 Club, A Ti, Max & Helen’s, Moo’s Craft Barbecue, Mr. Chow, Pizzeria Bianco and Saffy’s. Kazunori had the longest line (for custom toro, salmon, yellowtail, scallop and crab hand rolls), and other favorites included the matzoh ball soup from Phil Rosenthal’s new diner Max & Helen’s, the cacio e pepe from Funke, the honey sesame shrimp from Kato and the beef kabab from Saffy’s. Olivia Munn, Rachel Zoe and Julie Bowen Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Baby2Baby board member Julie Bowen and Malin Akerman led the fundraising portion — which resulted in a record-breaking over $18 million raised. Notable supporters like Paris Hilton and Jennifer Garner were among those making contributions. Alicia Keys Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Then, Alicia Keys honored athlete and entrepreneur Serena Williams with the Giving Tree Award. “We honor Serena for her fierce commitment to uplifting children and families with her powerful advocacy for maternal health,” Keys said. Williams spoke of her personal struggles in her acceptance speech. “When I had my daughter Olympia, I faced life-threatening complications,” she said. “I had access. I had privilege. But I wasn’t listened to. I wasn’t believed. And I came painfully close to losing everything.” Prince Harry and Meghan Markle flank honoree Serena Williams. Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby The experience changed her life: “It opened my eyes to the harsh reality that Black women are three times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes,” Williams said. “That’s why Baby2Baby’s maternal health [effort] in addition to what they do for babies is so deeply personal to me: They distribute mental health and newborn supply kits … and postpartum care and vital educational resources precisely when the mom needs them.” Missy Elliott and Ciara Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Jessica Alba and Ciara closed out the evening before a performance by musical guest, Ludacris — who got the crowd packed around the stage area and dancing to his hits, “All I Do Is Win,” “Stand Up,” and “Yeah!,” “Glamorous,” “How Low Can You Go” and “Shake Your Money Maker.” Kerry Washington and Camila Alves Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby An after-party DJed by DJ Nice continued to keep guests dancing — and eating, with pizzas by Jon & Vinny’s, PopUp Bagels and dessert items. Published Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:17:03 -0600 by Kaitlyn Booth | Comments Article Summary Netflix unveils the first official trailer for Wake Up Dead Man, the third film in the Knives Out series. Rian Johnson returns as writer-director, with Daniel Craig back as detective Benoit Blanc in a new mystery. The trailer teases an impossible crime and hints at dark religious undertones fueling the gripping whodunnit. Wake Up Dead Man marks the final film in Johnson's original Netflix deal, with a release date set for December 12, 2025. Netflix has some heavy hitters coming before the end of the year, and the third Knives Out film from writer and director Rian Johnson is absolutely one of them. There is a decent chance that no one thought the first film would hit as hard as it did, but it was a critical and commercial success. However, Lionsgate sold the rights to the next two films to Netflix, and Wake Up Dead Man is the final film in that initial deal. However, Johnson has been very upfront about the fact that he'd like to keep making these movies for a while. They are sequels in the sense that they have exactly one returning character, which means you have to work a schedule around star Daniel Craig and whoever decides to join the cast for the next one. And everyone who has been involved with these films as a cast member has had nothing but good things to say about the environment that Johnson creates on set. There is a reason these films keep drawing in top-tier talent. Netflix released the official trailer , which gives us a ton of new footage and teases some more of the mystery we're going to be solving. It also continues to push the idea that this is an impossible crime that Blanc is attempting to solve, and that, combined with some religious fantasticism, never ends well for anyone involved. Josh O’Connor and an all-star cast are the usual suspects. Print this Article View Comments From left: Josh O'Connor and Daniel Craig in "Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery." Courtesy of Netflix Just in time for Thanksgiving, Benoit Blanc, Daniel Craig’s unflappable detective from the “Knives Out” movies, is back! “Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery,” the third installment of writer-director Rian Johnson’s mystery franchise, is a movie to be thankful for. It’s not just a riveting case that will keep you guessing, it’s also a heartfelt ode to mystery books and their authors. If you love curling up with a good book starring Hercule Poirot or Father Brown, this is the movie for you. With this much darker installment, Johnson follows the same pattern as the recent Kenneth Branagh adaptations of Agatha Christie’s Poirot books. So far, both series have featured a more traditional murder mystery and one set in a vacation locale. With his third Christie movie, 2023’s “A Haunting in Venice,” Branagh sent Poirot down a much darker gothic path, adapting a murder scenario filled with often gory results. Working from his own original story, Johnson pays homage to several authors and the types of mysteries they crafted. If you’re well-versed in the specific types of cases authors like Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, Christie, and G.K. Chesterton (among others) made famous, you’ll recognize that Johnson is using them all to tell his story. The “locked room mystery” is just one type employed here. Get Starting Point A guide through the most important stories of the morning, delivered Monday through Friday. Enter Email Sign Up From left: Mila Kunis, Daniel Craig, and Josh O'Connor. Courtesy of Netflix If you’re not familiar with these elements, don’t worry! Benoit Blanc will fill you in as the film goes along. He even namechecks one of the most famous locked room mysteries, John Dickson Carr’s 1935 novel, “The Hollow Man.” As Blanc navigates “the Good Friday murder,” he points out every mystery book trope and every possible solution that it begot. But all this deducting may be for naught, because every possible outcome is immediately debunked. Could it be that the master sleuth has encountered a case he simply cannot crack? Advertisement It’s not that Blanc doesn’t have enough suspects. “Wake Up Dead Man” exists in a small, tightly knit church community whose denizens are way too familiar with one another and do not take kindly to outsiders. The parish is led by Monsignor Jefferson Wicks (Josh Brolin), a fire-and-brimstone preacher whose mean-spirited, authoritarian, and personal attack-style sermons sound lifted from the book of Republicans rather than Revelation. He’s a terrifying presence who keeps his flock in check. Glenn Close plays Martha Delacroix, a preternaturally devout church lady who’s also the Monsignor’s right-hand woman. So fierce is her devotion to her preacher that she’d do anything for him. The rest of the parishioners include former best-selling sci-fi author Lee Ross (Andrew Scott); the church’s groundskeeper, Samson Holt (Thomas Haden Church); anxious attorney Vera Draven, Esq. (Kerry Washington); wannabe politician/podcaster Cy Draven (Daryl McCormack), who records everything with his phone; suspicious doctor Nat Sharp (Jeremy Renner); and concert cellist Simone Vivane (Cailee Spaeny from “Priscilla”). From left: Andrew Scott, Mila Kunis, Daryl McCormack, Glenn Close, Cailee Spaeny, and Kerry Washington in "Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery." Courtesy of Netflix Into this closed circuit of a community comes the much younger priest, Rev. Jud Duplenticy (Josh O’Connor). He’s been sent by a church bishop (Jeffrey Wright, in an effective cameo) to assist Monsignor Wicks, whose reputation seems to have inspired a bit of concern. The rough and tumble Rev. Jud has a far from priestly past, one he navigated with fists of fury when he was, in his words, “young, dumb, and full of Christ.” (That line made me laugh so hard that I thought the ushers at the Toronto International Film Festival were going to throw me out of the theater.) Rev. Jud is not welcome at all in his new parish. Marie is especially suspicious of him, to the point where she thinks he’s demonic. Monsignor Wicks psychologically torments his protégé in some rather disgusting yet funny ways. And any attempt at reaching out to the rest of the flock results in secrets being revealed and grudges exposed. Advertisement Josh Brolin in "Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery." Courtesy of Netflix As with all great mysteries, everybody has a motive for committing “the Good Friday murder,” which, of course, takes place on Good Friday. Notice that I didn’t tell you who the victim is, and I’m not going to, but I will say that this person is dispatched in one of the most familiar types of murder mystery deaths. Instead, I’ll tell you that, as in his great (and now canceled) Peacock series, “ Poker Face ,” Johnson leans a bit into “ Columbo ” territory here. Unlike that classic Peter Falk show, “Wake Up Dead Man” isn’t a “howcatchem” style mystery, where we know who did it from the outset and watch as they’re eventually caught. But, like “Columbo,” we have to wait a while before the detective shows up on the scene. Benoit Blanc’s entrance is delayed; he’s offscreen far longer in this installment than he was in the original “Knives Out” or “Glass Onion.” For the first act, Rev. Jud is the star of the show, narrating and filling us in on who’s who and what’s what. We get to know everyone well before the mystery (and the mystery solving) begins. Josh O'Connor in "Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery." Courtesy of Netflix Blanc’s initial absence was a source of contention among some of the audience members I talked to after the TIFF screening . The gambit paid off for me, though. O’Connor is this film’s MVP for a reason, and the star, who has four movies out this year, gives an excellent, charismatic performance. The game is afoot once his Rev. Jud arrives on the scene, and he and Craig make a great team. Also assisting our sleuth is Chief Geraldine Scott (Mila Kunis), the town’s top cop, who proves more useful than you think. Advertisement As dark and gruesome as the film is (its PG-13 rating flirts with an R), “Wake Up Dead Man” is never without a sense of humor. It’s a nasty gallows humor, to be sure, but you will laugh. The impressive cast looks like they’re having a great time reveling in their villainy, heroics, or both. “Wake Up Dead Man” is one of the year’s best movies. I’ve enjoyed all three movies, but this one is the best of the “Knives Out” mysteries so far. His inability to land on a solution makes Benoit Blanc insecure, and it opens up new layers for Craig to play, and the resulting tension keeps us on our toes. ★★★★ WAKE UP DEAD MAN: A KNIVES OUT MYSTERY Written and directed by Rian Johnson. Starring Daniel Craig, Josh O’Connor, Glenn Close, Josh Brolin, Andrew Scott, Kerry Washington, Mila Kunis, Thomas Haden Church, Daryl McCormack, Jeremy Renner, Cailee Spaeny, Jeffrey Wright. At Coolidge Corner, Landmark Kendall Square, Alamo Drafthouse Seaport, suburbs. 140 minutes. PG-13 (language, violence, gore) Odie Henderson is the Boston Globe's film critic. Wake Up Dead Man will be released in select theaters on November 26 before streaming on Netflix on December 12. The star-studded cast of Wake Up Dead Man includes Daniel Craig , Josh O’Connor, Glenn Close, Josh Brolin, Mila Kunis, Jeremy Renner, Kerry Washington, Andrew Scott, Cailee Spaeny, Daryl McCormack, and Thomas Haden Church. Despite the release of the final trailer, the synopsis for the film remains sparse, as Netflix simply describes the film as being “Benoit Blanc’s most dangerous case yet in the third and darkest chapter of Rian Johnson’s murder mystery opus.” Final trailer for Rian Johnson’s Wake Up Dead Man released ahead of the film hitting select theaters on November 26 Wake Up Dead Man is the second Knives Out film to be released by Netflix after acquiring the rights to the franchise from Lionsgate in 2021 for $469 million. The first Knives Out sequel, Glass Onion , was released in 2022 and while less acclaimed than its predecessor, was still widely beloved and was a massive hit for Netflix. While Wake Up Dead Man is the last movie that’s part of the original $469M purchase in 2021, both director Rian Johnson and star Daniel Craig have expressed an interest in continuing to make films in the series. Jaden Lucas Miller | Raleigh native lands role on Hulu's 'Reasonable Doubt' - ABC11 Raleigh-Durham 24/7 Live Raleigh Durham Fayetteville Surrounding Area ARTS & ENTERTAINMENT Raleigh native Jaden Lucas Miller lands role on Hulu's 'Reasonable Doubt' By Amber Rupinta Thursday, November 6, 2025 A Raleigh native is stepping into the spotlight with a role on the hit Hulu legal drama "Reasonable Doubt." RALEIGH, N.C. (WTVD) -- A Raleigh native is stepping into the spotlight with a role on the hit Hulu legal drama "Reasonable Doubt." Jaden Lucas Miller plays the younger version of a character named Ozzie, who's on trial for murder. ABC11 first met Miller in 2023 when he was a rising senior at Cardinal Gibbons High School in Raleigh. Now, Miller is a full-time student at North Carolina A &T State University, taking classes online while his acting career takes off. He splits his time between Atlanta and Raleigh and says this role has been transformative. "Having to be vulnerable with this character, it not only helped me grow as a person, but it helped me realize what I was going through at a young age and being around my family," Miller said. "Luckily, I have a strong support system." Miller credited his mom and family for keeping him grounded as he navigates Hollywood -- and admits he's had plenty of "pinch me" moments. "I just never know who I'm going to meet," he said. "Some days it's Denzel Washington! And I'm like, I guess that happened today. I'm telling my mom, 'You're never going to believe who I met today.' It's just surreal when it happens." You can catch Miller in Episode 309, titled D'Evils, of " Reasonable Doubt ," now streaming on Hulu. The series, now in its third season, was created and executive-produced by Raamla Mohamed , with Kerry Washington also serving as an executive producer. It’s fun!” Jennifer Ouellette – Nov 17, 2025 12:48 pm | 41 Credit: YouTube/Netflix Credit: YouTube/Netflix Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Nothing says it’s holiday season quite like a new installment of Rian Johnson’s delightful Knives Out mystery series. The final trailer for Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery was just released, featuring Daniel Craig’s Benoit Blanc in all his Southern gentleman detective glory. This time, he’s tackling the strange death of a parish priest in a spookily Gothic small-town setting. As we’ve previously reported , the original Knives Out was a masterfully plotted winning mashup of Clue and Murder on the Orient Express —or any number of adaptations of novels by the grande dame of murder mysteries, Agatha Christie—along with other classics like Deathtrap , Gosford Park , and Murder by Death . Craig clearly found Blanc a refreshing counter to the 007 franchise, and he and Johnson soon committed to filming a sequel: 2022’s Glass Onion , inspired particularly by the Christie-based “tropical getaway” whodunnit Evil Under the Sun (1982) and an under-appreciated 1973 gem called The Last of Sheila . And now we have Wake Up Dead Man . With this franchise, the less one knows going in, the better. But Johnson has assembled yet another winning all-star cast. Josh Brolin plays the victim, the fire-and-brimstone-spewing Monseigneur Jefferson Wicks; Josh O’Connor plays a young priest named Rev. Jud Duplenticy; Glenn Close plays a devout churchgoer named Martha Delacroix, Wick’s loyal helper; Mila Kunis plays local police chief Geraldine Scott; Jeremy Renner plays town doctor Nat Sharp; Kerry Washington plays uptight lawyer Vera Draven; Daryl McCormack plays aspiring politician Cy Draven; Thomas Haden Church plays groundskeeper Samson Holt; Andrew Scott plays bestselling author Lee Ross; and Cailee Spaeny plays Simone Vivane, a disabled former classical cellist. Wake Up Dead Man garnered early rave reviews after screening at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) in September, and an initial teaser released shortly after showcased Blanc puzzling over a classic locked-room mystery. The new trailer builds out some of the details without giving too much away. Rev. Jud is the prime suspect in Wicks’ murder, since he loathed the man and hence had a clear motive, but he insists to Blanc that he is innocent. We learn that Wicks was wealthy, and this being a classic whodunit, we know the rest of the characters no doubt have their deep, dark secrets—one of which could have led to murder. And Johnson brings the humor, too, as Blanc, the groundskeeper, and Martha discover the desecration of Wicks’ tombstone with scrawled graffiti penises. “Makes me sick, these kids painting rocket ships all over his sacred resting place,” the unworldly Martha says. Wake Up Dead Man will be in select theaters on November 26, 2025, and will start streaming on Netflix on December 12, 2o25. We can’t wait. Facebook Instagram Twitter TikTok YouTube Subscribe Search Language English Español Entertainment This Is Your Last Chance to Stream One of the Best Teen Dramas Ever Made on Netflix By Sophie Hessekiel October 30, 2025 TOP STORIES Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Nikki Reed, Kip Pardue, Evan Rachel Wood in Thirteen Fox Searchlight/courtesy Everett Collection Tap Here To Add Us Weekly As A Trusted Source Add as a preferred source on Google Catherine Hardwicke is best known for directing the first Twilight movie in 2008, kicking off a major franchise that changed the teen movie landscape forever. But years before that, the director made her debut with a much darker teen movie — Thirteen — that got added to Netflix last summer but is already on its way off the streamer. Here’s why Watch With Us is recommending this controversial teen drama, which deals with sex, substance abuse and self-harm — and why you should stream it before it leaves Netflix on November 1. The Cast of ‘Thirteen’ Is Made Up of Future Stars Thirteen stars Evan Rachel Wood as Tracy, a well-behaved middle schooler whose life is changed when she becomes friends with troubled teen Evie. Evie is portrayed by Nikki Reed , who would go on to star as Rosalie in the Twilight franchise. At only 14 years old, Reed actually co-wrote the movie’s script with Hardwicke. The youthful performances from Wood and Reed are really impressive, and it’s easy to see why the two would both go on to star in big name projects like Westworld and Twilight . Wood was nominated for a Golden Globe for her performance. Thirteen was also the first onscreen performance of Vanessa Anne Hudgens , who appears in a minor role. Related: Why Ian Somerhalder Wants to 'Throw Up' Watching Nikki Reed in 'Thirteen' Nikki Reed got her big break in cult classic Thirteen 22 years ago, though her husband, Ian Somerhalder, still can’t take it seriously. “As a dad now, I watch it and I … throw up in my mouth a little bit,” Somerhalder, 46, joked during a Thursday, April 24, interview on SiriusXM’s The Julia Cunningham […] ‘Thirteen’ Has an Amazing Origin Story Thirteen was Hardwicke’s first time directing — she’d worked as a production designer prior to this movie. She got to know Reed because she had dated Reed’s father, and had stayed in her life after the breakup. The movie was inspired by Reed’s own teenage experiences. It’s remarkable that the relationship between a teen girl and her father’s ex was strong enough to lead to such an intense project. Hardwicke raised all the funds for the movie herself — she told The LA Times that people were “terrified” to make the movie because of the subject matter, which includes underage sexuality, drugs, violence and self-harm. Once they had secured a tiny budget and cast Holly Hunter as Tracy’s mom, the entire movie was shot in 24 days — with the child actor leads allowed to work far fewer hours than adult actors would have been. Related: Overall, Thirteen is a testament to the power and determination it takes to make an indie film — and the hard work shows in every frame of the scrappy, smart movie. Thank You! Since then, we’ve learned that Igby Rigney ( The Midnight Club ), Graham Campbell ( Late Fame ), pop singer Hayes Warner, and newcomer Homer Gere are also in the cast. Now, Deadline and The Hollywood Reporter have broken the news that they’re being joined by Evan Rachel Wood (Westworld) , Wes Bentley ( Yellowstone ), and Jordan Roth, a Tony Award-winning producer. Details on the characters Gerber, Wood, Bentley, and Roth will be playing have not been revealed, but we do know that Rigney is playing a young Bret Easton Ellis, Gere is Robert Mallory, and Campbell is Thom Wright. Warner is playing Debbie Shaffer, “a rich prep school girl with the right connects.” The series will be directed by Max Winkler, who has worked on many Murphy projects. He has been at the helm of episodes of American Horror Story, American Horror Stories, The Watcher , Feud: Capote vs. The Swans , Monster: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story , Grotesquerie , and Monster: The Ed Gein Story. sponsored content The Shards is a semi-autobiographical coming-of-age tale which follows a 17-year-old version of Ellis during his final year at Buckley prep school. When the enigmatic new student Robert Mallory arrives on campus, Ellis suspects he might be connected to the nearby serial killer known as The Trawler. The story, which is set in “a vibrantly fictionalized Los Angeles in 1981,” was initially released on Ellis’ Patreon in 2020 as a serialized audiobook, but was published as a novel in 2023. The Shards was previously in development at HBO, with Luca Guadagnino ( Challengers ) and Kristoffer Borgli ( Dream Scenario ) each considering directing the project. There were even rumblings that Jacob Elordi ( Saltburn ) was being eyed to star, but it ultimately fell apart due to creative differences. The Ryan Murphy / FX take on the concept is now filming, and Gerber and Gere have already been spotted on set . Are you interested in The Shards ? Murphy directed and wrote the screenplay for Running with Scissors , which was released in 2006. The former Westworld cast member starred alongside an all-star cast that included Annette Bening, Alec Baldwin, Gwyneth Paltrow, Gabrielle Union and Kristin Chenoweth. Now Murphy and Wood are back together on a new project, a TV show called The Shards , which will air on FX, according to Deadline . Rounding out the cast are Kaia Gerber, Igby Rigney, Homer Gere, Graham Campbell and Hayes Warner. Wood's role hasn't been revealed yet, but she will star as a recurring character. The show is an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' 2023 novel The Shards , which takes place at a high school in the 1980s. The story focuses on a tragedy that occurs after a new student arrives. Ellis is best known for writing American Psycho , which was turned into a film starring Christian Bale. Running with Scissors , which was critically panned despite winning multiple awards, was released while Murphy's medical drama Nip/Tuck was on the air and three years before his hit musical comedy series Glee catapulted his career into the stratosphere. Since then, Murphy has created, produced and written numerous shows like American Horror Story , Scream Queens , American Crime Story , Feud , 9-1-1 and Pose . The multi-hyphenate creator has multiple shows currently on the air, including 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville . The Ed Gein Story , the third season of his Monster anthology series, was released on Netflix on October 3. It only has a 21% on Rotten Tomatoes, making it the lowest-rated installment of the true crime series. Murphy is about to launch a star-studded legal drama on Hulu called All's Fair with Sarah Paulson, Niecy Nash, Naomi Watts, Kim Kardashian, Teyana Taylor and Glenn Close. Aside from The Shards , he's got other shows in the works, including The Beauty and Love Story . Wood, meanwhile, followed up her role in Running with Scissors by starring in such films as The Ides of March , Across the Universe , Frozen 2 and Weird: The Al Yankovic Story , as well as the TV shows True Blood and Westworld , the latter of which earned her a Critics' Choice Award, a Golden Globe nomination and two Emmy nominations. Including Running with Scissors , Murphy's track record has certainly been mixed when it comes to the critical reception of his projects, so it's way too early to tell how The Shards will be received by the public. However, the novel it's being adapted from received mixed reviews but was a bestseller nonetheless. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap HBO may have created one of the first “blockbuster” television events with Game of Thrones , but the reimagining of the classic Michael Crichton novel Westworld proved to be one of the most ambitious projects within the history of the medium. Although it had a scope, scale, and budget that rivaled most Hollywood blockbusters, Westworld ’s most captivating narrative device was its non-linear structure, which forced viewers to connect the dots to identify which point in the timeline a given scene was. While this occasionally led to some confusion for the viewer, it often sparked moments of revelation that had a tremendous impact on the story. Westworld completely subverted expectations by showing the backstory to the Man in Black , a character who had been depicted very differently in the original 1973 film. HBO's 'Westworld' Redefined One of Its Greatest Villains The Westworld film cast Yul Brenner as a ruthless android designed to look like a gunslinging cowboy, who tracked down and executed many of the unlucky guests that had come to the park. While Ed Harris was introduced as a similar character early on in the show’s pilot, it soon became clear that he was actually a human who had spent years in the park trying to crack a mystery initiated by its founder, Dr. Robert Ford ( Anthony Hopkins ). It wasn’t initially clear what drove the Man in Black to become such a sadistic villain, but Westworld took a wild turn by revealing that the viewers had been watching the bad guy the whole time . William ( Jimmi Simpson ), a young guest who falls in love with the host Dolores ( Evan Rachel Wood ), is eventually shaped by heartbreak and tragedy to become one of the most sinister characters in the Westworld universe. Westworld crafted an aura of ethical ambiguity because of the double-nature of many of its performances. Since the hosts are revitalized many times, and are often based on existing humans, it’s never exactly clear at what point in the timeline something is taking place. Westworld makes William into one of the most instantly likable characters because he does not share the same aggressive qualities as many of the other human characters. A majority of the guests at Westworld are wealthy, pretentious investors and bureaucrats who want to use their freedom to act on their darkest violent and sexual desires; by comparison, William is forced to attend a trip to the park with his soon-to-be brother-in-law, Logan ( Ben Barnes ), whose father James ( Peter Mullan ) is one of the board’s most important investors. Even though the series ultimately serves as a warning about putting too much faith in artificial intelligence , the kindness that William shows to Dolores indicates that he has a sense of moral decency that Logan and the other guests lack. Related Is Jonathan Nolan Right? Did Weekly Releases of 'Westworld' Hurt the Show? With so many different streaming release styles, did the weekly release hurt a twist-filled show like 'Westworld'? Posts By Liam Gaughan May 28, 2024 The genius of the first season’s construction is that Westworld examines how William’s experiences in the park unlock part of his nature that he has kept under the surface. While in real life he is forced to be subservient to Logan and struggles to express his confidence, the park is the rare place in which he feels powerful and free. Initially, William’s self-actualization is seen as a positive character development because he goes out of his way to save Dolores. However, his protective attitudes slowly transform into possessive toxicity when he realizes that she can be reincarnated, and has no memory of him. Simpson impressively shows how William’s heartbreak eventually leads him to begin brewing in his own anger; while initially the series is somewhat sympathetic to him because he genuinely seemed to care about Dolores, it subsequently builds the idea that William believes that nothing matters , and that he is therefore excused to do whatever he wants in the park. HBO's Sci-Fi Hit 'Westworld' Establishes a Brilliant Labyrinthian Structure Westworld 's Season 1 finale, “The BiCameral Man,” finds a clever way to stage the reveal about William’s identity because it is framed through Dolores’ perspective. Dolores is just as clueless about the mechanics of the timeline as the audience is , and therefore is not able to differentiate between her memories of William and the terror she feels when facing off with The Man in Black. Even though William is never seen interacting with The Man in Black, the show doesn’t call attention to the disparity, particularly when viewers are tracking other twists, such as the reveal that Bernard ( Jeffrey Wright ) is actually Ford’s former partner, Arnold . Wood gives an impressive performance that mirrors the shock and horror that the audience may have felt upon realizing they’d been duped into being emotionally engaged with such a violent character. The subsequent montage that examines William’s transformation is masterfully done, and there’s also a complexity to the emotions within Harris’ performance that makes the scene even more painful. Harris is one of the best living actors, and is able to show that there is still part of William that hasn’t stopped being in love with Dolores. It is often the case that shows with innumerable plot twists aren’t able to adequately follow through with the ramifications. However, Westworld ’s revelation about William made the rest of the show more interesting . William’s negative experiences with his own family were cast in a new light when he’s forced to team up with his daughter, Grace ( Katja Herbers ), who seeks to rekindle their relationship. In order to make the transition between the two actors more believable, Westworld Season 2 was able to explore more with Simpson’s version of the character as he tricked his father-in-law into living within a simulated reality where he was unaware of his artificial consciousness. Despite the horrific actions he was capable of, William served as a bit of an audience avatar through his desperation to solve all the riddles in the park. The premature nature of Westworld ending with Season 4 means that there was much squandered potential and unanswered questions, but the incredible development of the character of William is one of the show’s most impressive achievements. I’d move to Derry if it meant buying a house for 900 dollars… The 10 Best Sci-Fi Shows of The 21st Century By Sarah Fimm Oct 30th, 2025, 1:18 pm It’s the 21st century, and you know what that means! It means we’re closer than ever to the sci-fi future of tomorrow! But will that future be utopian or dystopian? Human or alien? Soundtracked by cool synth music or no? Your guess is a good as mine. However, neither of our guesses are as good as the futures predicted by these stellar sci-fi series. If you’re looking to take a glimpse into the world of tomorrow before it arrives, tune in to the 10 best sci-fi shows of the 21st century. Recommended Videos Stranger Things (Netflix) A nostalgia drenched, synth scored pop culture phenomenon, Stranger Things is a love letter to nerd culture and the pulp sci-fi past. Set in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana, the small town peace is disturbed by the disappearance of young Will Buyers, abducted by an eldritch entity off the street! It’s every mom’s worst nightmare! Will’s friends are determined to get him back, and with a combination of Dungeons and Dragons logic and the help of a psychic girl, they might just do it. While it goes off the rails slightly in later seasons, prime Stranger Things is all the best parts of 80s coming of age classics like Stand By Me , combined with the vintage horror thrills of It and Invasion of the Body Snatchers . Creepy, cozy, campy, comic, cathartic, can’t get any better. Orphan Black (BBC America) While not set in space or involving aliens like most of the other entries on this list, Orphan Black firmly establishes its genre roots through the exploration of a real life sci-fi phenomenon: cloning. Con artist Sarah Manning happens to witness the suicide of police detective Beth Childs – a woman who could be her twin… or doppelgänger? Surely there’s nothing sci-fi going on there! After assuming Beth’s identity, Sarah discovers that she’s actually part of an entire network of clones – each of whom has adopted a radically different life with one thing in common: someone is trying to kill them. A cerebral sci-fi thriller, the series is held together by the monumental performance of Tatiana Maslany – who plays half the show’s characters. She’s so convincing that I swear the producers must have cloned her themselves. Firefly (20th Century Studios) A modern classic, Firefly is a short lived and well loved sci-fi about a spaceship crew with an antagonistic relationship to authority. A space western with all the charm of Cowboy Bebop (the anime, not the live action) the plot follows the Serenity ‘s captain Malcom “Mal” Reynolds as he attempts to hold his found family crew together in a lawless universe. As the series progresses, the crew members’ often checkered pasts are explored – giving context to why this team of opposites has formed such tight bonds. Ex-rebel soldiers, lab created psychics, macho mercenaries who love their mothers – the Serenity takes all kinds. Thrilling, witty, and utterly devastating, Firefly is a titan of the genre. Westworld (HBO) Inspired by a 1973 pulp sci-fi classic of the same name, Westworld is set in a near future where the rich can pay for the privilege of cosplaying as cowboys and outlaws in a real-life video game, at the expense of the androids that serve the world’s NPCS. For a hefty sum, the wealthy can enter “Westworld,” an Old West themed amusement park that allows you to play out your inner gunslingin’ desires. You can save the damsel, or tie her to the train tracks while twiddling your mustache. “She’s a robot,” the amusement park’s creators say, “she doesn’t care one way or the other.” But when the designated damsel Dolores gets tired of being abused at the hands of Westworld’s guests, she decides to strap on the shooting iron herself and become the deadly gunslinger they’ve been pretending to be. A gritty, violent sci-fi Western about robots vs rich people? Sign me up. The Expanse Amazon Prime Video) Inspired by an acclaimed series of sci-fi novels, The Expanse is set hundreds of years in the future – the Solar System has been colonized, and an uneasy peace exists between planetary superpowers Earth and Mars, and the loose confederation of human settlements in the Asteroid Belt. That uneasy peace is toppled after the ice mining ship Canterbury accidentally stumbles across secret Martian technology, sparking conflict throughout the system. While the stakes are cosmic in scope, the plot is grounded by the found family relationships on the Rocinante – made up of the Canterbury ‘s surviving crew. How do you contend with interstellar war, extraterrestrial threats, and megacorp menace? Easy, you don’t do it alone. Futurama (20th Century Television) Like The Hitchhiker’s Guide to The Galaxy decades before, Futurama ‘s creators took a look at sci-fi and asked “what if this genre stopped taking itself so seriously?” Like a baby star in a nebula cradle, shining sci-fi sitcom greatness was born. From the minds that brought us The Simpsons comes the story of Phillip J. Fry, a dimwitted pizza boy who accidentally becomes cryogenically frozen while making a New Year’s Eve delivery in 1999. After reawakening the year 3000, Fry is taken in by a spaceship delivery crew consisting of a mad scientist, a cigar chomping robot, a one eyed mutant, and an alien medic whose doctorate degree is in Art History. One of the funniest shows ever conceived, Futurama parodies the 21st century through a far future lens. Assisted suicide telephone booths, extraterrestrial soda corporations, mind control T.V. stations (all glory to the Hypnotoad!) – it’s all there. Battlestar Galactica (NBC Universal) One of the most successful reboots ever made, Battlestar Galactic took a 70’s cult T.V. series and turned it into 21st century pop culture phenomenon. Picking up where the 2003 miniseries left off, Battlestar Galactic focuses on the last remnants of humanity – sequestered into a starship fleet after their home system was nuked by sentient space robots. The fleet is spearheaded by Battlestar Galactica , an old and powerful warship that will someday lead humanity to its lost, last colony: Earth. A titanic space opera, the series chronicles the war between humanity and the Cylons – a conflict that is interceded by a “God” that appears to watch over both civilizations, whispering to both to end the cycle of suffering. Massive in scope and equally intimate, Battlestar Galactica is a spiritual odyssey the realm of genre-greats like Dan Simmons’ novel Hyperion . Black Mirror (Netflix) Named after the appearance of the soul-sucking rectangle that we all keep in our pockets, Black Mirror is a grimdark sci-fi series dripping with 21st century cynicism. An anthology series about the many ways the future can go wrong, the series reflects the dark realities of the modern era back at us. Far from a feel good watch, the show tackles the reality warping nature of social media, the gamification of capitalist society, the morally dubious ways that humanity could attempt to cheat aging and death – and so much more. Deeply disturbing and darkly funny, Black Mirror is a sci-fi satire that will make you think twice about the world of tomorrow. Are we creating a future that is actually sustainable for all humans? For only for a lucky few? Or for no one at all? Lost (ABC) One of the most influential TV series of all time, Lost ‘s reputation precedes it. Emotionally devastating, famously enigmatic, infinitely re-watchable – it’s simply one of the greatest shows ever. The plot centers around the crash survivors of Oceanic Airlines Flight 815, who find themselves stranded on a (seemingly) uninhabited tropical island. As the passengers struggle to survive the hostile natural world, they discover a hostile supernatural world lurking beneath. Smoke monsters, creepy cultists, polar bears woefully far from the Arctic – this island is full of unexplainable mysteries. Culminating in one of the most hotly debated final seasons ever aired, Lost cemented its legacy as one of the most confusing, compelling and culturally significant shows ever made. Severance (Apple TV+) Shaping up to be a modern classic, Severance put a sci-fi spin on a mundane reality: the nine to five job. A ubiquitous aspect of modern society, everyday people have been forced to “circle back,” “get the ball rolling,” and write “finds you well” emails as their souls are slowly sucked from their bodies. But what if there was a way to escape the grind? With the help of the “severance” procedure, now there is! By splitting the brain into two parts, the employees of Lumen are now able to keep their work lives and their personal lives separate – splitting themselves into distinct “at work” and “at home” personalities. What serves as salvation for the “at home” personality quickly becomes damnation for the “at work” personality, as the working employees of Lumen never get a break. If you were stuck in a labyrinthian office building, held captive by a capitalist cult, and told nothing of the outside world, you’d probably start plotting rebellion in the break room too. Part social commentary, part corporate America satire, part cerebral sci-fi thriller, Severance is working quite a few different jobs at once. Have a tip we should know? The small but mighty cast of Pluribus is relatively non-starpowered for an Apple show, led by Better Call Saul ’s Rhea Seehorn , playing one of a dozen people on Earth who are immune to a hive-mind virus. Pluribus ’ premise is completely original, and only a few episodes in, there are already themes of autonomy and loneliness among the thriller and noir elements that put Pluribus in conversation with some of the greatest sci-fi shows of all time . Fans of Pluribus will also find a lot to love in the following seven TV series. The Leftovers (HBO) 3 Seasons - 2014-2017 Kevin Garvey kneeling down with his hand extended toward Nora Durst, inviting her to dance at an outdoor party in The Leftovers series finale The Leftovers and Pluribus are both series built around the emotional aftershocks of a world-altering event. In Pluribus , a hive-mind virus reshapes humanity. The Leftovers begins with the Sudden Departure — 2% of the world’s population vanishing without explanation — which fractures society and forces everyone to question their beliefs, identities, and relationships. Both shows are fundamentally about grief, isolation, and the search for meaning. In Damon Lindelof's underrated masterpiece The Leftovers , the world is still populated, but nearly every character carries a deeply personal devastation: the loss of a loved one, the loss of faith, or the loss of who they used to be. What ties The Leftovers and Pluribus together is their focus on rebuilding after the unimaginable. The Leftovers didn’t offer easy answers, and Pluribus is still unfolding its mystery. The Leftovers examined how fragile and resilient humanity can be when its foundations suddenly disappear, making it an essential watch for viewers drawn to the haunting introspection of Pluribus . The Last Man On Earth (Fox) 4 Seasons - 2015-2018 While The Last Man on Earth doesn’t share Pluribus ’s hard sci-fi edge, it explores many of the same emotional themes that make the Apple TV series so compelling. Will Forte’s show is technically a sitcom, but its comedy is rooted in the same core questions about loneliness and battling loneliness and depression in a post-apocalyptic world. Like Rhea Seehorn’s Carol Sturka, Forte’s Phil Miller is not an inherently “ good ” person — at least not at first, though Carol’s journey is just at its beginning. Visually, The Last Man on Earth echoes some of Pluribus ’s eerie stillness and vast emptiness, but on a far more modest scale. Fox didn’t have $15 million an episode to play with, yet The Last Man on Earth still captures that haunting quiet. While there are some superficially fun perks, eventually the stillness always becomes more unsettling than comfortable. Sadly, The Last Man on Earth was canceled after four seasons , but it's funnier, lighter, and less bleak than Pluribus while sharing its emotional DNA. Devs (Hulu/Disney) 1 Season - 2020 Sergei and Forest standing in the forest in the series finale of Devs Devs shares Pluribus ’ near-future sci-fi sensibility, but the two series are even more closely connected by the questions they ask about free will, determinism, and the limits of human agency. In Devs , the tech world’s most secretive quantum computing project becomes a lens through which characters confront whether their choices are truly their own or simply predetermined code unfolding. Pluribus approaches the same existential dilemma from a biological and societal angle. Its hive-mind virus forces Carol to grapple with the terrifying idea that her autonomy may vanish. Her desperate search for someone who can fix the world echoes Lily’s journey in Hulu's underrated sci-fi thriller Devs , where a single woman becomes the fulcrum around which the entire system turns. Both series center on characters who don’t yet realize that their stubbornness, love for just one other person, and willingness to question the system make them uniquely suited to reshape their world. Carol isn’t just resisting infection; she’s resisting the philosophical erasure of self. Invasion (ABC) 1 Season - 2005-2006 Invasion operates in a similar space as Pluribus , even if the latter insists its threat is a virus rather than a traditional alien takeover. The short-lived ABC series follows a small Florida town slowly being infiltrated by water-based extraterrestrial creatures who merge with and ultimately replace human hosts through a cloning-like process. As the townspeople begin to change, the show leans heavily into psychological tension and identity horror, raising the same questions that Pluribus explores about what makes a being human as opposed to something else. Characters have to grieve loved one that are in some ways still alive. The major difference lies in perspective. Invasion keeps both its characters and viewers in the dark for much of the season, creating paranoia through not knowing what has happened. In contrast, Carol in Pluribus is explicitly told what is happening — but that doesn’t make her feel any safer, since she cannot trust the Others’ intentions. Although Invasion ended far too soon after one season, it remains a cult favorite, frequently cited as one of the best TV shows canceled too soon . That’s one place it diverges sharply from Pluribus , which Apple commissioned for two seasons from the start, virtually guaranteeing a fuller, more complete story. Westworld (HBO) 4 Seasons - 2016-2022 Evan Rachel Wood as Dolores Smiling on her front porch In Westworld Westworld is a clear thematic pairing with Pluribus , especially when it comes to questions of free will, autonomy, and the ethical questions of control. While Westworld examines these ideas through the lens of artificial intelligence — specifically the Hosts, whose every desire, memory, and behavior is written into code — the show ultimately asks the same unsettling questions that underpin Pluribus . In Pluribus , the Others claim to be optimizing humanity, smoothing out chaos, and making reality more efficient. But that efficiency comes at the steep cost of individuality, spontaneity, and authentic choice. Similarly, HBO's sci-fi Westworld centers on characters who believe they are acting on their own impulses, only to discover that their paths have been meticulously engineered. Both shows blur the line between benevolent guidance and authoritarian control, challenging viewers to consider whether a perfectly ordered world is worth the loss of personal agency. Ultimately, Westworld functions as a darker, more operatic counterpart to Pluribus , using sci-fi spectacle to interrogate the same core tensions. After all, Pluribus may be the perfect AI allegory . 3 Body Problem (Netflix) 1 Season (Renewed For 2 & 3) - 2024-present a distorted image of Liam Cunningham Seen on a Shiny Surface in 3 Body Problem 3 Body Problem and Pluribus both explore what happens when humanity encounters alien intelligence that claims to be benevolent — yet whose idea of “helping” comes with devastating consequences. In both shows, the aliens’ worldview is shaped by a profound disconnect with human nature. Former Game of Thrones showrunners David Benioff and D.B. Weiss frame the San-Ti as logical beings who initiate contact through code, much like the first signals the spread of the Pluribus virus. In 3 Body Problem , the San-Ti panic when they realize humans can lie, deceive, and strategize unpredictably. Their fear drives them toward control. In Pluribus , the Others reach a similar conclusion, though through a different mechanism: humans, left to their own free will, are too chaotic to “optimize” the planet or themselves. The result is a quiet, nonviolent takeover that echoes what 3 Body Problem might look like after the San-Ti finally arrive on Earth. Where 3 Body Problem season 1 ends before the physical invasion, Pluribus essentially picks up where that story could go — examining life under a power that believes it knows what’s best for humanity, even if humanity doesn’t agree. Severance (Apple) 2 Seasons (Renewed For Season 3) - 2022-present Adam Scott walks down a hallway with balloons in Severance Severance shares a surprisingly deep spiritual kinship with Pluribus , even though its sci-fi elements feel far more mundane. That’s by design: Severance imagines a near-future corporate world where the technology isn’t flashy, just brutally efficient. Instead of reshaping reality or altering society at scale, Lumon Industries exerts control by splitting its employees’ memories in half—creating “ Innies ” and “ Outies ” who can never fully know each other. It’s a chilling form of compartmentalized control, one that weaponizes absence through the excellent Severance season 2 finale . Pluribus flips this concept on its head. Rather than isolating people from their own memories, the Others achieve domination by forcing a communal consciousness — everyone shares everything, which means personal emotion and individual resonance are erased. Where Severance explores the terror of not knowing, Pluribus taps into the horror of knowing too much, yet feeling none of it. Both shows hinge on mysterious organizations with unclear endgames. Lumon’s ultimate purpose remains hidden behind layers of corporate ritual and myth, just as the Others’ long-term goals are still deliberately obscured. What’s unmistakable, though, is streamers’ growing mastery of the sci-fi thriller. Between Severance , Pluribus , and Silo , Apple TV holds the crown for prestige sci-fi storytelling. 19 8.7 /10 8 /10 Pluribus 10 stars 9 stars 8 stars 7 stars 6 stars 5 stars 4 stars 3 stars 2 stars 1 star Like Follow Followed TV-MA Drama Thriller Sci-Fi Release Date November 6, 2025 Network Apple TV Directors Adam Bernstein, Zetna Fuentes, Melissa Bernstein 7 Images Rhea Seehorn staring into the distance in Pluribus Rhea Seehorn's Carol holding a doctor by their arms looking worried in an ER lobby in Pluribus Rhea Seehorn's Carol looking seriously over her shoulder in Pluribus Rhea Seehorn in Pluribus Apple Rhea Seehorn in Pluribus ©Apple TV+ / Courtesy Everett Collection Rhea Seehorn's Carol looking distracted and Karolina Wydra's Zosia smiling at someone in Pluribus Rhea Seehorn curled up on the couch in Pluribus Close Cast See All Rhea Seehorn Carol Sturka Karolina Wydra Zosia Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming Writers Ariel Levine Genres Drama , Thriller , Sci-Fi Creator(s) Vince Gilligan Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. He has self-published a fantasy novel and a book of short stories, and is actively working on publishing his second novel. A lifelong fan of watching movies and talking about them endlessly, he writes reviews and analyses on his Instagram page dedicated to cinema, and occasionally on his blog. His favorite filmmakers are Andrei Tarkovsky and Charlie Chaplin . He loves modern Mexican cinema and thinks it's tragically underappreciated.
