Thanksgiving-themed shows Young Glinda Spacey on 'homeless' claim A 'Wicked' farewell ELLE’s 2025 Women in Hollywood Event Was Full of Stars, Tears, and Celebration Brea Cubit Tue, November 18, 2025 at 7:51 AM UTC 8 min read Inside ELLE’s 2025 Women in Hollywood Celebration Monica Schipper - Getty Images THE RUNDOWN On November 17, ELLE hosted its annual Women in Hollywood event, bringing together some of the industry’s biggest stars with support from partners Ralph Lauren, Bulgari, Lucid Motors, Hendrick’s Gin, and Evian. This year’s honorees included Jennifer Aniston, Teyana Taylor, and Rose Byrne, who all took the stage to deliver heartfelt speeches. The celebration took place at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles, where guests joked, mingled, and reflected on the state of Hollywood. On Monday night, ELLE’s 2025 Women in Hollywood celebration gathered some of the industry’s most influential talents. The annual event, held at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles, honored an extraordinary slate of women featured in ELLE’s latest issue : Jessie Buckley , Teyana Taylor , Jennifer Aniston , Rose Byrne , Renate Reinsve , Chase Infiniti , Emily Blunt , and Sinners co-stars Jayme Lawson, Wunmi Mosaku, and Hailee Steinfeld. Each was recognized for her artistry, ambition, and influence. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Guests in attendance included Selma Blair, Melissa McCarthy, Ruth E. Carter, Mandy Moore, Niecy Nash, Jackie Tohn, and Jessica Alba. A select few arrived at the event via Lucid cars, setting the tone with show-stopping looks . The venue came to life with the help of the evening’s partners: Ralph Lauren, Bulgari, Lucid Motors, Hendrick’s Gin, and Evian. Attendees—many dressed in Ralph Lauren and Bulgari—mingled and sipped on Hendrick’s Gin cocktails and Evian water before settling into their seats, kicking off a lineup of tributes that underscored the power of women shaping show business. Mandy Moore arrives at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles in a Lucid car. Getty Images for ELLE Hendrick’s Gin cocktails. Getty Images for ELLE Diana Silvers at the Evian bar. Getty Images for ELLE ELLE editor-in-chief Nina Garcia opened the program, framing the evening as both a celebration and a moment to acknowledge the industry’s progress and path forward. “For three decades, this event has witnessed Hollywood history—and even made some of its own. I feel that legacy in the room tonight as I look out on this spectacular crowd,” she noted. “At the first events, merely spotlighting the work of women in the industry felt like something new. But over the years, this event has become a forum for candid and meaningful reflection.” Nina Garcia poses on the red carpet in Ralph Lauren and Bulgari. Amy Sussman - Getty Images Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Regina Hall then took the stage to present the Ralph Lauren Spotlight Award to Infiniti. The 25-year-old star accepted the honor, delivering a heartfelt speech that reflected on her creative upbringing and life-changing roles in the Apple TV series Presumed Innocent and this year’s critically acclaimed film One Battle After Another . “My parents never once hesitated helping me achieve my wildest dreams, and they didn’t make them seem all that wild,” she said, tearing up. “This is crazy!” she added as she laughed it off. Throughout the night, even more stars commanded the room’s attention and gave one another their flowers. Sebastian Stan introduced Reinsve , who revealed that she brought her son as her date. “I’m so happy and proud to be here and be celebrating with all you amazing women—and I see some men here, too,” she added with a wave as the audience laughed. She offered sweet remarks about her son, saying, “He’s such a wonderful person, so sensitive, and strong, and cool.” Ralph Lauren Spotlight Award winner Chase Infiniti poses next to a photo from her ELLE cover shoot. Gilbert Flores - Getty Images Dwayne Johnson—who mentioned that he was “raised in a house full of estrogen”—welcomed Blunt, his Smashing Machine castmate. The actress clued the crowd into an inside joke, sharing that she nicknamed Johnson “Tutz,” then “Toosie,” which the former wrestler said sounded like “Titties.” Hence, Blunt’s onstage jest directed at Johnson: “Your soulfulness is as great as your titties.” And, in her signature comedic form, the Devil Wears Prada star also encouraged everyone to play a game of “What song blew your mind?” Kerry Washington then honored Taylor, who thanked the Scandal actress for splitting her time between the Women in Hollywood event and the L.A. premiere of her upcoming film Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery . The multihyphenate performer also gave Aniston a shout-out, saying, “Jen, I loved you on Friends , girl.” Chloé Zhao in Ralph Lauren presenting to Jessie Buckley. Getty Images for ELLE Chloé Zhao followed with an introduction for Buckley, who cried while delivering an emotional speech that supported the event’s focus on perseverance. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement One of the evening’s most powerful moments came courtesy of the women of Sinners , introduced by Michael B. Jordan and Ryan Coogler. Steinfeld couldn’t attend because she was feeling under the weather, but Lawson and Mosaku acknowledged that she’s there “in spirit” before reflecting on the power of their vampire film . Lawson offered a heartfelt tribute to Jordan and Coogler for trusting the cast with such nuanced characters. She described Sinners as a cultural phenomenon that brought women with agency, desire, and unapologetic appetite to the big screen. Her speech evolved into a celebration of sisterhood as she shed tears and spoke about finding her creative family: “When you find your sisters in this industry, you hold on for dear life and you do not dare let them go.” Mosaku’s remarks were equally impassioned. She spoke about the honor of standing alongside talented women and the responsibility to help build environments where women can thrive freely. She thanked Coogler and Jordan for carving out more space for women of color in Hollywood. “Your contribution to this industry has expanded our vision of what film can do,” she said. Jordan even took a moment to help fix the train of Mosaku’s dress. Next, Melissa McCarthy introduced Rose Byrne, highlighting the If I Had Legs I’d Kick You star’s acting chops and reminiscing on their time filming Bridesmaids . Jennifer Aniston onstage in Ralph Lauren. Getty Images for ELLE Finally, Aniston received her award from Adam Sandler (who called her “the best in so many ways”), closing out the night’s speeches by tracing her journey from her first Women in Hollywood honor in 2011 to the present. While she looked back on what’s changed since then, she also reflected on what still motivates her and “keeps me showing up every day.” She explained, “It’s the friendships and the shared belief that storytelling still matters. That baring our souls and creators still matters, something that AI will never be able to duplicate, no matter how ‘smart’ it gets.” Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As all the honorees posed for a group photo with Garcia, the room filled with a vibrant energy that fit the uplifting feel of the night. Sheikha Al Mayassa and Anna Wintour Raise $4 Million at Inaugural Franca Fund Gala in Doha Ritu Upadhyay Mon, November 24, 2025 at 9:53 PM UTC DOHA, Qatar — The evening after Fashion Trust Arabia’s star-studded awards ceremony , the fashion world reconvened for a more intimate cause: honoring the legacy of Franca Sozzani while raising funds to advance preventive genomics research. The inaugural Franca Fund Gala, held at the Museum of Islamic Art on Sunday, brought together Anna Wintour, Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, and Francesco Carrozzini, Sozzani’s son and cofounder of the Franca Sozzani Fund for Preventive Genomics. The mission: to raise more than $4 million for medical research at Harvard Medical School and Mass General Brigham. It was so generous and kind of her.” The evening drew a remarkable guest list that included Queen Rania of Jordan, Miuccia Prada, Gisele Bündchen, François-Henri Pinault, Natalia Vodianova, Selma Blair, Tessa Thompson, Tyra Banks, and designers including Christian Louboutin, Pierpaolo Piccioli, Simone Rocha, and Giambattista Valli. Carrozzini delivered an emotional keynote, thanking Wintour, who is his mother-in-law, and channeling his mother’s philosophy. “She once told me, ‘If it’s not strange, it’s not new. And if it’s not new, it won’t matter,'” he recalled. “That was Franca, fearless, restless, always pushing everyone, including herself, to see what others did not see.” He framed the fund’s mission in terms his mother would have embraced. “Health, like creativity, should not be a privilege. Preventive genomics has the power to save lives, not years from now, but today.” Advertisement Advertisement Dr. Robert Green, the Harvard professor of medicine leading the research, outlined the stakes. His team first analyzed the DNA of a healthy newborn in 2015 and discovered that nearly one in 10 babies carries genetic markers for diseases they may develop over their lifetime — conditions that can be treated or even prevented when detected early. “Could Qatar become the first nation on Earth to offer sequencing to every child, maybe in the next two to three years?” Dr. Green asked the crowd. “This isn’t just about health care. This is about economics as well.” Sheikha Mayassa recalled meeting Sozzani in 2013 at the opening of a Damien Hirst exhibition in Doha — the same artist who donated a portrait of Sozzani for the evening’s auction. “She taught us that beauty must reveal truth, not conceal it, that aesthetics must serve ethics.” The silent auction raised significant sums for the cause. The Damien Hirst portrait of Sozzani sold for $380,000, while a private tennis lesson with Jannik Sinner — the first time the world number one has offered such an experience — went for $350,000 to Qatar’s minister of health. An Audemars Piguet watch fetched $280,000. Advertisement Advertisement Wintour reflected on the fashion industry’s long history of rallying around causes, from the AIDS crisis to COVID-19 relief. “They’re always the first to step up, and they’re the first to step up as a community,” she said. With U.S. funding for medical research facing potential cuts, she noted the evening’s significance. “I know that Francesco’s team of doctors are very concerned about funding for the future, so it makes tonight even more important.” Sozzani, who died in 2016, was known for using Vogue Italia as a platform for social commentary — publishing groundbreaking issues on domestic violence, the BP oil spill, and plastic surgery. Wintour said her late friend would have been moved by the evening. “She always believed in using her platform to help others,” Wintour said. “I think she would be honored and thrilled, but so proud of her son. They had the most remarkable relationship. She really brought him up as a single mother, and I think that she would see that he was really following in her footsteps.” Best of WWD Victoria Beckham's Style Through the Years: From Her Spice Girls Era to Today [PHOTOS] Dolly Parton Through the Years: Glittering Concert Styles, Red Carpet Looks and More [PHOTOS] At What Point Is an Engagement Ring Gaudy? A few months ago, I was diagnosed with MS,” the Married … With Children alum wrote via X […] According to the Mayo Clinic , progressive supranuclear palsy is a “rare brain disease that affects walking, balance, eye movements and swallowing.” The condition results from damage to brain cells that control body movement, coordination, thinking and other functions. PSP “worsens over time and can lead to dangerous complications, such as pneumonia and trouble swallowing,” per the Mayo Clinic. There is no cure for the disease. Zooey Deschanel and Jonathan Scott are yet to plan their wedding The loved-up couple got engaged in August 2023, after four years of dating - but Jonathan admits that they haven't yet made any meaningful progress with their wedding planning. Speaking to Us Weekly, the 47-year-old TV star said: "We don’t have any updates yet. Yeah, we are the worst at planning that." On the other hand, Jonathan suggested that he and his future wife are very capable when it comes to "planning other parties". The Property Brothers star - who was previously married to Kelsy Ully, a WestJet crew scheduler, between 2007 and 2013 - said: "We’re great at planning other parties." Earlier this year, the celebrity couple claimed that they intended to get their wedding plans "figured out" in 2025. Jonathan admitted at the time that they'd made very little progress with their wedding plans, explaining that they'd both been too busy to focus on their big day. Asked if they've made any progress with their plans, Jonathan told People: "I can guarantee you we have done absolutely zero percent more work. We've just had a lot of things going on." Prior to that, Jonathan admitted that he wants to have an "intimate" wedding when they eventually tie the knot. The TV star explained that the loved-up couple had a firm idea of what they want their wedding day to look like. He told Us Weekly: "The ceremony and the pomp and circumstance, we’ll get that out of the way, and then it’s the reception. It’s going to be a blast." Jonathan and the New Girl actress were "very different people" during their younger years. But he suggested that their interests and ambitions have become more closely aligned over recent times. The reality TV star - who began dating Zooey after meeting her in 2019 - said: "I mean, we’ve both been married before, but even when we were younger, you’re looking for different things, and who knows what we were looking for at that time?" A heartfelt romantic comedy about second chances, furry feelings, and finding love again. By Kriti Pandey November 12, 2025 1 min. read Merv Trailer_pic courtesy Youtube Amazon MGM Studios is serving up something sweet this December with Merv , a heartwarming romantic comedy about love, loss, and a dog who just wants his humans to figure things out. The film stars Zooey Deschanel as Anna and Charlie Cox as Russ, a once-happy couple who’ve called it quits. But the breakup doesn’t just break their hearts, it breaks their dog’s too. Merv, their beloved pet, starts losing his spark, forcing the duo into the most awkward co-parenting situation imaginable. Hoping to help Merv find his joy again, Russ takes him on a trip to Florida for some sunshine and fresh air. Everything seems fine until Anna shows up, uninvited and still holding on to the same mix of love and frustration that broke them apart. What follows is a funny, tender, and slightly chaotic reunion where their dog’s recovery might just lead to theirs too. Directed with charm and emotional warmth, Merv is a story about how healing sometimes happens in the most unexpected ways. Zooey Deschanel brings her signature quirk and heart, while Charlie Cox balances it with quiet sincerity, creating an easy, believable chemistry that feels like a throwback to old-school rom-coms, the kind that made you believe love can find its way back. At its core, Merv isn’t just about romance. It’s about companionship, the kind that stays even when relationships don’t. The film explores how pets often become emotional anchors for humans, teaching us to love softer, forgive quicker, and laugh even when life gets messy. Merv releases on December 10, 2025, exclusively on Amazon Prime Video and will stream until June 10, 2026. It’s funny, heartfelt, and just the right kind of comfort movie we all need, because sometimes, love deserves a second leash. In recent weeks, the channel has aired the 2003 film Elf, as well as other festive favorites. The 1983 film A Christmas Story, which stars Peter Billingsley, aired twice on November 20. The bizarre move comes months after HGTV axed several fan favorite shows including The Flipping El Moussas, Christina on the Coast, Bargain Block, Married to Real Estate, Farmhouse Fixer, Izzy Does It, and Battle on the Beach. Furious viewers have voiced their complaints over the schedule and have lambasted the network for airing Christmas films instead of filling the gaps with home renovation content. Some have even suggested to bosses that they bring back some of the several shows that were canceled over the summer. Taking to Reddit, one frustrated fan started a thread which began: 'Why is Elf on HGTV?' 'This is the second week in a row that some lame a** old movie is on HGTV,' they continued. 'Where are the design shows?!? If this is the new direction of HGTV, I'm out!' But this is why I don't mess with cable anymore.' Another angry user wrote: 'We don't tune into HGTV to watch Elf. Sounds like HGTV management needs to bring back some of the cancelled programs that actually highlighted home building, remodeling, landscaping and interior design. MAYBE.' And it seems as though HGTV will not be bowing to fan pressure as there are plans to air the 2023 comedy Christmas film Candy Cane Lane, starring Eddie Murphy, on Thanksgiving. Despite the uproar, the network has recently started airing a new television show that follows people who are so obsessed with Christmas that they spend thousands of dollars each year just to store their ornaments. Hoarding for the Holidays, which began on November 11, is a four-part show that exposes the lengths some people take to house their expansive collections – and just how much it really costs to be utterly consumed by the festive season. Hoarding for the Holidays isn't the only new show headed to HGTV before the end of the year. HGTV culled numerous shows over the summer, including Married to Real Estate starring Egypt Sherrod and Mike Jackson (pictured) Cheap A$ Beach Houses, described as a 'fantasy lifestyle series,' will humorously show viewers how to own a slice of affordable paradise when it premieres on December 3. Across 16 half-hour episodes, bargain buyers will chase their coastal dreams on realistic budgets, proving you don't need to break the bank to live the beach life. The synopsis teases: 'In the series premiere, a quirky couple from Flint, Michigan, will flee harsh winters for sunny Fort Myers Beach, Florida. 'Their vivacious realtor will search for the ideal waterfront home at a reasonable price, helping them overcome obstacles like her fear of heights in high-rise properties and his obsession with properly installed electrical outlets.' Some see genius in the disguise, while others remain harsh critics. Yet even the most skeptical fans might be surprised to learn that the glasses weren’t Superman’s only choice of disguise. Mark Waid and Cian Tormey return with Action Comics #1092, exploring Clark’s early years as Superboy in Smallville . Though set in the past, the story is part of main continuity, making it a treasure trove of new details about the Man of Steel’s early life. Superman takes off his Clark Kent glasses in DC Comics This latest issue once again puts the spotlight on one of Superman’s early career disguises, where he blurred his face using super-speed vibrations. As Clark notes in the narrative, it was an impractical long-term solution, making his complete switch-over to glasses seem downright genius in comparison. Superman’s Vibration-Blurring Might Be Cool, But It Was Off-Brand Main Cover by Ryan Sook for Action Comics #1092 (2025) Action Comics #1092 follows Clark as he narrates some of his early heroics, explaining that he used to blur his face with vibrations to conceal his identity. While this method might seem brilliant at first, Clark reveals why it wasn’t practical for his kind of heroics, especially in Smallville, and why he ultimately couldn’t continue using it. Superman explains that he stopped vibration-blurring his face because he needed to give people every reason not to fear him. He adds that this is also why he chose not to wear a mask and instead opted for a bright costume, saying he “wanted people to see [him] coming, not find [him] in the shadows.” In Clark’s mind, blurring his face only made him seem less trustworthy and more frightening. So, while the disguise might have been theoretically clever, it went against his mission to gain the public’s trust. It was also likely distracting to maintain the blur, especially while he was still learning to control his powers. Still Think Superman’s Glasses Disguise Sucks? Just Look at Zooey Deschanel Cover B Joe Quinones Variant for Action Comics #1092 (2025) Clark’s reasoning for abandoning the blurred disguise and mask also shows why the box-frame glasses were such a brilliant solution for him. The glasses allowed him to maintain a civilian identity without actually hiding his features, giving him the best of both worlds. And for those who still believe Superman’s glasses disguise is unbelievable , the viral side-by-side photo of actress Zooey Deschanel, with and without her glasses and bangs, proves how dramatically small changes can alter one’s appearance, validating just how effective Superman's Clark Kent disguise really is. Movies Will Ferrell’s Elf Sets 2025 Theatrical Rerelease Date With New Content November 21, 2025 By Ryan Louis Mantilla Warner Bros. Discovery has prepared an exciting gift for Elf fans: an annual celebration honoring the classic Christmas movie, along with a theatrical rerelease and new content on the way. Starring Will Ferrell , the holiday feature — released on November 7, 2003 — is widely considered one of the best Christmas movies of all time. The Jon Favreau -directed film also stars James Caan, Zooey Deschanel, Mary Steenburgen, Ed Asner, and Bob Newhart. What new content is in the 2025 Elf theatrical rerelease? Elf is scheduled to return to cinemas on December 12. According to The Hollywood Reporter, the theatrical rerelease of the film will also feature “Buddy’s Sing & Cheer Along Edition,” along with on-screen lyrics, trivia, and some visual comedic bits. Warner Bros. Discovery will also honor the beloved movie with the first annual celebration called “December the TwELFth,” set to commence on December 12. Elf the Musical will kick off the festivities with a special noon performance in New York City’s Times Square. This one-day festivity will also include Elf photo stations, some shopping experiences, an opportunity to write to Santa Claus, and Warner Bros. Studio Tour Hollywood — a visit to the Warner Bros. Studio Store, which would allow guests to see the film’s original costumes. WBD will also match all donations to the American Red Cross made that day, up to $100,000. Elf tells the story of Buddy Hobbs (Ferrell), a man raised in the North Pole by Santa’s elves. When he learns he’s actually human, he sets off for New York, where he meets his biological father, Walter Hobbs (Caan). Elf premiered in 2003 to strong critical praise and quickly became a major box-office hit, securing its place as a beloved holiday cult classic. The movie later inspired the 2010 Broadway production Elf: The Musical as well as the 2014 stop-motion TV special Elf: Buddy’s Musical Christmas. (Source: The Hollywood Reporter ) Ryan Louis Mantilla Ryan writes about music, movies, and television shows for a living. He consumes all three for “research” purposes — fooling absolutely no one. If you make a purchase via links on this page we will earn commission - learn more The countdown to Christmas has officially begun, and streaming services are here to make sure your festive watchlist is fully stocked. From romantic mix-ups and meet-cutes to high-stakes holiday capers and family chaos, this year’s new releases promise something for everyone. Whether you’re in the mood for snowy love stories with Alicia Silverstone and Minka Kelly , hilarious misadventures with Michelle Pfeiffer and Zooey Deschanel, or action-packed Christmas mayhem with Mark Wahlberg and Michelle Monaghan , there’s plenty to keep you entertained during those long winter evenings. Here are our favourite new Christmas films to stream this holiday season. A Merry Little Ex-Mas Ready to sign the divorce papers and determined to pull off one last perfect Christmas in her family home, Kate (Alicia Silverstone) is thrown off course when her ex-husband Everett (Oliver Hudson) turns up – with his brilliant new girlfriend in tow. As the festive decorations go up and old feelings bubble back to the surface, Kate begins to realise what truly matters isn’t flawless holiday cheer, but the life she already has. A Merry Little Ex-Mas is available to stream on Netflix A Very Jonas Christmas When pop trio Jonas Brothers – Kevin, Joe and Nick – wrap their tour in London only 48 hours before Christmas, what could go wrong? Plenty. A comedic snowball of travel delays, sibling rivalry and holiday chaos lands them far from home – and far from the Christmas they were hoping for. With original songs, surprise cameos and self-aware humour, this musical comedy reminds them (and us) that getting home might just be the best kind of gift. A Very Jonas Christmas is available to stream on Disney+ Tyler Perry’s Finding Joy Joy (Shannon Thornton) is a New York fashion designer whose talent is always overshadowed – at work and in love. Determined to take a chance, she follows her crush Colton (Aaron O’Connell) to snowy Colorado. But after a shocking discovery and a brutal snowstorm, she gets stranded – only to meet Ridge (Tosin Morohunfola), whose warmth and kindness help her rethink what it really means to find joy. Tyler Perry’s Finding Joy is available to stream on Prime Video Champagne Problems When high-powered exec Sydney Price (Minka Kelly) flies to Paris to acquire the legendary Château Cassell before Christmas, her business-first plan goes off the fizz. One magical night in the City of Lights leads to a meet-cute with Henri (Tom Wozniczka), only to discover he’s the heir to the very wine empire she’s trying to buy. Now she must juggle corporate rivals, family stakes and an unexpected romance that just won’t stay corked. Champagne Problems is available to stream on Netflix The Family Plan 2 Former assassin-dad Dan (Mark Wahlberg) plans a perfect overseas Christmas with his wife Jessica (Michelle Monaghan) and their kids – but when a shadowy figure from Dan’s past (Kit Harington) crashes the party, their European holiday spirals into a festive game of cat-and-mouse filled with bank heists, car chases and family chaos. The Family Plan 2 is available to stream on Apple TV Jingle Bell Heist On Christmas Eve in London, two down-on-their-luck workers – retail assistant Sophia (Olivia Holt) and repairman Nick (Connor Swindells) – join forces to rob a posh department store. But as they plan the ultimate festive caper, sparks fly and secrets unravel, putting their unlikely alliance – and very naughty mission – in jeopardy. Jingle Bell Heist is available to stream on Netflix on 26 November My Secret Santa Single mum Taylor (Alexandra Breckenridge) is struggling to make ends meet – especially when her daughter gets into an elite snowboarding camp. Desperate, she disguises herself as an elderly man and lands a seasonal job as Santa at a luxury ski resort. But when she falls for Matthew (Ryan Eggold), the resort manager, her jolly secret threatens to unravel – and it’s not just the beard that’s on the line. Jingle Bell Heist is available to stream on Netflix on 3 December Oh. What. Fun Claire Clauster (Michelle Pfeiffer) is the unshakeable glue keeping her chaotic family’s Christmas together – until one year they forget her entirely. Feeling invisible, she sets off on a spontaneous solo adventure while her loved ones scramble to find her. Along the way, Claire rediscovers the true magic of the holidays as she learns what happens when Christmas goes off-script. Oh. What. Fun is available to stream on Prime Video on 3 December Tinsel Town When washed-up Hollywood action hero Bradley Mack (Kiefer Sutherland) lands in a tiny snow-dusted village to star in its eccentric panto production of Cinderella, he’s expecting a career reboot – but he gets so much more. Under the tough-love direction of choreographer Jill (Rebel Wilson), Bradley’s big ego begins to thaw, and he rediscovers hope, friendship and a little Christmas magic. Tinsel Town is available to stream on Sky Cinema on 5 December Merv When Anna (Zooey Deschanel) and Russ (Charlie Cox) break up, their beloved dog Merv falls into a funk – and the only way to help him heal is the most awkward co-parenting arrangement imaginable. Russ whisks Merv off to sunny Florida, only for Anna to show up unexpectedly. As Merv regains his spark, his humans might just rediscover theirs. Deadline Print Article deadline-logo-svg Print Jacki Weaver Joins Comedy Feature ‘Trash Mountain’ By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy ‘One Piece’ Casts Awdo Awdo & Daisy Head For Season 3 Sean Combs Doc From Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson Sets Netflix Premiere ‘NCIS: Origins’ Casts Shea Buckner As Young Dwayne Pride; Prequel To Round Out Fed Five View All November 11, 2025 10:27am Jacki Weaver Chelsea Lauren/Penske Media via Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Two-time Academy Award-nominated Jacki Weaver ( Animal Kingdom, Silver Linings Playbook ) joins the previously announced Caleb Hearon, Zooey Deschanel, Kyle Marvin, and Jaboukie Young-White in the comedy film Trash Mountain . The Hearon and Ruby Caster-written film is currently in production in Chicago. From director Kris Rey (I Used to Go Here) , Trash Mountain follows 27-year-old gay man Gavin (Hearon), who is thriving in Chicago, when the sudden death of his father forces him back to his hometown in rural Missouri. The story takes the audience on an emotional journey as Gavin and his half-sister Abbi (Deschanel) navigate challenging family dynamics and their complicated relationships with the past. Weaver plays Grandma Helen, the matriarch of the family and mother of Gavin and Abbi’s deceased father, who was an obsessive hoarder. Distraught by the death of her son, Grandma Helen struggles to connect with her family. Lilly Wachowski ( The Matrix , Cloud Atlas ) executive produces, as well as Julie Lebedev and Eddie Vaisman for Sight Unseen, Carrie Holt De Lama, alongside Zachary Spicer, Chris Cafero for Five Sticks Productions, and Scott Goldstein for Streeterville Productions. Colin Trevorrow is producing through his Metronome banner, which most recently released the comedy Deep Cover. Rebecca Linfoot will oversee on behalf of Metronome. Weaver is best known for her performance in the David Michôd feature Animal Kingdom (2010), for which she was nominated for the 2011 Oscar for Best Supporting Actress. Subsequently, Weaver received an Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress for David O. Russell’s The Silver Linings Playbook . On the TV front, Weaver was a lead in FX’s limited series Clipped , where she stars as Shelly Sterling, the co-owner of the Los Angeles Clippers and wife of Donald Sterling. She also had a starring role on the Apple TV series Hello Tomorrow! , in a large recurring arc in Taylor Sheridan’s Yellowstone , and in the lead role in the Australian series Bloom . Weaver is repped by Elevate Entertainment and CAA. "It’s like a book club but with movies," said RPL. Watch the selected film on your own and then join the group for a lively discussion each month. Plots, themes, characters, soundtracks, symbolism, cinematography, and more are all discussion options. From casual viewers to cinephiles, all levels of interest in film are welcome. Participants can request the selected film through interlibrary loan or find it on various streaming services. This month’s discussion is centered on the 2022 biographical drama, Dreamin’ Wild, written, directed, and produced by Bill Pohlad, and starring Casey Affleck, Noah Jupe, Zooey Deschanel, Walton Goggins, Jack Dylan Grazer, and Beau Bridges. Thirty years after it was recorded, the 1978 debut album of brothers Donnie and Joe Emerson is rediscovered long after they have given up on their rock 'n roll dreams. For more information or with questions, call 594-0310 or email refdesk@rocklandmaine.gov . Editorial Opinion By DanielKlissmman - Nov 23, 2025 02:11 PM EST Filed Under: Captain Marvel I'm a big Captain Marvel fan. I love Carol Danvers and have followed her comic book adventures for a long time. When Marvel Studios announced plans to adapt her for live-action in her very own feature film, it was, frankly, a dream come true. After that, came the waiting period for a casting announcement. With each passing day, my excitement to know who'd bring Danvers to life grew significantly. Then, the news I (alongside many other fans) had been waiting for hit the internet: Brie Larson had officially been cast as the Captain . Saying I was delighted when I saw the announcement would be a significant understatement, because she remains, to this day, one of Marvel Studios' best casting choices. Not only did Larson look like Kevin Feige himself had reached into a Captain Marvel comic and plucked her from it, she was an Oscar-winning actress with a solid track record in films like 21 Jump Street and Short Term 12 . Following her casting, Larson shared a picture of herself doing research for the role, building up excitement for her portrayal. Then, her arrival was teased in the post-credits scene of Avengers Infinity War —arguably one of the most memorable MCU stingers to date. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Brie Larson (@brielarson) With all of that, hype levels for her portrayal were through the roof. Finally, 2019 came around, and Captain Marvel released... and, well, neither Brie Larson nor the film disappointed. You know what? Let's not downplay it: The movie was a massive hit. It scored a 79% on Rotten Tomatoes, and earned $1.1 billion worldwide against a reported $150 million budget , making it one of the most successful films in Marvel Studios' nearly-20-year history. All signs pointed to the public embracing Larson's Danvers. Sadly, though, the years following her MCU debut would see the actress be incessantly maligned. During the Avengers: Endgame press tour, for example, her body language was closely scrutinized, and then somehow used as fuel to feed the idea that she was, simply put, insufferable. That perception, disappointingly enough, stuck, and the actress became a controversial figure in the eyes of the audience. Even with only one standalone film and a supporting part in a large ensemble piece under her belt, Brie Larson quickly rose through the ranks of most disliked MCU performers. Not helping matters was the spectacular flopping of The Marvels , the follow-up film in her once promising franchise. The movie made $206 million worldwide against a reported budget of approximately $370 million . It made less than The Flash , and that was a gosh-darn disaster of epic proportions. The failure aided in the narrative that Larson was not right for the cosmic hero. So, yes, things have, unfortunately, not looked good for Brie Larson's Captain Marvel for a while popularity-wise... but you know what? It needs to be said: Marvel Studios hit the jackpot with her, because she is the perfect Carol Danvers. Admittedly, that may not mean much when she's the only live-action version of the character, but her portrayal is, nonetheless, a brilliant translation of the hero from the comics. Call me Captain Marvel. pic.twitter.com/IgqRIb9ijM — Brie Larson (@brielarson) July 24, 2016 Much has been said about the actress' performance in Captain Marvel , often called stiff. However, for the life of me, I have never understood the problem with it. The point of the film was Carol rediscovering her identity after being kidnapped and being re-raised as a secret weapon by the Kree. She was meant to be serious, stern, and she conveyed that perfectly without coming across as stiff. Furthermore, there were still glimmers of Danvers' original, livelier personality in her sternness, which shone through more and more as she shed her complex brain re-programming. Larson gave Captain Marvel a nuanced personality, successfully conveying her internal struggle between the person she thought she was, and the personality that was within her, eager to burst out of its imposed shell. Something that's often forgotten is the fact that Larson is a powerhouse actor. There's a reason, after all, why she earned an Academy Award for 2015's Room . That movie is a punch to the gut in the best way possible. It fills you with existential dread, and forcibly puts you in Joy's emotional states as her mental health declines throughout the film. That largely stems from Brie Larson's brilliant character work. She delivers a beautiful performance, gripping you and taking you into a harrowing sea of emotions. You understand Joy's pain, and love, and regret, and pride in her son. She makes you feel it, and that's not easy to do. For a more recent example of her acting prowess, she also delivers a great performance on Apple TV+'s Lessons in Chemistry . Larson is a world-class artist, and the fact that Marvel Studios got her to star as one of its premier superheroes is arguably one of the biggest accomplishments in the company's long list of successes. Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars are fast approaching, and I sincerely hope we get to spend more time with Larson's Carol Danvers in these upcoming MCU adventures. Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18, 2026. News Brie Larson and Benny Safdie cast in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie Larson will voice Princess Rosalina, with Safdie playing Bowser Jr. Donovan Erskine November 12, 2025 6:38 AM 1 The Super Mario Galaxy Movie got its first full-length trailer, and it introduced Rosalina and Bowser Jr. as two new characters joining the adventure. Nintendo and Universal have confirmed that Rosalina and Bowser Jr. will be played by Brie Larson and Benny Safdie, respectively. We got our first look at the two new members of the Mario family during the latest Nintendo Direct . Both making their debut in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Bowser Jr. and Rosalina will be significant characters in the story. While Bowser Jr. is on a mission to free his imprisoned father, Rosalina watches over a family of Lumas in outer space. We see Rosalina fighting off a robotic enemy in the trailer. Brie Larson is an Academy Award-winning actress most known for her role as Captain Marvel in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. She’s also a well-documented Nintendo fan, and even appeared in a commercial for the Nintendo Switch. Benny Safdie is an actor-director hybrid who co-directed Uncut Gems, and appeared in blockbusters like Oppenheimer. We’ll get to hear Larson and Safdie in full when The Super Mario Galaxy Movie hits theaters in April 2026. In the meantime, tune into This Week in Switch 2 for more Nintendo discussions. The actress revealed that she was initially hesitant to play the role, concerned about how the fame and attention might affect her everyday life. Brie Larson talks being hesitant to play Captain Marvel at first Brie Larson recently opened up about her initial hesitation to play Captain Marvel in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Speaking at SpaceCon San Antonio in October 2025, the actress revealed that she initially struggled with the idea of taking on such a high-profile role. She said, “I was offered the role of Captain Marvel, and I was really nervous about saying yes to it, and I literally sat down with a piece of paper and wrote down why it made me so scared to say yes.” Larson went on to share her concerns about the impact the role could have on her privacy and everyday life. She explained, “I was really an introvert, and I was very worried about all the things that would come after. I was worried about lack of privacy.” The actress added, “I was worried that I wouldn’t be able to have a voice or be…I’d have stage fright doing something like this.” She was also worried about letting other people down. To overcome those fears, Larson focused on establishing a balance between her public career and personal life. She stated, “And I was able to say, ‘Okay, well, I know when this movie is coming out. I got a couple of years. So that gives me three years of a runway to figure out what matters to me in my life, what I’m going to protect, what’s going to be private for me.” Larson ultimately accepted the role, debuting as Carol Danvers in 2019’s Captain Marvel. Meghan Markle joins cast of Amazon MGM movie with Brie Larson and others Meghan Markle has officially returned to acting after an eight-year hiatus. Sources confirmed to Deadline that the Duchess of Sussex has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios’ film Close Personal Friends, marking her first role since departing Suits in 2017. She was recently seen filming in Pasadena, Calif., where People reported she “seemed very relaxed and happy” on set. According to The Sun , Markle has a small role in the Jason Orley–directed project, which also stars Brie Larson, Lily Collins, Jack Quaid, and Henry Golding. An insider told People, “She introduced herself to everyone and was very sweet and down-to-earth.” The film, described as a comedy about a couple meeting celebrities during a Santa Barbara trip, began production in London before moving to California. Suits creator Aaron Korsh told Deadline he had once considered a cameo for Markle in the show’s finale but chose not to ask out of respect for her “new life.” Markle’s last on-camera appearance was in her Netflix cooking series With Love , Meghan, which released two seasons under her Archewell Productions banner. The actress last appeared in 2023's The Marvels , where she teamed up with fellow MCU superheroes Ms. Marvel (Iman Vellani) and Monica Rambeau (Teyonah Parris). Although The Marvels post-credits scene seemed to set up Avengers: Doomsday by showing Monica in an alternate universe where her mother, Maria Rambeau (Lashana Lynch), had become Captain Marvel and worked with the X-Men — including Kelsey Grammer's Beast — the characters' futures in the franchise remain unknown. That includes Larson's Captain Marvel. When Marvel unveiled the official cast of Avengers: Doomsday , Larson was nowhere to be seen. In fact, the only actor to appear in The Marvels that was confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday was Grammer. He joined MCU mainstays like Chris Hemsworth and Anthony Mackie alongside a handful of original X-Men movie actors, including Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen. So the question has become why Beast would appear in Avengers: Doomsday but not Monica Rambeau or Captain Marvel. Well, after a recent post from Larson, MCU fans are convinced Marvel Studios is keeping some members of the Avengers: Doomsday cast under wraps. Why Marvel Fans Think Brie Larson Is In Avengers: Doomsday captain marvel looking tough Earlier this week, Larson shared a photo of her voting on Election Day, Nov. 4, with a caption that reads, "Ignore the wig!! 🤫" With the hood of Larson's sweatshirt pulled up, only a lock of blonde hair is visible, but it's notably longer than the short pixie cut she's been rocking for the last couple of months. Since the glimpse of the wig looks like a longer hairstyle, Marvel fans are convinced Larson was wearing it to play Captain Marvel. Last Carol Danvers appeared in the MCU, she did sport longer hair. Additionally, Larson's caption, with the shushing emoji, does make it seem like a spoiler of some kind, and Marvel is notoriously secretive, causing fans to believe it's an Avengers: Doomsday spoiler. Will Brie Larson Really Be In Avengers: Doomsday? Captain Marvel glowing and looking serious in The Marvels However, there's one major problem with the assumption that Larson has accidentally spoiled a potential return in Avengers: Doomsday . It's very unlikely she's currently filming on Avengers: Doomsday since the film wrapped a few months ago, and it's too soon for reshoots to have begun. While there undoubtedly will be reshoots, the filmmakers and studio need to first sift through the footage from the main production before they can figure out what they still need. Additionally, reshoots aren't likely to be done in Los Angeles, California, which is where Larson lives and would be voting. Most Marvel productions are filmed in London, UK, or Atlanta, Georgia, with a few exceptions. But it seems unlikely Larson would be filming Doomsday reshoots the same day she was voting in LA. All that said, it's not impossible for Captain Marvel to appear in Avengers: Doomsday . Since Beast and other members of the X-Men are confirmed to return, it would certainly make sense for Monica Rambeau and Captain Marvel to be in the movie as well. Unless Marvel has decided to retcon The Marvels and leave it behind them. For now, it remains to be seen whether Larson's Captain Marvel will be in Avengers: Doomsday . When the cast was first announced, Marvel indicated more actors would be revealed at a later date, but they've yet to do so. It's possible Larson will be confirmed later for Avengers: Doomsday and has either already completed her filming or will be part of reshoots. While fans might be convinced of her return, it's best to wait for Marvel to confirm whether Captain Marvel really will be in Avengers: Doomsday when it debuts next year. Nintendo showcased its special Super Mario Galaxy Movie Direct event today, which, ultimately, only confirmed a few things we didn't already know, like how it would've been a better surprise that Bowser Jr. is in the film if that hadn't leaked ahead of time . That's not to say there wasn't anything worth checking out, since we did get new insight into the plot of this film, and two major new cast members were revealed. Of course, we also got a new trailer for the film, which showed off more of Illumination's impressive animation work. While the first Super Mario Bros. Movie focused on introducing Mario and Luigi to the Mushroom Kingdom, the Super Mario Galaxy Movie picks up right where the first one left off, with Bowser still shrunk after eating a shrinking mushroom, and life in the Mushroom Kingdom relatively peaceful. Related Story Nintendo Switch 2 System Update 21.0.1 Fixes Frustrating Bluetooth Issue and More Enter Bowser Jr., played by Benny Safdie, who you'd recognize from his work in Oppenheimer and Uncut Gems, who is on a quest to save his father from what essentially looks like a small prison he's being kept in, so Mario and Luigi can keep an eye on him. In a currently unexplained way, Bowser Jr.'s attempted rescue of his dad leads to a galaxy-spanning journey, which is also where Princess Rosalina comes in, played by Marvel star Brie Larson. Brie Larson's involvement isn't exactly a surprise, considering her outspoken love for Nintendo and involvement in multiple Nintendo Switch commercials. If anything, it's a shock that she wasn't already involved in the first film, and had to wait for the second one to come around to get a role. Benny Safdie is a more intriguing choice, and from the sounds of it, will be a fun one as he steps into the junior Koopa feet of Bowser Jr., heir to his father's throne. The trailer also includes a few hints at what's to come, like confirmation that the Sand Kingdom from Super Mario Odyssey will be one of the locations the film visits on its journey. The first full Super Mario Galaxy Movie trailer has finally landed, and it looks like Nintendo and Illumination are doing it big for their next animated feature. Though there are a few shots of the Mushroom Kingdom and a very miniscule Bowser (Jack Black) imprisoned in a tiny castle, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie ’s new trailer has everyone looking up to the sky as Mario (Chris Pratt), Luigi (Charlie Day), Toad (Keegan-Michael Key) and Princess Peach (Anya Taylor-Joy) venture off into space. That’s where the group encounters a vengeful Bowser Jr. (Benny Safdie) who’s ready to wage war and free his father using a magic paintbrush that can transform things into metallic versions of themselves. The young villain’s arsenal of weapons makes it seem like Mario and his crew might be outgunned for a while. But the heroes will have Princess Rosalina (Brie Larson) — who looks like she’ll end up being a heavy hitter — on their side. The trailer leans heavily into the action set pieces team Mario will find themselves at the center of as they hop from planet to planet looking for a way to stop their new foe. Curiously, Yoshi doesn’t make an appearance here. But given the last film’s post credits sequence, we can probably expect to see the shoe-wearing dinosaur as we get closer to The Super Mario Galaxy Movie ’s April 3rd, 2026 premiere date. Destin Daniel Cretton ’s feature, Short Term 12 is based on the award-winning short of the same name. The film premiered at the SXSW Film Festival in 2013 and received critical acclaim for its raw and emotional subject matter and standout performances, particularly from then newcomer Brie Larson . Short Term 12 went on to win the Jury Award and Audience Award for Narrative Feature Competition. Earlier this year, Cretton re-teamed with Larson for the adaptation of The Glass Castle , based on the memoir by Jeannette Walls . We are happy to share his #SXSWFilm25 story with you. "I am forever grateful to SXSW for seeing the heart of our little movie and believing that audiences would connect with it. I remember watching our first screening at the Alamo Drafthouse on a Sunday morning, just after the daylight savings switch-over. Everyone was hung-over from the night before, and I had convinced myself they'd all hate the movie. But sitting in that theater alongside Brie Larson , John G Jr ., Keith Stanfield , Rami Malek and the rest of our team was one of the most moving experiences of my life. I've never felt so connected to an audience before. Without this festival, I honestly don't know if Short Term 12 would have seen the light of day. We owe you all so much for believing in us." The follow-up to 2023's $1.3 billion hit The Super Mario Bros. Movie , the brand-new teaser trailer confirms that famous Nintendo characters Rosalina and Bowser Jr. will be a part of the story. With the returning cast of Chris Pratt, Charlie Day, Anya Taylor-Joy, Jack Black, and Keegan-Michael Key, the new movie will be based in part on the plot of the Super Mario Galaxy game, seeing Mario and friends traveling to new locations across the galaxy as they again must fight Bowser, whom they defeated and imprisoned in the previous installment. With this trailer's release, it was announced that MCU star and Academy Award winner Brie Larson will be voicing Rosalina, while actor and filmmaker Benny Safdie will be playing Bowser Jr. Both have big moments teasing what is to come in the trailer. Check out the announcement below: There has been much anticipation and speculation surrounding which new Nintendo characters would be in The Super Mario Bros. Movie 2 , with Rosalina especially being an oft-discussed choice. The adoptive mother of the Lumas, Rosalina acts as a guide to Mario in Super Mario Galaxy , though she appears to have a more active role in the movie adaptation. Meanwhile, Bowser Jr. is critical because Bowser, as a threat, has been neutralized; the movie needs his son to come and rescue him in order for there to be conflict. Safdie is both a comedic and dramatic actor who can imbue Bowser Jr. with much chaotic energy, having appeared in movies including Pieces of a Woman, Licorice Pizza, Oppenheimer , and Happy Gilmore 2 . Safdie is also known as a witty writer-director, co-directing Uncut Gems with his brother Josh Safdie, though he had less success with his solo project, The Smashing Machine , this year. Meanwhile, Brie Larson is a longtime megastar; she was not on my list of actors who could have played Rosalina in the Super Mario movie , but she is exactly the talent role calls for. Getting her start with feel-good movies like Scott Pilgrim vs. the World and The Spectacular Now , Larson went on to win her Oscar for the heavy drama Room , before landing her MCU role as Captain Marvel . Her Marvel storyline has been in decline in recent years, but she has starred in other action movies and even reprised her role in Scott Pilgrim Takes Off . The Super Mario Galaxy Movie hits theaters on April 6, 2026, roughly three years after its predecessor. It is gearing up to be another crowd-pleasing adventure, with delightful bouts of nostalgia and a stellar cast carrying it all the way through. Deadline Print Article deadline-logo-svg Print Jacki Weaver Joins Comedy Feature ‘Trash Mountain’ By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy ‘One Piece’ Casts Awdo Awdo & Daisy Head For Season 3 Sean Combs Doc From Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson Sets Netflix Premiere ‘NCIS: Origins’ Casts Shea Buckner As Young Dwayne Pride; Prequel To Round Out Fed Five View All November 11, 2025 10:27am Jacki Weaver Chelsea Lauren/Penske Media via Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Two-time Academy Award-nominated Jacki Weaver ( Animal Kingdom, Silver Linings Playbook ) joins the previously announced Caleb Hearon, Zooey Deschanel, Kyle Marvin, and Jaboukie Young-White in the comedy film Trash Mountain . The Hearon and Ruby Caster-written film is currently in production in Chicago. From director Kris Rey (I Used to Go Here) , Trash Mountain follows 27-year-old gay man Gavin (Hearon), who is thriving in Chicago, when the sudden death of his father forces him back to his hometown in rural Missouri. The story takes the audience on an emotional journey as Gavin and his half-sister Abbi (Deschanel) navigate challenging family dynamics and their complicated relationships with the past. Weaver plays Grandma Helen, the matriarch of the family and mother of Gavin and Abbi’s deceased father, who was an obsessive hoarder. Distraught by the death of her son, Grandma Helen struggles to connect with her family. Lilly Wachowski ( The Matrix , Cloud Atlas ) executive produces, as well as Julie Lebedev and Eddie Vaisman for Sight Unseen, Carrie Holt De Lama, alongside Zachary Spicer, Chris Cafero for Five Sticks Productions, and Scott Goldstein for Streeterville Productions. Colin Trevorrow is producing through his Metronome banner, which most recently released the comedy Deep Cover. Rebecca Linfoot will oversee on behalf of Metronome. Weaver is best known for her performance in the David Michôd feature Animal Kingdom (2010), for which she was nominated for the 2011 Oscar for Best Supporting Actress. Subsequently, Weaver received an Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress for David O. Russell’s The Silver Linings Playbook . On the TV front, Weaver was a lead in FX’s limited series Clipped , where she stars as Shelly Sterling, the co-owner of the Los Angeles Clippers and wife of Donald Sterling. She also had a starring role on the Apple TV series Hello Tomorrow! , in a large recurring arc in Taylor Sheridan’s Yellowstone , and in the lead role in the Australian series Bloom . Weaver is repped by Elevate Entertainment and CAA. She is passionate about finding new angles on the latest movies and TV shows. With over five years of industry experience, her goal is to highlight lesser-known and interesting elements of pop culture projects. Sign in to your Collider account follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Jennifer Lawrence has built one of the most versatile and acclaimed careers of her generation, effortlessly moving between blockbuster franchises and unique indie projects . Beloved for her authenticity and emotional intensity, she's the kind of actor who can ground even the most fantastical story in truth. On Letterboxd , a platform where cinephiles value performance, storytelling, and craft, Lawrence's best-rated movies reveal not just her range, but the kind of work that resonates most deeply with thoughtful movie lovers everywhere. What's striking about Lawrence's highest-rated movies is how they capture different stages of her evolution as an artist. Across these roles, she manages to present complex characters who are fighters, survivors, outcasts. Her projects not only showcase her acting chops but also engage with themes like identity, resilience, and morality that resonate strongly with the Letterboxd community. Ultimately, Jennifer Lawrence's top-rated movies on Letterboxd tell a story of artistic integrity and evolution . 10 'The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2' (2015) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.4/5 Natalie Dormer next to Jennifer Lawrence drawing a bow and arrow in The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 2. Image via Lionsgate The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 concludes Katniss Everdeen's (Lawrence) journey as she leads the rebellion against the oppressive Capitol . After being manipulated by both sides, Katniss joins a covert mission with Gale ( Liam Hemsworth ), Finnick ( Sam Claflin ), and Peeta ( Josh Hutcherson ) to assassinate President Snow ( Donald Sutherland ) and end the conflict once and for all. As they navigate a deadly, booby-trapped Capitol, they face devastating losses. Since Katniss Everdeen is one of Lawrence's most well-known roles, it makes sense that Letterboxd users would rate all The Hunger Games movies as some of her best projects. In particular, it makes sense that fans would highlight The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 , since it brings Katniss' story to a close. Of all The Hunger Games movies, it's clear that this one resonates with fans because Lawrence shows how far Katniss has come . 9 'Causeway' (2022) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.4/5 Jennifer Larence as Lynsey looking outside her window in Causeway. Image via Apple TV Causeway introduces Lynsey (Lawrence), a U.S. Army engineer who suffers a traumatic brain injury while serving in Afghanistan and returns home to New Orleans to recover. Struggling with memory loss, emotional instability, and a sense of disconnection, she moves in with her mother and tries to rebuild her life. As she grapples with the desire to return to active duty, Lynsey forms an unexpected friendship with James ( Brian Tyree Henry ), a local mechanic coping with his own trauma. Causeway is a compassionate portrayal of PTSD and highlights real issues veterans face every day. The movie represents Lawrence's return to the kind of intimate, emotionally grounded storytelling that first earned her critical acclaim and has made her fans appreciate her work . It makes sense that Causeway would resonate with Letterboxd users since it highlights Lawrence's ability to portray a deeply relatable character with subtlety and nuance. 8 'Die My Love' (2025) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.4/5 Grace (Jennifer Lawrence) and Jackson (Robert Pattinson) dancing together in 'Die My Love' Image via MUBI Die My Love is a psychological drama that follows Grace (Lawrence) and Jackson ( Robert Pattinson ), a young couple who move from New York City to rural Montana to live in Jackson's childhood home, seeking a quieter life after the birth of their child. As Grace struggles with post-partum depression, she slips into isolation and confusion as her mental health worsens . Grace and Jackson's relationship also deteriorates as Grace's inner world becomes more chaotic. Die My Love gives Lawrence the space to deliver one of her most visceral and vulnerable performances to date, which makes it stand out among Letterboxd users. Die My Love dives deeply into complex themes like the realities of motherhood, mental illness, and feminine rage with unflinching honesty . Lawrence showcases the fact that she can elevate any partnership or ensemble she's part of, which makes this one of her most notable works . 7 'Mother!' (2017) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.5/5 Him guiding Mother through a crowd of strangers Image via Paramount Pictures Mother! is a psychological horror movie that follows a young woman living with her poet husband in a secluded house she has painstakingly rebuilt after a fire . Their tranquil life unravels when uninvited guests arrive, first a mysterious couple and then a chaotic flood of people who invade their home, which completely upends their lives. As events spiral into violence and destruction, the story morphs into a disturbing metaphor for creation. It makes sense that Mother! is one of Jennifer Lawrence's highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it’s the kind of bold, divisive, and symbolically rich movie fans have come to expect from her. Lawrence's emotionally raw, physically demanding portrayal of a mother anchors the chaos and gives the movie its human core . Mother! is exactly the kind of movie that so many viewers respond to since it's so unique and unforgettable. 6 'Winter's Bone' (2010) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.5/5 Jennifer Lawrence as Ree standing next to her horse in 'Winter's Bone' Image via Roadhouse Attractions Winter's Bone follows 17-year-old Ree Dolly (Lawrence) as she struggles to keep her impoverished family together in the Ozark Mountains. When her missing father, out on bail after serving time for a drug charge, puts their home up as bond collateral, Ree must find him before they lose everything . Her search leads her through a harsh, secretive rural community steeped in poverty, crime, and silence. She has only herself to rely on as she tries to do what's best for her family. It makes sense that Letterboxd users would highlight Winter's Bone as one of Lawrence's best movies because it's an early example of her talent and range as an artist. Through her character, Lawrence explores the realities that many living in rural America face . The movie's quiet intensity, social realism, and moral complexity make it a standout example of early-2010s American indie cinema , a genre in which Lawrence made a name for herself. 5 'X-Men: First Class' (2011) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.6/5 Charles Xavier (James McAvoy), Magneto (Michael Fassbender), Mystique (Jennifer Lawrence), Moira MacTaggert (Rose Byrne), Beast (Nicholas Hoult), Havok (Lucas Till), and Banshee (Caleb Landry Jones), standing outside in X-Men: First Class Image via 20th Century Studios X-Men: First Class is a superhero origin story that explores the beginnings of the X-Men and the ideological divide between future rivals Charles Xavier ( James McAvoy ) and Magneto ( Michael Fassbender ). Set during the Cold War and the Cuban Missile Crisis, the film follows young mutants discovering their powers and banding together to stop the powerful mutant Sebastian Shaw ( Kevin Bacon ), who plans to trigger global nuclear war to wipe out humanity. It makes sense that X-Men: First Class is one of Jennifer Lawrence's highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it stands out as a stylish, character-driven reinvention of the superhero genre. Unlike many formulaic comic-book movies, First Class blends political history, emotional depth, and sleek 1960s aesthetics with well-drawn characters and moral complexity. As Mystique, Lawrence proves that she could always hold her own in big franchises and stand out in a crowd . 4 'X-Men: Days of Future Past' (2014) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.7/5 Jennifer Lawrence as Mystique looking intently in the 2014 movie X-Men: Days of Future Past Image via 20th Century Studios X-Men: Days of Future Past is a continuation of First Class , and a time-bending superhero epic that unites the casts of the original X-Men trilogy. In a dystopian future where mutant-hunting Sentinels have nearly exterminated both mutants and humans who aid them , the surviving X-Men send Wolverine's ( Hugh Jackman ) consciousness back to 1973 to prevent the war’s origins. His mission is to convince a disillusioned young Charles Xavier and an embittered Magneto to work together and stop Mystique. It makes sense that X-Men: Days of Future Past is one of Jennifer Lawrence's highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it represents the X-Men franchise at its creative and emotional peak . If First Class proved Lawrence could hold her own in a massive franchise, X-Men: Days of Future Past proved she could be a leader. Lawrence's role as Mystique is pivotal . She's not just a shapeshifting fighter but the emotional core of the story, whose moral choices determine the fate of mutantkind. 3 'Silver Linings Playbook' (2012) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.7/5 Jennifer Lawrence, who is wearing her hair in a ponytail and a black shirt, glares at Bradley Cooper, who is wearing a number 10 Eagles jersey, in Silver Linings Playbook. Behind them, there is a large photograph of a couple holding a toddler. Image via The Weinstein Company Silver Linings Playbook is a romantic dramedy that follows Pat Solitano ( Bradley Cooper ), a man struggling with bipolar disorder after a violent breakdown, as he tries to rebuild his life after a stint in a mental health facility . Determined to reconcile with his estranged wife, he moves back in with his parents, Dolores ( Jacki Weaver ) and Pat ( Robert De Niro ). He meets Tiffany (Lawrence), a young widow dealing with her own grief and emotional instability. Silver Linings Playbook stands out with Letterboxd users because it perfectly showcases her emotional range, comedic timing, and naturalistic acting style. Lawrence's portrayal of Tiffany as a complex, impulsive, and deeply empathetic woman feels raw and authentic, grounding the movie's blend of chaos and charm. Silver Linings Playbook balances its indie with a story that earned mainstream appeal, making it one of Lawrence's most beloved and respected works . 2 'The Hunger Games' (2012) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.8/5 The Hunger Games is a dystopian drama that is the first chapter in the franchise. The story is set in the totalitarian nation of Panem, where the ruling Capitol forces 12 impoverished districts to send a boy and a girl each year to fight to the death in a televised event known as the Hunger Games. When her younger sister Prim ( Willow Shields ) is chosen as a tribute, 16-year-old Katniss Everdeen (Lawrence) volunteers to take her place, joining Peeta Mellark as District 12's representatives. It makes sense that The Hunger Games is one of Jennifer Lawrence's highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it's a rare blockbuster that combines thrilling entertainment with strong social commentary. This movie proves beyond a doubt that Lawrence can shine in a blockbuster franchise while elevating the performances of those around her . Lawrence's performance anchors the story with authenticity and quiet strength, turning a popular book adaptation into a genuinely respected project . 1 'The Hunger Games: Catching Fire' (2013) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.9/5 Josh Hutcherson as Peeta and Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss look pensive in The Hunger Games: Catching Fire. Image via Lionsgate The Hunger Games: Catching Fire continues Katniss Everdeen's story as she becomes a reluctant symbol of hope after surviving the Hunger Games with fellow tribute Peeta Mellark. Katniss struggles with trauma and guilt while trying to protect her loved ones from President Snow , who sees her defiance as a threat to his power. To crush her growing influence, Snow announces the "Quarter Quell," a special edition of the Games that forces previous victors to compete again. The Hunger Games: Catching Fire being Jennifer Lawrence's highest-rated movie on Letterboxd makes sense because it's widely considered the artistic and emotional peak of the Hunger Games franchise . This chapter of the story features a darker tone and a clear sense of purpose, which makes it stand out . This movie highlights how much Lawrence understands Katniss, since she compassionately showcases the trauma she's lived through. Share Link copied! Share ADVERTISEMENT Florence Pugh has opened up about her past relationship with Zach Braff and the public scrutiny surrounding their 21-year age gap. Speaking on The Louis Theroux Podcast , the British actress recalled feeling “hurt” by the wave of negative comments she faced during her relationship with the Scrubs star. Florence and the 50-year-old actor dated for three years between 2019 and 2022. Throughout their relationship, she publicly defended him several times against criticism of their age difference. Highlights Florence Pugh discussed the "toxic" public scrutiny surrounding her former relationship with Zach Braff, who is 21 years her senior. The actress dated the 50-year-old 'Scrubs' star from 2019 to 2022. Florence also spoke candidly about struggling with her mental health, including accidental self-injuries. BP Daily - Your Source for Unbiased Reporting Florence Pugh reflected on the 21-year age difference between her and her ex, Zach Braff Florence Pugh wearing a white strapless dress and diamond necklace, addressing age gap with ex Zach Braff and public backlash. Image credits: florencepugh “It was an insane amount of ab*se being hurled at my relationship just because there was an age gap,” she told Louis Theroux. ADVERTISEMENT “I stood up for it, and I stood up for him and I stood up for me just being allowed to do whatever the f*** I wanted to do, and that kind of did actually change a few people’s minds.” Florence added that defending the people she cares about is part of who she is, even if it means going against what’s considered the norm. Florence Pugh and Zach Braff smiling together in a casual setting discussing their age gap and public reactions. Image credits: officiallouistheroux “I’ll always make sure that if there needs to be a reset and there needs to be a bit of a smack on the wrist, I will do that because it’s not fair that so much of your life gets to have jabs,” she said. In 2020, Florence turned off the Instagram comments on a post celebrating Zach’s 45th birthday after receiving what she described as “toxic” remarks about their age gap, which left her feeling “sad” and “upset.” ADVERTISEMENT Florence said she was “hurt” by the intense public criticism of their age difference Florence Pugh speaking in a podcast studio about age gap with ex Zach Braff and the backlash she faced. Image credits: Louis Theroux She later addressed her critics in a video, telling them, “I do not need you to tell me who I should and should not love.” In December 2019, Zach left a crown emoji beneath one of Florence’s Instagram posts, prompting one person to comment, “You’re 44 years old.” Florence defended her partner, replying simply, “And yet he got it👌🏽” Florence Pugh outdoors in a black shirt, looking thoughtful while reflecting on age gap and public reaction. ADVERTISEMENT Image credits: A24 ADVERTISEMENT Comment discussing societal pressure on happiness and mental health, relating to Florence Pugh age gap with ex Zach Braff. The Oscar nominee , who made her acting debut in The Falling over a decade ago, has learned that being in the spotlight means people will criticize her relationship if they don’t align with their expectations of who she should be dating. “It doesn’t matter how much you speak on it or how little you speak on it, people don’t care,” Florence told Louis. “They want a story; they want a reality show. It doesn’t really matter how much you say you love someone or how much they make you happy. “If they don’t like them and it doesn’t fit that image that they want of you, they don’t care. And I think that hurt me.” The Oppenheimer actress recently appeared on The Louis Theroux Podcast ADVERTISEMENT View this post on Instagram A post shared by Louis Theroux (@officiallouistheroux) Screenshot of Safeguard Recovery Team comment emphasizing mental health support and stigma removal in crisis situations. At another point in the podcast, the 29-year-old got candid about one of the most difficult periods in her life, when her body would “scream” at her that she needed to make a change. ADVERTISEMENT Florence reflected on a past relationship that made her realize how harshly she had been treating herself. Florence Pugh speaking in a podcast studio, discussing age gap and experiences with ex Zach Braff. Image credits: Louis Theroux “I had a breakdown,” she told Louis. “When you are not sleeping or you’re drinking too much or you’ve got the sh**s because you’re so anxious – that’s your body screaming at you.” ADVERTISEMENT The Midsommar star shared that, during this challenging time, her body “was just like, in full panic mode” and was “asking for help.” Florence and the Scrubs actor dated between 2019 and 2022 Florence Pugh and Zach Braff posing together at an event, addressing age gap and public reaction. Image credits: Karwai Tang/WireImage Facebook comment by Will Scott discussing Florence Pugh and Zach Braff's breakup and age gap in a light blue text box. Man lying on couch cuddling a small dog near large yellow flowers and rainy window, reflecting Florence Pugh age gap with ex Zach Braff. ADVERTISEMENT Image credits: florencepugh ADVERTISEMENT Comment screenshot showing a discussion about Florence Pugh addressing age gap and public reaction with ex Zach Braff. Florence added that she felt pressured to spend all her energy focusing on the wellbeing of others, ultimately neglecting her own mental health. “When you are such a bubbly person and you fill in a lot of energy for other people, I’m definitely the last person that I look after. “I felt like there was an expectation that I needed to be good for everybody else. My issues, my worries, my pains weren’t worthy of being spoken about because it would bring people down. “Then of course you find yourself in a pit or in a mess.” Florence previously defended Zach after turning off comments on her social media to protect him from criticism View this post on Instagram A post shared by Florence Pugh (@florencepugh) Comment by Ben Mapp discussing adults and privacy, relating to Florence Pugh age gap with ex Zach Braff controversy. ADVERTISEMENT In the 2019 horror film, Florence plays a woman who travels to Sweden and becomes entangled with a violent cult. Florence Pugh and Zach Braff at a movie premiere, addressing the age gap and public reactions between them. Image credits: Tristan Fewings/WireImage She revealed that the role had adverse effects on her and that she suffered from mental illness for months afterward. “I’d ab*sed myself and really manipulated my own emotions to get a performance. I just can’t exhaust myself like that because it has a knock-on effect.” ADVERTISEMENT Image credits: Louis Theroux The Oppenheimer actress told the podcast host that she’s now in a “very good” relationship and focusing on her mental health. By Josh Weiss Nov 20, 2025, 11:01 AM ET HOLLYWOOD, CALIFORNIA - APRIL 26: Bob Gale speaks onstage at the screening for "Back to the Future" during the 2025 TCM Classic Film Festival at TCL Chinese Theatre on April 26, 2025 in Hollywood, California. Photo: Courtesy of Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for TCM & Universal Pictures You'd be hard-pressed to find a more universally beloved movie than 1985's Back to the Future . Even Quentin Tarantino recently named it as one of his seven perfect films in all of existence. Like Casablanca or E.T. , the time travel classic boasts an untouchable cinematic pedigree. In other words, Back to the Future does not—nor will it ever—require a remake or reboot, and Hollywood would be utterly insane to try . Leave it alone for the love of all that is good and holy. With that said, if franchise co-creator Bob Gale could go back in time and do it all over again, he would make two notable changes to the original he wrote alongside director Robert Zemeckis. Why, you may ask? To help it jive a little better with the two sequels. "People always say, 'You guys must have been sure that you were gonna do a sequel because of the end of the movie,'" Gale previously told SYFY WIRE . "And we said, 'No, that's not true. That's a satisfying ending, whether there's another movie or not.'" For More on Back to the Future: Doc Brown Was Almost Very Different in Back to the Future Back to the Future Fan Theory: Did Marty Invent Pop Music? Is There Going to Be a Back to the Future 4? Back to the Future creator would make these two changes to the 1985 original But had they known Part II was a sure thing, "we would have never have Jennifer get in the car," he admitted. "Because when it came time for us to figure out what we were gonna do, we [asked], 'What the f---k are we gonna do with Jennifer?'" You can tell they had a difficult time finding a meaningful role for character because Jennifer (Claudia Wells in the first, Elisabeth Shue in the sequel) becomes something of an afterthought once Marty (Michael J. Fox) and Doc Brown (Christopher Lloyd) arrive in 2015. By the time—no pun intended—our protagonists realize they need to go back to 1955 to prevent Biff (Thomas F. Wilson) from getting the sports almanac, the plot simply calls for Jennifer to be left in the dystopian 1985. The second tweak Gale would make, if given the chance, is a proper setup for Marty's inability to walk away from a fight whenever someone accuses him of cowardice. "The first movie's central character arc is [centered around] George McFly," he explained. "It's not Marty. Marty is basically the same guy at the end of the movie as he is at the beginning—he just has a better understanding of who his parents are. But he's the same guy. Well, we figured we needed to do something more to give Marty some sort of a character arc. We didn't really create a significant character flaw that he has to get over." Looking back, they realized he was, as Gale put it, "a hot head." "He's always getting into these confrontations with Biff and kind of acting like a little dog who thinks he's a big dog," he shared. "Let's use that as the basis of what his character flaw is. So, if we were gonna go back in time and revise the first movie in those two scenes where Marty faces off [with] Biff, we would've had Biff call him a chicken and had Marty get pissed off about that." Back to the Future actor Christopher Lloyd had been announced as one of the stars that fans would be able to meet and have their picture taken with. ‌ The 86-year-old is best known for playing the iconic role as Dr Emmett 'Doc' Brown in the Back to the Future trilogy. He is also highly recognised for his performances as Reverend Jim Ignatowski in the sitcom Taxi, Uncle Fester in The Addams Family films, and Judge Doom in Who Framed Roger Rabbit . ‌ However, Comic Con Liverpool have now confirmed Christopher will not be attending the fan convention this weekend due to health reasons. A statement shared to social media by Comic Con organisers last night, said: "Unfortunately we have some very disappointing news. You may have been aware that Christopher Lloyd had a small health concern after arriving in Italy last week. Due to this he was unable to attend the convention in that country he had been booked in for on Nov 8/9. ‌ "We have been in regular contact with his team, and whilst every party wanted to make this appearance happen he has now been advised by his Dr that he should not travel from Italy to the UK for our show."
