Related Articles Special Features 4 Times Couture Fashion Designers Took Their Talents to the Stage Halston, Christian Dior, Pierre Cardin, and Isaac Mizrahi all started in the fashion industry but took a turn at Broadway costume design. By Talaura Harms June 01, 2021 Halston, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Liza Minnelli and Gower Champion Bob Deutsch Ryan Murphy’s Netflix series Halston culminates [spoiler alert] with the fashion designer creating the costumes for Martha Graham’s 1987 dance work Persephone at City Center. Halston had previously sold his brand to Esmark, Inc., and in doing so, was prevented from releasing any designs branded as a Halston. Earlier in the series, the character of Halston sneers at the world of theatrical costuming—both with his colleague Joe Eula’s costume design for Got Tu Go Disco and when meeting John David Ridge, the costumer turned fashion designer who would eventually replace Halston as the head of the brand bearing his name. However, this Episode Five collaboration with Graham (played by Mary Beth Peil) wasn’t his first foray into the field. Not only had Halston had a years-long friendship and working relationship with Graham, his deep friendship with Liza Minnelli ( Krysta Rodriguez in the series ) led to his sole Broadway credit as costume designer for the 1977 John Kander, Fred Ebb, and George Furth musical The Act , starring Minnelli decked out in Halston sequined jumpsuits. (Fun fact: The Act also happens to be director Martin Scorcese’s single Broadway credit.) Click through the gallery below for a look back at Halston's designs. Read on for a few other times couture designers turned their spindles toward Broadway for costume design. And not just for Josephine Baker’s gowns (looking at you, Balenciaga). Pierre Cardin Paris couturier Pierre Cardin once designed suits for The Beatles, and was well-known for his avant-garde flair and Space Age fashion. He favored geometric shapes and created the “bubble dress.” But in 1963, Cardin was credited for the execution of the ladies’ costumes for the period romance The Lady of Camellias , adapted by Terrance McNally from Alexandre Dumas’ La Dame aux Camélias (also the source material for Verdi’s La Traviata ). The production was directed by famous film director Franco Zeffirelli and starred Susan Strasberg as Camille. Despite three Tony nominations, including one for Marcel Escoffier’s costume design, it only ran for 13 performances. Susan Strasberg in The Lady of the Camellias Friedman-Abeles/©NYPL for the Performing Arts Christian Dior Just after WWII, Christian Dior founded his own Paris design house and created what became known as the “New Look.” His designs were more voluminous than women had worn during the fabric-rationing war years—incorporating wasp-waist corsets, with hip padding and petticoats under fuller longer skirts. In 1960 he is credited for the Women’s Costume Designs for the Broadway adaptation of Giraudoux’s Duel of Angels , starring Vivien Leigh. The play is set in southern France in 1868, but Dior infuses the gown designs with his own “New Look” adding pleats and volume to the period pieces. Isaac Mizrahi American designer Isaac Mizrahi attended the High School of Performing Arts before going on to Parsons School of Design, so it’s no stretch for him to step into the theatre world for costume design. He launched his first couture collection in 1987 and had a multi-million dollar diffusion line at Target in the early 2000s. His first Broadway costume design was for the 2001 revival of Clare Booth Luce’s 1936 comedy of manners The Women, winning a Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Costume Design . He added two additional Broadway credits in 2006 with designs for both Barefoot in the Park and The Threepenny Opera. Amy Ryan, Jennifer Coolidge, Lisa Emery, Cynthia Nixon and Lynn Collins in Broadway's The Women , 2001 Joan Marcus It’s Reversible Special mentions must go to two costume designers who also made names for themselves in the fashion industry: Bob Mackie and Emilio Sosa . Bob Mackie Mackie’s career began as a sketch artist for the costumers at Paramount Studios, but he quickly moved to designer. His work in the film industry led to an invitation in 1966 from Mitzi Gaynor to design her costumes for upcoming Las Vegas cabarets and television specials, which in turn led to his hire by The Carol Burnett Show. Mackie remained costumer designer for all eleven seasons of the series, creating everything from the sequined gowns Burnett wore in the show closings to the Scarlet O'Hara parody curtain(rod) gown. His first costume for Cher was her appearance on The Carol Burnett Show; he would go on to costume her for The Sonny and Cher Show. Mackie's first Broadway design was for the 1971 revival of On the Town, followed by Carol Channing's costumes for Lorelei. After years of dressing celebrities on stage and for the red carpet (especially Cher), he released a ready-to-wear collection in 1982. Mackie won his first Tony in 2019 for, of course, The Cher Show. Emilio Sosa Raised in New York City, Sosa attended Art and Design High School before studying Fashion Design at Pratt Institute. He made his Broadway debut in 2002 with the costume design for Topdog/Underdog. Sosa has a string of theatrical credits, including four additional Broadway shows (with a Tony nomination for The Gershwin's Porgy and Bess ), The Alvin Ailey Dance Company, and The Rockettes. In 2010, Sosa was a contestant on the fashion design competition series Project Runway , finishing as runner-up and creating what would become his own label, esosa. He returned for the second season of Project Runway All Stars, again winning runner-up honors. Sosa hasn't left the theatre industry though. Liev Schreiber - Instagram account Liev Schreiber, the 58-year-old actor known for "Ray Donovan," was admitted to a New York City hospital on Sunday after experiencing a sudden, severe headache. Medical personnel conducted extensive testing throughout the day, though no definitive diagnosis has been confirmed. Schreiber contacted his physician when the intense pain began, and was immediately advised to seek hospital care. He spent the night under observation while doctors performed numerous tests to determine the underlying cause of his condition. Despite the medical emergency, his representatives confirmed that he maintains full physical capabilities, including the ability to walk, speak, and use all limbs normally. His representative told media outlets that "out of an abundance of caution, Liev went into the hospital for testing and as of this afternoon, he has been cleared to return to work." The statement indicates the actor's condition did not present immediate neurological complications, though further evaluation remains ongoing. Read more: Catherine Castro Hospitalized for Mysterious Illness: Former Televisa Star and Nuestra Belleza Latina Says Doctors Can't Find a Diagnosis The hospitalization marks a second significant health episode for Schreiber involving headaches. During his run in the Broadway production of "Doubt: A Parable" last year, the acclaimed performer experienced transient global amnesia, a temporary but complete memory loss condition triggered by a severe migraine. During that incident, he found himself unable to recall his scene partner Amy Ryan's name backstage and lost all memory of the play itself once onstage. Following that episode, multiple medical tests, including an MRI, revealed no brain abnormalities or bleeding. Schreiber's career spans decades, with notable roles in film and television. The Tony Award-winning actor is perhaps best known for his lead role in Showtime's crime drama "Ray Donovan," which ran for seven seasons and earned him three Emmy nominations. He has also appeared in the "Scream" franchise, the Oscar-winning film "Spotlight," and recent projects including Netflix's "The Perfect Couple" and the crime thriller "Caught Stealing." The actor maintains a full professional schedule , recently voicing the character Sam Fisher in the adult animated series "Splinter Cell: Deathwatch." He has been recognized throughout his career with numerous accolades, including a Tony Award, a Golden Globe, and 9 Emmy nominations. Schreiber's family includes two adult children, Sasha and Kai, whom he shares with actress Naomi Watts, as well as a daughter, Hazel Bee, born in August 2023, with his wife, Taylor Neisen. The family resides in New York. Divorce Comedy by Alex Billington November 18, 2025 Source: YouTube "Man, I wish I had a punch line!" 🎤 Searchlight Pictures has revealed the main official trailer for Is This Thing On? , the latest film directed by actor turned filmmaker Bradley Cooper , following A Star is Born and Maestro before. This first premiered at the 2025 New York Film Festival as their big Closing Night gala ( view the teaser from then ), with a full theatrical release set for December coming up. If anyone wants to watch. As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex faces middle age and a divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene; while his soon-the-be-ex-wife Tess confronts the sacrifices she made for the family—forcing them both to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take on a new form. Cooper's beautifully lived-in third feature is both lacerating and sweet-souled, funny, and tender. Inspired by the true story of British comedian John Bishop . The very dry comedy stars Will Arnett as Alex and Laura Dern as Tess, with Andra Day , Bradley Cooper , Amy Sedaris , Sean Hayes , Christine Ebersole , Ciarán Hinds , and Scott Icenogle . Reviews were mixed-to-good at the fests, saying the film is a "warm, essential reminder that it's never too late to grab the microphone and start telling our own story." It's worth a watch. Here's the official trailer (+ 3 new posters) for Bradley Cooper's film Is This Thing On? , from YouTube : You can rewatch the teaser trailer for Bradley Cooper's Is This Thing On? film right here for the first look. Intro via NYFF : In a pair of galvanizing, deeply honest performances, Will Arnett & Laura Dern play Alex & Tess Novak, whose marriage has reached an impasse. With amicable sorrow, the couple—parents of two young boys—mutually agree to split up. Yet in Cooper's keenly observed comic drama, their separation leads to unpredictable midlife self-reckonings, most dramatically in Alex's wild career pivot to become a confessional stand-up comedian in NYC's West Village, where he finds new direction & camaraderie. This seemingly outlandish scenario—in a script by Cooper, Arnett, and Mark Chappell inspired by the true story of British comedian John Bishop —is never played for easy laughs, while Cooper uses his penchant for naturalism to give the actors space to find their complicated centers. Is This Thing On? is directed by American actor / producer / filmmaker Bradley Cooper , director of the films A Star Is Born and Maestro previously; he also produced War Dogs , A Star Is Born , Joker , Nightmare Alley . The screenplay is written by Bradley Cooper, Will Arnett, and Mark Chappell. Produced by Weston Middleton, Kris Thykier, Cooper, Arnett. This is premiering at the 2025 New York Film Festival this fall. Searchlight Pictures opens Cooper's Is This Thing On? film in select US theaters starting on December 19th, 2025 coming soon. (Credit: Getty Images) “One Piece” has cast one of its antagonists for Season 3. Bon Clay will be played by Cole Escola , TheWrap has learned. Escola is perhaps best known for creating and starring in the Broadway show “Oh, Mary!” which won two Tony Awards earlier this year. They’ve also appeared in “Search Party” as well as “At Home with Amy Sedaris,” “Difficult People” and “Big Mouth.” In addition to winning a Tony for Best Performance by a Leading Actor in a Play, Escola was also a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize for Drama earlier this year. It’s pretty great casting. In the anime and manga, Bon Clay, also known as Bentham of the Wild, is defined by their love of wild looks and an eccentric, borderline manic fighting style. And no one in Hollywood captures oddly charismatic mania better than Escola. “A master of performance and precision, Bon Clay is as dangerous as they are dazzling — a theatrical assassin who turns combat into art,” a press release from Netflix reads. In the original story of “One Piece,” Bon Clay was a member of Miss Goldenweek’s Baroque Works as well as a major antagonist of the Straw Hats during the Arabasta Arc. But, as is often the case when it comes to Luffy, they eventually come to be one of his closest allies. Production for “One Piece” Season 3 will happen later this year in Cape Town, South Africa. More cast will be announced at a later date. Season 2, which is also known as “One Piece: Into the Grand Line,” will premiere on Netflix on March 10. The Hollywood Reporter film critic David Rooney writes of the comic drama in his New York Film Festival review: “In Cooper’s tenderly observed third feature, Is This Thing On? , performance is a rebound reflex, a therapeutic means of working through the end of a marriage and stumbling onto the self-discovery necessary to process what went wrong — inadvertently realizing that the foundations on which it was built remain intact. It’s an unassuming comic drama that sneaks up on you, its emotional honesty fueled by gorgeous performances of unimpeachable naturalness from Will Arnett and Laura Dern.” Is This Thing On? is Cooper’s directorial follow up to Maestro and his directorial debut with A Star Is Born . As with A Star Is Born and Maestro , Cooper is also part of the cast of his third film, the ensemble cast of which includes Andra Day, Christine Ebersole, Ciarán Hinds, Sean Hayes and Amy Sedaris. Watch : Amy Schumer Deletes Her Pre-Weight Loss Social Media Photos Amy Schumer is starting anew. As the Snatched actor continues to focus on her weight loss journey, she deleted all her social media photos and offered a new look at her body transformation. “I actually left my house tonight. Who’s proud?” Amy, 44, wrote on her Nov. 11 Instagram post , which sees her posed on her staircase. “I’m feeling good and happy. Deleted my old pics for no reason!” Indeed, the comedian—who shares son Gene Fischer , 6, with husband Chris Fischer —is embracing soft glam this season. In her new post, Amy wore a mini red Valentino dress and black heels, her hair styled in a straight side part. This isn’t the first time the I Feel Pretty alum has showed off her new figure. After all, she’s been open about her health journey since 2022. photos Amy Schumer's Personal Confessions to Howard Stern Before she gave her grid a fall makeover, Amy showed her progress in numerous photos last month, including baring her toned stomach in a since-deleted selfie. She also flexed her legs in a short, black Miu Miu dress during a girls’ trip to Vegas, and her friends complimented her new look. “I’m so pissed about your legs, I can barely talk to you,” Kathy Griffin joked in the comments section, while director Lee Daniels added, “Skinnnnnnnny mommmmma.” Amy Sedaris echoed the supportive sentiment, writing, “You look incredible. Look at those pins!!!” And Amy appreciated all the love, as she replied, “My legs thank you!” View this post on Instagram Though the Trainwreck star Amy is proud of her transformation, she’s also hit some roadblocks in achieving her weight loss goals. In fact, she shared her negative experience with taking Ozempic—a type 2 diabetes drug that can help people slim down due to its appetite-reducing properties—earlier this year. “I was like bedridden,” she explained during her appearance on The Howard Stern Show in January. “I was vomiting, and then you have no energy. But other people take it and they’re all good. So, God bless them.” Keep reading to see more celebrities who have debuted their weight loss journey on social media… TikTok / Trevor Larcom Trevor Larcom The Fresh Off the Boat alum used to weigh 300 pounds and lost 130, showcasing his journey on TikTok. TLC Tammy Slaton Tammy Slaton may be a star of TLC’s 1,000-Lb. Sisters , but she didn’t want to be beholden to that title forever. “ I’m down 500 pounds now , around 500,” the 38-year-old said in a confessional on an April 2025 episode of her show. “When I was at my heaviest, I was 700-plus pounds. Right now, I’m weighing in at 238.” She underwent bariatric surgery in 2022, a choice her physician has praised as the right one for her. “Tammy has consistently demonstrated her dedication to making sustainable lifestyle changes to maximize the benefits of her surgery,” Dr. Eric Smith told People in October 2024. “I've emphasized the importance of making small, daily adjustments to ensure not only her continued progress but also her long-term success. She's truly committed to her health journey.” Erika Goldring/Getty Images, Taylor Hill/FilmMagic Jelly Roll It seems as if every time Jelly Roll hits a red carpet, he’s down a sizable slice of weight . “I started at 540 pounds and I was 357 pounds this morning,” the singer born Jason DeFord told Pat McAfee in April 2025 during the ESPN host's Big Night Aht live show . “I’m gonna lose another 100 pounds and go skydiving with my wife in Sweden, baby!" The 6-foot-1 artist admittedly needed to overhaul his relationship with food to get where he wanted to go. "I've always said that I believe obesity is directly connected to mental health," he explained on an October 2024 episode of On Purpose With Jay Shetty . "I know how easy it is for people to go, 'Just quit eatin' so much, just work out, it's so easy!' I wish I looked at food that way.” Weight was still “the mountain” in front of him, Jelly Roll noted, but his lifestyle changes were working. "I'm learning, I'm being very diligent with it,” he said. “I'm taking it serious, I'm drinking a bunch of water, I'm cold plunging, I'm eating right, I'm doing good." Nick Elgar/Getty Images, Jason Davis/Getty Images for Bentonville Film Festival Al Roker Al Roker wasn’t kidding around with the title of his cookbook Recipes to Live By . Because having lost a hard-fought 100 pounds , the longtime TODAY weatherman literally walks the walk (aiming for at least 10,000 steps a day), watching what he eats and fitting in some sort of exercise on a daily basis. “My mantra is ‘something is better than nothing,’” he told People in a June 2025 interview. “Maybe you’ll be running marathons or entering weight-lifting contests, but I think most people just want a level of fitness that improves their quality of life.” Roker underwent gastric bypass surgery in 2002 to get his fitness journey underway, but, he acknowledged, “There’s no magic bullet.” Surgery is “not the end,” he advised. “You’re still going to have to put in the work.” Mitchell Leff/Getty Images, Christopher Polk/Variety via Getty Images Jason Kelce While previously known for the tush push, former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce has been busy showing off his buff bod . Not that the athlete wasn’t in fighting shape during his 13-year career in the NFL, but he’s down at least 25 pounds from his playing weight of 295, sharing during the 2025 Truist Championship pro-am golf tournament in Philly that he weighed around 270. All of which is part of his retirement plan. “I feel like for some reason, 250 to 260 feels like I'll be still big and be happy with the way I look without having a six-pack,” Kelce told GQ in June 2024. “But I’ll still be able to have that stature a little bit.” Really, the most important aspect for the father of four daughters with wife Kylie Kelce was to be able to keep pace with his kids. Then weighing in at 277, “my back already feels better,” he shared. “My knees already feel better. So another 20 pounds hopefully will make that much more adept at playing with my children.” Bruce Glikas/Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic, Chelsea Guglielmino/Getty Images Rosie O'Donnell It wasn’t just a change of scenery that did the trick for Rosie O’Donnell , who relocated with her family from the U.S. to Ireland. " I've lost more weight here ,” she shared in a March 2025 TikTok. “I am on Mounjaro for my diabetes and one of the side effects is you lose weight.” The former View cohost had recently gone shopping for better-fitting clothes in Dublin. “I’m one of those people,” she said, “who's always had a weight issue and now that I'm a size large, instead of an XL or a 2XL, I find it shocking.” JC Olivera/Getty Images, Jazz Jennings/Instagram Jazz Jennings Jazz Jennings embarked on a diet-and-fitness journey in 2022, explaining on Instagram two years later, “I finally care about myself after years of neglecting my health. I had truly let myself go when it came to eating. I am so proud of my weight loss, and I feel my confidence radiates through." In August 2024, the I Am Jazz star shared that she had lost almost 100 pounds and was “so proud” of her progress. Phillip Faraone/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images, Charley Gallay/Getty Images for Netflix Christopher Schwarzenegger It turns out Christopher Schwarzenegger is a chip off the ol’ muscly block. The youngest of Arnold Schwarzenegger and ex-wife Maria Shriver ’s four kids together laid low while he dropped 30 pounds , but now he’s back in action. “It’s not an overnight thing, but it took a lot of trial and error,” he shared in May 2025 at the Inaugural Beacher Vitality Happy & Healthy Summit, noting that just giving up bread made a big difference. “And even still to this day, when [I look at] before and after photos, I don’t feel like I’m an ‘after’ yet.” Meanwhile, Christopher did not let a certain seven-time Mr. Olympia in on his plan. “I could never go and say to him, 'You’re overweight,'” dad Arnold told The Times in June 2025 . "We just kept introducing healthy foods. We introduced him always to the gym and all of that kind of stuff. And then, out of nowhere, he decided that he wanted to be lean. And now he is. So that is of course fantastic, the self-discipline and the self-motivation. I always felt one day it will have to come from him—and it did.” Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images, Leah Puttkammer/FilmMagic Chrissy Metz Chrissy Metz doesn’t like to run “unless I’m being chased,” she quipped, but she’s a big fan of strength training—and working out is part of the regimen that resulted in her losing 100 pounds. “I want to age the best way that I can, and I want to be strong,” the This Is Us alum told DailyMail.com in April 2025. “And that’s really the impetus behind any of it.” To Metz, aging gracefully means “staying strong and flexible,” so she tries to be active every day. ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content, Christopher Willard via Getty Images John Goodman Being a big teddy bear of a guy was part of the package when John Goodman starred on Roseanne in the 1990s, at one point “pushing 400” pounds, as he told David Letterman in 2010 . By the time The Conners premiered in 2018, however, family patriarch Dan Conner had made a few lifestyle adjustments. Goodman quit drinking in 2007 , the first step on his road to getting in better shape, while his favorite activities included boxing and walking his dogs. “I’m breaking a sweat but I’m not going nuts,” he told People in 2010, sharing he had lost about 100 pounds working out six days a week and cutting sugar out of his diet. Overall, the 6-foot-2 actor has lost about 200 pounds since he was at his peak weight. “I just got tired, sick and tired of looking at myself,” Goodman told ABC News in 2016 . “You’re shaving in the mirror and you don’t want to look at yourself. It gets dangerous.” Ron Galella Collection for Getty Images, Theo Wargo/Getty Images for Tony Awards Productions Oprah Winfrey Oprah Winfrey has been sharing the highs and lows of her weight loss journey for decades. From donning skinny jeans and rolling out a wagon loaded with 67 pounds of fat to wow her Oprah Winfrey Show audience in 1988, to buying a stake in WeightWatchers in 2015 , she has used her platform to keep the conversation going. And taking on the topic du jour, she revealed in March 2024 on An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame and the Weight Loss Revolution that, along with eating smaller portions and staying active, she was taking medication to help regulate her weight. "It's not just one thing,” she said of her secret to staying fit, “it's multiple things.” Her goal with the special, Winfrey explained, was to “start releasing the stigma and the shame and the judgment—to stop shaming other people for being overweight or how they choose to lose or not lose weight—and more importantly to stop shaming ourselves." Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images for BET, Udo Salters/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images Lizzo Lizzo simply wanted to feel better from head to toe. “Once I started working out for mental health, to have balanced mental health or endorphins, so that I don't look at myself in the mirror and feel ashamed of myself, and feel disgusted with myself,” the “Good as Hell” singer explained in a May 2023 TikTok , “exercise has helped me shift my mind, not my body.” She acknowledged in a January 2025 TikTok that she was on an “intentional weight loss journey,” her goal was simply to be the best version of herself. “Even at the end of my weight loss journey, I'm not going to be considered thin by any means,” Lizzo said. “I will still be considered morbidly obese on the BMI and little bros on the internet are still going to call me 'big backed.' But I will be happy." A second later, the video jumped to Lizzo exclaiming, “And I am happy,” as she showed off a screen showing her body fat had gone down by 16 percent and she’d shaved 10.5 points from her Body Mass Index (BMI). “Let this be a reminder that you can do anything— anything —you set your mind to,” she added. “Now I guess it’s time to set new goals.” For the latest breaking news updates, click here to download the E! Cole Escola Writing Miss Piggy Movie from Emma Stone, Jennifer Lawrence - Nerdist Main Navigation Open menu READ WATCH PLAY LISTEN SHOP PITCH ADVERTISE Open search Open search Search for: Search Close search Topics Newsletter Dark Mode Movies Cole Escola Writing Miss Piggy Movie Produced by Emma Stone and Jennifer Lawrence by Michael Walsh Nov 5 2025 • 11:30 AM “ Oh, Mary! ‘s Cole Escola is writing a Miss Piggy featured film” is the kind of sentence that sounds too good to be true. But not only is that a real thing that is actually happening, it’s somehow even better than that. Oscar winners Emma Stone and Jennifer Lawrence are both producing and plan to appear in the movie. CBS Jennifer Lawrence announced Cole Escola, who just joined the cast of One Piece , is penning a movie centered on The Muppets ‘ fashion icon. Lawrence revealed this perfect pairing of writer and subject matter during an appearance on the Las Culturistas podcast hosted by Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers . (A visit we first learned about at Deadline .) “I don’t know if I can announce this,” said Lawrence, “But I’m just going to. Emma Stone and I are producing a Miss Piggy movie and Cole is writing it.” Both will almost certainly appear in the film, too. When asked about that possibility, Lawrence said, “I think so. We have to.” Yes. You do, Jennifer Lawrence. You really do. The Muppets While there’s no official word from either Disney or The Jim Henson Company about the film’s development, and Lawrence didn’t share any plot details, this announcement guarantees fans will do everything they can to make sure it happens. It has to. Despite being one of the most vocal divas in history, Miss Piggy has never starred in her own film. And Escola—who wrote and won a Tony for starring in their Broadway smash comedy Oh, Mary! —is an absolutely perfect choice to capture Miss Piggy’s voice. Their other notable credits include At Home With Amy Sedaris , Tuca & Bertie , and Difficult People . If anyone can make The Muppets ‘ diva shine, Escola can. Writing a movie, even one produced by two big-time stars like Emma Stone and Jennifer Lawrence, is still a long way off from actually getting that movie to theaters. But we think this film has a real shot at actually happening even beyond Escola’s talents. What executive would be brave enough to tell Miss Piggy no? When she was asked if she and Stone would be starring in the movie together, she said " I think so… We have to. " No further details about the project have been revealed at the time of writing. Miss Piggy hugging Kermit Cole Escola has so far not written any screenplays for movies that have been officially released, but the Tony Award winner has had their fair share of writing credits on the small screen . Escola has penned episodes for a variety of television series, including The Other Two , At Home with Amy Sedaris , and Ziwe . Their irreverent humor and ability to craft compelling narratives around iconic female figures could very well be a good fit for a story centering on Miss Piggy, who is one of the most iconic characters from the long-running Muppets franchise . Miss Piggy, a pig who is a glamorous diva and is romantically obsessed with Kermit the Frog, first appeared on the 1974 special Herb Alpert and the TJB before being developed into a bigger character on The Muppet Show . Since then, she has appeared in a wide variety of Muppets projects and has become one of the puppets franchise's most well-known characters , alongside Kermit, Fozzie Bear, Gonzo, and Animal. It is unknown what roles Lawrence and Stone might play opposite Miss Piggy, but Muppet movies typically feature several human figures starring alongside the iconic puppets , as well as a robust roster of celebrity cameos. In fact, the most recent Muppet movie, 2014's Muppets Most Wanted , featured a wide variety of well-known human performers , including Tina Fey, Ricky Gervais, Ty Burrell, Lady Gaga, James McAvoy, Chloë Grace Moretz, Ray Liotta, Tom Hiddleston, Stanley Tucci, Danny Trejo, Saoirse Ronan, Salma Hayek, Christoph Waltz, Ross Lynch, and Josh Groban. Given the history of the franchise, it stands to reason that both Jennifer Lawrence and Emma Stone could appear in the movie. Even if their busy schedules lead to them only being able to make brief cameos, that approach would fit in with previous appearances from Muppets celebrity guests and allow them to finally have their first official movie together. Published Sat, 08 Nov 2025 07:17:03 -0600 by Aedan Juvet | Comments Article Summary Jennifer's Body director Karyn Kusama confirms Diablo Cody is working on a sequel script right now The 2009 cult horror film gained a passionate following after an underwhelming box office debut Kusama promises the sequel will be as fun and wild as the original, staying true to its unique tone Fans and creators believe Jennifer's Body is finally getting the recognition it deserves in horror Sixteen years after release, Jennifer's Body keeps gaining ground. The 2009 teen horror from writer Diablo Cody and director Karyn Kusama follows Jennifer Check, a popular small-town cheerleader who becomes demonically possessed after a botched rock-band ritual, then begins feeding on male classmates. Her best friend Anita "Needy" Lesnicki pieces together the truth and fights to stop the killings, becoming a showdown that reframes high-school power dynamics through a sharp, darkly comic lens. The cast did a lot of the heavy lifting. Megan Fox leads as Jennifer, and Amanda Seyfried co-stars as Needy, with Adam Brody as frontman Nikolai, Johnny Simmons as Chip, J. K. Simmons as Mr. Wroblewski, and Amy Sedaris in support. The film premiered in 2009 after Cody's teen breakout hit Juno and quickly became a conversation piece about gender roles and media consumption, even as some viewers and critics missed what it was doing at the time. On paper, the numbers looked pretty underwhelming. Jennifer's Body cost about $16 million and grossed roughly $32 million worldwide in theaters, becoming a modest return that fueled the "flop" label before home release success and the cult following really kicked in. Yet the reassessment has been steady and loud. Many fans have argued the movie was mismarketed ahead of its release, and that its blend of friendship drama, anger, and satire reads much clearer now. "I know she's working on it right now, and I'm very excited to hear what comes of it. I know some of the bones of it, so I'm not going to give anything away, but it sounds fun and crazy like the first film. And I have no doubt that Diablo will do something absolutely incredible with it." At this point, it's obvious that Jennifer's Body has outlasted its first-weekend narrative. It found its audience, influenced a wave of feminist-leaning horror, and became a touchstone for teen terror (with teeth). We’ve officially known since August that One Piece Season 3 is on the way, although we’d known of its existence way before then thanks to Roronoa Zoro actor Mackenyu . Now the first Season 3 casting has been revealed, and I really like who’s been chosen to play Bon Clay, a.k.a. Mr. 2. Tony-winning actor Cole Escola has been tapped to play the high-ranking Baroque Works member ahead of One Piece heading back to Cape Town, South Africa to resume production later this year. Like the manga/anime counterpart, Escola’s Mr. 2 is described by Deadline as a “master of performance and precision, and “as dangerous as they are dazzling — a theatrical assassin who turns combat into art.” Like Escola, the Mr. 2 in Netflix’s One Piece is “envisioned as non-binary.” (Image credit: HBO Max) In addition to starring in TV shows like Difficult People , Mozart in the Jungle , At Home with Amy Sedaris and The Girls on the Bus , Cole Escola is best known for writing and starring in Oh Mary! , which is a spoof about Mary Todd Lincoln’s relationship with President Abraham Lincoln in the days leading up to his assassination. Oh Mary! has been met with numerous accolades since premiering on Broadway last year, including Escola winning the Tony Award for Best Performance by a Leading Actor in a Play, and the production as a whole being a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize for Drama. I’ll admit that I’m disappointed that Mr. 2 won’t appear in One Piece Season 2, but I’m also glad their introduction has merely been delayed rather than them being left out of the show entirely. Among the other new characters we’ll meet in Season 2 include David Dastmalchian as Mr. 3 , Callum Kerr as Smoker, Katey Sagal as Dr. Kureha, Charithra Chandran as Miss Wednesday , and Mikaela Hoover voicing Tony Tony Chopper . 'Jennifer's Body' is a 2009 comedy horror film directed by Karyn Kusama and written by Diablo Cody. Starring Megan Fox, Amanda Seyfried, Johnny Simmons, J K Simmons, Amy Sedaris, and Adam Brody, the film follows Jennifer Check (Fox), a demonically possessed high school student who kills her male classmates and devours their flesh to survive. While discussing preparing for the role, Fox recalled two scenes, including one that made her cry after it "unlocked" unexpected emotions, according to the outlet. Playing Jennifer in the film opposite Amanda Seyfried as her best friend "wasn't super physical for me," the actress said, "but it did stretch me." "There were some moments that required a lot of vulnerability that I don't think I went into it prepared to show," Fox said, "because it's so revealing about possibly my own past, my own childhood, whatever, those moments where something comes through -- whether it's when I'm in the mirror putting on the makeup, trying to cover up my skin because I'm not beautiful anymore." Apart from the mirror scene, there was one moment in particular that demanded a lot from Fox, "It was a really upsetting day," director Kusama, who was also at the L A screening, said of the day they filmed the disturbing scene, led by Fox and Adam Brody. "There was something about maybe from a past life, I don't know, something about having a circle of men standing around me, and when they would start chanting the song taunting me before they were going to kill me, that triggered something so deep in me where I was just, like, I was weeping," Fox recalled, according to People. "It unlocked things that I wasn't prepared for," she added. "It was like an ayahuasca trip, to be honest. I didn't know it was going to unlock those things, but it brought things to the surface...." During the screening of 'Jennifer's Body', Fox also recalled how "lost" and angry she felt while working on the supernatural horror-comedy. "I think where I was at that point in my life, so lost, so full of that rage that I had towards how I had been treated in the industry," Fox said, "and how I was dealing with fame ... at that time, before we started filming." "I just left a premiere for something where I had to go, I'm obligated to go, and I remember the paparazzi were so ruthless back then, the way they would talk to women," she said, as quoted by the outlet. "And I walked out just to try to get to my car, and they're all shooting," Fox recalled. "And one guy's like, 'Megan, why are you such a bitch?' And another guy is like, 'Megan, do you think you're overrated? The internet says so,' and I'm just trying to do my job." "I was asked to be at this premiere. I'm trying to get to my car," Fox continued. "And so I had all of this grief and sorrow and also anger and rage that needed a place to go," reported People. 'Jennifer's Body' is currently streaming on Hulu and Tubi. Brining, baking and brand buzz By Deniz Ataman 25-Nov-2025 Last updated on 25-Nov-2025 at 14:55 GMT Thanksgiving 2025 trends show consumers embracing scratch-made comfort foods, premium upgrades and nostalgic brands, while retailers and brands compete on value. (Image: Tyler Darden) From budget-friendly feasts to playful twists, brands are blending affordability, nostalgia and creativity to win over holiday hosts This Thanksgiving, consumers are leaning into scratch-made comfort foods, premium upgrades and playful twists – while brands respond with value-driven deals and nostalgic favorites. Consumers are planning to cook and eat at home more this year compared to last year, according to recent data from Kroger’s 84.51 Precision Marketing’s consumer digest. On Thanksgiving, 82% of shoppers plan to share a sit-down meal with others and 66% plan to cook and bake at home. Consumers’ menu will revolve around scratch-made dishes like main courses, savory sides and fresh sides, while snacks and appetizers, desserts and breakfast will be made with mixes. Pre-made items like dinner breads and candy are expected to be present as well, according to 84.51. With Thanksgiving recipe searches up 32.9% year over year across Google, TikTok and Instagram, consumers are looking for staples and elevated ingredients to incorporate into their at-home menus, according to Spate search data from Oct. 2024 to Sept. 2025 vs. Oct. 2023 to Sept. 2024. Comfort, quality and nostalgia are driving holiday search behavior Searches for holiday staples are surging, like green beans, brine, turkey brine, egg and Gournay cheese all jumped more than tenfold year over year, signaling prep for casseroles, turkey brining, baking and cheese boards. Searches for cheese climbed +235% YoY to 63.0K searches, chicken rose +178.9% to 29.7K (a 19.0K increase YoY), and pantry staples like potato (110.2K, +24.2K) and sweet potato (83.1K, +28.5K) continue to anchor meal planning, per Spate. Searches for nostalgic and premium brands are also spiking. Velveeta tops the list with >1,000% YoY growth and 422.4K searches (+420.9K), followed by Boursin (255.8K; +249.8K) and Kerrygold (158.0K; +158.0K). Pantry staples like Campbell’s (+634%; 223.6K) and Kraft (+418%; 183.3K) are trending, while sweet treats and baking essentials – Lotus Biscoff and King Arthur Baking – also jumped more than tenfold, per Spate. International twists on traditional Thanksgiving dishes, like pumpkin tamales, butternut squash risotto, green-chile and jalapeno cornbread, key lime cranberry relish and oyster stuffing also are on the rise, according to Tastewise data . Lidl announced earlier this month that its Thanksgiving offerings can feed 10 people for less than $36, which they claim is “nearly $10 cheaper than last year’s feast.” (Image: Lidl) Brands double down on affordability and accessibility for holiday hosts Companies are tapping into consumers’ acute focus on value while delivering core staples that deliver classic comfort foods. Lidl announced earlier this month that its Thanksgiving offerings can feed 10 people for less than $36, which they claim is “nearly $10 cheaper than last year’s feast.” The retailer offers its Thanksgiving staples like pie crusts, brown gravy mix, canned pumpkin, boxed macaroni and cheese and a whole turkey for $0.25 per pound for shoppers using the MyLidl app. Frozen food brand Amy's Kitchen partnered with Instacart and actress and comedian Amy Sedaris to offer one free frozen meal while supplies last. (Image: Amy's Kitchen) On a similar vein of offering accessible products to consumers, frozen food brand Amy’s Kitchen and Instacart partnered to “give every ‘Amy’ in America a night off from dinner duty” by offering a free Amy’s meal on Instacart using a promo code while supplies last through Nov. 26. To promote the offer, Amy’s Kitchen launched a marketing campaign on social media featuring actress and comedian Amy Sedaris . JELL-O launched its “No Thanks” Thanksgiving molds in shapes resembling brussels sprouts, cranberry sauce and pecan pie to reimagine “playful, jiggly creations that are as fun to look at as they are to eat.” JELL-O launched its “No Thanks” Thanksgiving molds in shapes resembling brussels sprouts, cranberry sauce and pecan pie to reimagine “playful, jiggly creations that are as fun to look at as they are to eat.” (Image: Jell-O) According to the brand’s social listening research, nearly one-third of consumers consider Brussels sprouts their least favorite Thanksgiving side, more than a quarter avoid cranberry sauce and one in five skip pecan pie. “Over 60% say they are more likely to try dishes that look fun and believe a holiday should feel playful, not stiff,” and adding JELL-O brings color and nostalgia back to the Thanksgiving table, according to the company. Blue Diamond's holiday-inspired mixed nut blends contain almonds, pistachios and cashews in three different seasonings: Smokehouse, Roasted Sea Salt and Honey Roasted (Image: Blue Diamond) In an effort to “bring the holidays earlier than ever,” Blue Diamond launched its Almonds and More mixed nut blend with a pop-up event on Halloween in Pasadena, Calif, according to Maya Erwin, VP of marketing and innovation for Blue Diamond. The brand is marketing Almonds and More as an accompaniment for consumers throughout the holiday season. Almonds and More is packaged in a festive container and features a blend of almond, cashew and pistachio in three seasonings: Smokehouse, Roasted Sea Salt and Honey Roasted. Her work has also appeared in publications such as Reactor, BookBub, Litro, PopMatters, BUST, and Bloody Women. She holds a Bachelor of Arts in Creative Writing and Cinema Studies from the State University of New York at Purchase and lives in New Jersey with a very small dog. Her debut novel, Midnight on Beacon Street, is an hommage to vintage horror movies. Her ghostly novella, Shiva, is due out from Dark Matter Ink in 2026. Sign in to your MovieWeb account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There is a reason so many horror movies are also coming-of-age stories. Puberty is a nightmare and while growing up is hard for everyone, there is something particularly monstrous in the shift from girlhood into womanhood . There is a lot that goes on biologically and socially during this time. The pressures placed on young girls by themselves, their peers, their parents, the media, and grown men who have no business weighing in at all certainly doesn't help. It's no wonder, then, that there are some pretty incredible horror movies highlighting the torments of girlhood. From the innocence of childhood to the chaos of one's teenage years, these movies explore the female experience with harrowing precision. They examine not only the horrors of girlhood, but also how different stressors, expectations, and influences contribute to those horrors. 10 'Carrie' (1976) United Artists Carrie is the first screen adaptation of Stephen King's classic 1974 debut novel. Sissy Spacek ( Coal Miner's Daughter ) stars as the quiet and sensitive Carrie White, a teenage girl who is ruthlessly bullied at her high school. The film was directed by Brian De Palma ( Scarface ) with a screenplay by Lawrence D. Cohen ( Ghost Story ). The cast features Amy Irving ( Crossing Delancey ), Nancy Allen ( The Philadelphia Experiment ), P. J. Soles ( Halloween ), William Katt ( Jawbreaker ), John Travolta ( Pulp Fiction ), Betty Buckley ( Tender Mercies ), and Piper Laurie ( The Hustler ) as Carrie's strict and fanatically religious mother, Margaret White. Public Humiliation Is De Palma the right director for this movie? Debatable. Is Sissy Spacek a phenomenal Carrie? Absolutely. Right from the beginning, the film jumps into the deep end of girlhood torment. Carrie gets her first period in the gym locker room at school. Since her mother has never explained menstruation to her, she thinks she is dying and panics. From there, Carrie develops telekinetic powers as the bullying intensifies and her mother's religious zeal reaches new heights. Carrie received two Academy Award nominations, Best Actress in a Lead Role for Sissy Spacek and Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Piper Laurie. Today, the movie is certified fresh with a 94% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. 9 'Poison for the Fairies' (1986) Flavia becomes Veronica's prey in Poison for Fairies Colección IMCINE Poison for the Fairies , also known as Veneno para las hadas , is a Mexican supernatural horror film written and directed by Carlos Enrique Taboada ( The Book of Stone ). The film earned 10 nominations at the Ariel Awards, winning in five categories, including Best Picture and Best Direction. Ana Patricia Rojo ( Fugitivas, en busca de la libertad ) won Best Child Performance at the Bogota Film Festival and the SIlver Goddess Award for Best Child Acting from the Mexican Cinema Journalist. The film has an 80% rating from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes. Bullying and Black Magic Veronica (Rojo) is a young girl who fantasizes about being a witch to cope with her loneliness at school. When her class gets a new student, Flavia (Elsa María Gutiérrez), Vernonica covets Flavia's wealth and stable home life. So what does Veronica do? She convinces Flavia that she is a witch and forces her to partake in increasingly dangerous games. Veronica delights in the new power she holds over Flavia through this facade, a complete flip from the lack of control she felt when the other students were making fun of her. 8 'The Craft' (1996) Assumpta Serna in The Craft Sony Pictures Releasing The Craft is directed by Andrew Fleming ( Bad Dreams ), who also wrote the screenplay with Peter Filardi ( Chapelwaite ). Robin Tunney ( The Mentalist ) stars as Sarah Bailey, a teenage girl with unique abilities who moves to a new home with her family in Los Angeles, California. At her new school, she befriends Nancy Downs, Bonnie Harper, and Rochelle Zimmerman — played by Fairuza Balk ( Almost Famous ), Neve Campbell ( Scream ), and Rachel True ( Nowhere ). Together, the four outcasts form a coven. They become powerful witches , but as they seek revenge on those who have wronged them at school, the consequences become more extreme than they could have anticipated. We're the Weirdos, Mister While the mainstream media didn't give The Craft much credit upon release, the film received five Fangoria Chainsaw Award nominations and two Saturn Award nominations. This movie is an absolute cult classic today, despite mediocre reviews back in the 1990s. The line "We Are the Weirdos, Mister" has become iconic, adapted by contemporary women in horror almost as both affirmation and battle cry. The way the film tackles bullying, racism, and sexual double standards continues to resonate with audiences. 7 'Ginger Snaps' (2000) Motion International Ginger Snaps is a Canadian cult classic werewolf movie directed by Orphan Black co-creator John Fawcett with a screenplay by Orphan Black writer Karen Walton. Emily Perkins ( Stephen King's It ) and Katharine Isabelle ( American Mary ) star as Brigitte and Ginger Fitzgerald, two teenage sisters who are obsessed with death and are determined to get out of their suburban town, whatever the cost. One night, Ginger is bitten by a creature that's been attacking local dogs. In the days that follow, Brigitte starts to notice that her sister is changing in ways she can't explain — ways that might just be dangerous. Shades of David Cronenberg When we talk about girlhood and horror, Ginger Snaps is always going to come up. The movie is on just about every college syllabus for women in horror classes and this list wouldn't be complete without it. The film did well upon release, with critics comparing it to the work of David Cronenberg and Buffy the Vampire Slayer . Ginger Snaps earned seven Fangoria Chainsaw Award nominations, winning for Best Screenplay and Best Limited-Rlease/Direct-to-Video film. It won Best Canadian Feature Film Special Jury Citation at the Toronto International Film Festival and Best Movie at the International Horror Guild Awards. The movie is certified fresh with a 90% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. 6 'Teeth' (2007) Roadside Attractions Written and directed by Mitchell Lichtenstein ( Angelica ), Teeth blends dark comedy and body horror for an unforgettable premise. The film stars Jess Weixler ( Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story ) as Dawn O'Keefe, a high school student in a Christian abstinence group who discovers a startling fact about her own body during a sexual assault. She has vagina dentata, with teeth in her vagina that bite off her attacker's genitals. An Unexpected Adaptation Critics praised Teeth for the way it uses the relationship between horror and virginity in unexpected ways. Lichtenstein won the Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Festival and Jess Weixler was awarded a Special Jury Prize for her performance. The film scored three Fangoria Chainsaw Awards and was nominated for Best Feature Film at the Berlin International Film Festival. It's certified fresh on Rotten Tomatoes with an 81% score from critics. In 2024, Anna K. Jacobs and Michael R. Jackson adapted the film into an off-Broaday musical in New York. 5 'Jennifer's Body' (2009) Directed by legendary filmmaker Karyn Kusama (The Invitation) with a screenplay by Diablo Cody ( Lisa Frankenstein ), Jennifer's Body follows in the footsteps of Ginger Snaps , exploring the relationship between puberty and womanhood with the monstrous. Amanda Seyfried ( Things Heard & Seen ) stars as Anita "Needy" Lesnicki, a bookish high school student who is best friends with the popular Jennifer Check, played by Megan Fox ( Night Teeth ). The cast includes appearances by Adam Brody ( Ready or Not ), Kyle Gallner ( Strange Darling ), Johnny Simmons ( Scott Pilgrim vs. the World ), Amy Sedaris ( At Home with Amy Sedaris ), and J. K. Simmons ( Spider-Man ). How the Movie was Misunderstood Jennifer's Body is another movie that got rough reviews when it came out, but has since been reclassified as a cult classic. To give a sense of the mixed signals surrounding the film's release, Fox was nominated for Worst Actress at the Razzies but won Choice Movie Actress at the Teen Choice Awards. It's a prime example of what happens when marketing and expectations have a negative impact regardless of a film's intentions or actual merits. Jennifer's Body went from hated to loved in just a decade's time. It's a complex tale that explores themes of revenge, sexuality, and personhood. 4 'The Witch' (2015) A24 Robert Eggers made his feature film debut writing and directing The Witch . The folk horror drama stars Anya Taylor-Joy ( Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga ) as Thomasin, a teenage girl in a 1630s Puritan New England family who encounters witchcraft and possession after the disappearance of her younger brother. The cast includes Ralph Ineson ( Nosferatu ), Kate Dickie ( Dept. Q ), Harvey Scrimshaw ( The School for Good and Evil ), and Julian Richings ( Supernatural ). A Chilling Slow-Burn The Witch has been celebrated as an incredibly unnerving slow-burn that launched Taylor-Joy's career. The film won Best First Feature and Best First Screenplay at the Independent Spirit Awards. Taylor-Joy won Breakthrough Actor at the Gotham Awards and was nominated for Best Performance by a Younger Ator at the Saturn Awards. The Witch received five Fangoria Chainsaw Award nominations, winning Best FIlm and Best Actress for Anya Taylor-Joy. It is certified fresh with a 91% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. 3 'Raw' (2016) Wild Bunch Titane director Julia Ducournau made her feature film debut writing and directing Raw . This French coming-of-age body horror movie stars Garance Marillier ( Marinette ) as a vegetarian veterinary student who develops an unmanageable taste for human flesh. The cast includes Ella Rumpf ( Tiger Girl ), Rabah Naït Oufella ( The Class ), Joana Preiss ( Paris, Je T'aime ), and Laurent Lucas ( Lemming ). 'Suspiria' Meets 'Ginger Snaps' Sisterhood, academia, and growing up are all explored in Raw as cannibalism is used as a metaphor. Variety called the movie " Suspiria meets Ginger Snaps ." Raw won the Directors' Fortnight or Critics' Week Prize at the Cannes Film Festival as well as the Citizen Kane Award for Best Directorial Revelation at the Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. It was nominated for six César Awards and won the Sutherland Award for First Feature at the London Film Festival. It is certified fresh on Rotten Tomatoes with a 93% rating from critics. 2 'Piggy' (2022) Filmax Carlota Pereda ( The Chapel ) wrote and directed Piggy , basing it on a short film she made in 2019 of the same name. Laura Galán ( Unknown Origins ), who also starred in the short film, plays Sara, a teen who is bullied for her weight by girls at the pool while she is on vacation. The bullies steal her backpack and clothes, forcing her to walk home in her bathing suit. When Sara realizes that her bullies have been kidnapped by an unknown stranger, she says nothing. Sharp Social Commentary Piggy is atmospheric and bloody with a sharp social commentary that explores the dangers of bullying . The film received four nominations at Spain's Cinema Writers Circle Awards with a win for Galán in the Best New Actress category. The movie received six nominations at the Goya Awards, again with a win for Galán in Best New Actress. She also won the Newcomer Award at the Spanish Actors Union. Piggy is certified fresh with a 91% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. 1 'Hatching' (2022) Nordisk Film Hatching , also called Pahanhautoja , is a Finnish body horror movie directed by Hanna Bergholm ( Helsinki Crimes ) in her feature film debut and written by Ilja Rautsi ( Fleak ). Siiri Solalinna stars as 12-year-old Tinja, a young gymnast struggling with her mother's (Sophia Heikkilä) insistence that they present themselves as the perfect family. When Tinja finds what she thinks is a crow's egg, she brings it home and protects it from the elements. She hides the egg from her family, but when the egg catches, a strange human-sized bird-like creature emerges. Today, we cover Larry David’s recent chat with Seth Meyers, The Daily Show’s Michael Kosta on the NBA betting scandal, John Oliver on Medicare, and a funny moment on The Tonight Show with Allen Iverson. “How can they live? I feel so sorry for them.” Such were the words of Larry David last week, describing on Late Night with Seth Meyers what he thinks every time he sees one of his children. The thought of his two daughters walking around with his genes was too much for the man to bear. Ever the perceptive interviewer, Seth Meyers then pivoted to asking Larry (referring to him as “David” somehow feels disrespectful, no?) about his own parents. “My mother had nothing to brag about,” Larry said, referring to himself. “The poor woman.” He went on to share that he never lived up to her high hopes—in other interviews, Larry has discussed how his parents hoped he would join up with one of our nation’s most honorable professions: the US Postal Service. Instead, as he explained here to Meyers, she was stuck with a then-failing comic. But Larry had a backup plan. His mother, he told Meyers, was like much of America, a massive fan of Johnny Carson. “She couldn’t stop talking about Johnny,” Larry said. “Oh, Johnny. You should have heard Johnny last night. Oh, Johnny was so funny.” That’s when he came up with a deathbed plan. “I wanted her to die happy,” he said. “So I came up with this plan that I would go into the hospital and I would say, ‘Ma, Ma, Johnny saw me perform last night. Johnny wants me on his show, Ma. Johnny likes me.’” Meyers, however, saw a flaw in this never-realized plan: “Do you think there was a chance that you’d tell her that and instead of her having one last happy moment, she would’ve died sad, being disappointed in Johnny Carson’s taste?” Always the honest man, Larry considered the thought before responding, “Quite possibly.” Sometimes, the rotating cast of hosts over on The Daily Show just works out too perfectly. Such are the beautiful ebbs and flows of the news cycle. And last week was one of those times , as former pro-athlete Michael Kosta was behind the desk to discuss the news that shocked the sports world: a betting scandal involving NBA players and the mob. Kosta had the take that went through the heads of NBA and Sopranos fans everywhere. “The mafia must really be hurting if the biggest NBA name they can get is Chauncey Billups,” Kosta said. “They couldn’t get Shaq? He’ll take money for anything.” Somewhere, Charles Barkley smiled. The other major star allegedly part of the deal is Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier. With the perspective of a former struggling athlete, Kosta had a unique take on Rozier’s involvement. “Jesus Christ, Terry. You’ve made over $160 million in your career. You shouldn’t be doing gambling schemes,” Kosta said. “Leave the schemes for the guys on the bench. They’re the ones who need the money.” But as always, Kosta turned back to being the moral compass of a confused and disappointed nation. “The NBA understands this scandal has really tarnished their integrity,” Kosta said. “That’s why the league is making it up to fans by offering them a $50 freeplay on FanDuel using the promo code JailBlazer.” “I’m gonna make it baby, come on, come on!” Over on Last Week Tonight, John Oliver addressed a topic of some importance: Medicare. Or, rather, something called Medicare Advantage, a supplement to the government program administered by private insurers. “They’re just not the same,” Oliver said. “It’s like the difference between a flashlight and a fleshlight.” Oliver begins by pointing out the slew of misleading advertisements targeting seniors during Medicare’s open enrollment period, which use the catch-all “Medicare” when they are actually referring to Medicare Advantage. He hilariously dissects these ads, which often feature celebrities, but are also sometimes long-form advertisements that play with “amateur porn level acting,” to borrow his phrase, with one spouse pleading with another to sign up for Medicare Advantage. You know, the kind of ad you would see on TV at 3 a.m. when you were up sick all night in the pre-streaming days. Oliver wonderfully plays one of these ad for far too long, only to reveal that it was only halfway over. “I also love the disclaimer saying ‘paid actor portrayal,'” Oliver said, enlarging the screen. “As if we’d be so sucked in by the natural delivery of concussed Rob Reiner and over-caffeinated Amy Sedaris here that we’d need to be reminded.” But, as always, Oliver goes on to discuss the serious ramifications of these ads and the truth behind Medicare Advantage, which actually inflates, you’ll be shocked to learn, the cost of Medicare by bringing in private insurers. The upshot: among other flaws, insurers(yes, insurers) are able to add diagnoses to patients’ charts through a process called “upcoding,” essentially billing the government for treatments not actually given, for diagnoses unknown to patients and doctors. “The whole point of a doctor is for them to diagnose you,” Oliver said. “Or, in my case, for them to look at me, down at the chart, look at me again, back at the chart, and then say, ‘48 years old? Are we sure about that?’” And finally, a clip from The Tonight Show. Allen Iverson has been on the press circuit lately, promoting the docuseries about his life, Allen Iv3rson. Well, he and Jimmy Fallon couldn’t resist taking a trip down memory lane, reliving Iverson’s most memorable moment with the sports media, and indeed, perhaps the most famous press conference in sports history. Have a look. Will DiGravio is a Brooklyn-based critic, researcher, and late night comedy columnist, who first contributed to Paste in 2022. When not writing, Tyler enjoys watching more cartoons and reading fantasy books in his home in Ontario, Canada. Whereas a movie only takes up a few hours to tell its story, television shows require a significantly larger investment to get to know the characters and see how the story unfolds. Thus, when a show isn't very good or gets worse later into its run, the disappointment stings even more. Fortunately, there are several animated shows out there that not only started strong but also improved with time . With the rise of streaming services and almost everything now available to watch online, they can be a constant source of entertainment for both returning fans and new ones discovering them for the first time. 10 'The Legend of Vox Machina' (2022–) Image via Prime Video When a mysterious monster begins to attack villages in the Tal'Dorei Empire, a call is put out for heroes to slay it. After all the best ones are brutally murdered, the only ones left are Vox Machina, a group of seven adventurers who can best be described as dysfunctional screw-ups. Still, they're the only heroes available, so Vox Machina will have to deal with their flaws and hang-ups if they're going to save the realm from the likes of dragons, necromancers, and other such threats to the realm. The Legend of Vox Machina is based on Critical Role's popular Dungeons & Dragons campaign, and does a great job translating the silly antics at the table to an epic high-fantasy series full of love, heartbreak, violence, and raunchy humor. The fact that the voice actors are friends and have been playing these characters for nearly a decade means that the interactions sound perfect, and sells Vox Machina as a found family trying to sort out their issues. The first season is a great setup, but come Season 2, the crew one-ups it with more impressive animation , grander set pieces, and even deeper character work that is continued into Season 3. 9 'Transformers: Prime' (2010–2013) Optimus Prime and Megatron clash blades in 'Transformers: Prime' Image via Hasbro Two factions of sentient robots from the planet Cybertron have taken their civil war to Earth. The noble Autobots, led by Optimus Prime ( Peter Cullen ), are on the back foot in their fight against the evil Decepticons, led by Megatron ( Frank Welker ), but find new allies among humans. They'll need all the help they can get because the Decepticons have dangerous ambitions related to raising the dead, and new threats emerge in the form of a human terrorist group called M.E.C.H., and a sadistic rogue Decepticon named Airachnid ( Gina Torres ). Transformers: Prime combined aspects from classic Transformers lore and the Michael Bay film series to create a show that had the best of both worlds. It featured strong-quality writing that wasn't afraid to go to dark places that showcased the horrors of war as best a family show could, while its small cast allowed each character to receive their own character arc. Even new characters introduced in later seasons were given enough attention to leave strong impressions, and the story got even more interesting as it introduced new factions and powerful Cybertronian artifacts. 8 'Teen Titans' (2003–2006) The Titans standing and looking skeptical. Image via Warner Bros. Animation On an island just off the coast of Jump City lies Titans Tower, home of the superheroes Robin ( Scott Menville ), Cyborg ( Khary Payton ), Raven ( Tara Strong ), Beast Boy ( Greg Cipes ), and Starfire ( Hynden Walch ). Together, they form the Teen Titans and fight to protect the city from all manner of threats, such as the masked mastermind Slade ( Ron Perlman ). When they're not saving the city, the Titans navigate the difficulties of five teens trying to live together, or sometimes going on wacky adventures. Teen Titans was one of the dominant superhero shows of the 2000s, and the voice actors were so perfectly chosen that they returned for the more lighthearted Teen Titans Go! Their camaraderie is the show's greatest strength, and only gets better with each season as they settle more into their roles, develop a better repertoire, and each season focuses on the development of a different Titan. Despite how weird some of its episodes could be, Teen Titans also knew when to get serious, with episodes focusing on heavy themes like obsession, self-destruction, prejudice, and showing vulnerability to those you love. 7 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' (2008–2020) R2-D2, Anakin Skywalker, and Mace Windu in 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' Image via Cartoon Network The galaxy finds itself divided by the Clone Wars, fought between the Galactic Republic, fielding an army of clone soldiers, and the Confederacy of Independent Star Systems, using legions of battle droids. Leading the armies of the Republic are the Jedi, warrior-monks who can manipulate an unseen energy called The Force and wield energy weapons called Lightsabers. The war is fought across many worlds, from the battlefields of once peaceful planets to the dark underbelly of major cities and the cutthroat landscape of politics. Star Wars: The Clone Wars was born from George Lucas' desire to explore more stories set during the divisive prequel trilogy, and became one of the most beloved Star Wars shows. During its nearly 140-episode run, the show covered all sorts of Star Wars storylines , with debates about the ethics of war, a look at how war affects the lives of the innocent as well as the soldiers, and crime lords trying to seize power in the chaos, just scratching the surface. Some of the best episodes focused on the clone soldiers ( Dee Bradley Baker ), who, as the seasons go on, transform from flesh robots like they were in the movies to fully fleshed-out characters with their own personalities and opinions on the conflict. 6 'Justice League (2001–2004) / 'Justice League Unlimited' (2004–2006) Justice League Unlimited animated series cast. Image via Warner Bros. Animation After working together to save the world from an alien invasion, Superman ( George Newbern ), Batman ( Kevin Conroy ), Wonder Woman ( Susan Eisenberg ), Green Lantern ( Phil LaMarr ), The Flash ( Michael Rosenbaum ), Martian Manhunter ( Carl Lumbly ), and Hawkgirl ( Maria Canals-Barrera ), decide to form a superhero team called the Justice League. From their Watchtower that orbits the Earth, they answer threats that are too big for any one hero to overcome. Later on, they expanded their roster to include even more heroes, though adversity would once again raise its head in the form of supervillain team-ups and government organizations. Justice League and Justice League Unlimited are really one show split over two different formats: the former told its stories through multi-episode storylines, while the latter was a more traditional half-hour episode. Season 1 can feel a bit slow as it's setting up the league members who hadn't appeared in previous DC shows, but it quickly finds its footing and jumps into bigger action with each subsequent season . The storylines were also very impressive for a kids' show, and often showcased that the reason these characters were superheroes wasn't their powers, but their hearts and how much they were willing to sacrifice for others. 5 'Gravity Falls' (2012–2016) The cast of Gravity Falls in a cave during the Weirdmageddon finale. Image via Disney XD Twin siblings Dipper ( Jason Ritter ) and Mabel Pines ( Kristen Schaal ) spend the summer at Gravity Falls with their great uncle, Stan ( Alex Hirsch ), who runs a tourist trap called the Mystery Shack with his slacker receptionist, Wendy ( Linda Cardellini ), and faithful handyman, Soos (Hirsch). On his first day, Dipper discovers a strange journal that details many strange, paranormal events in the town's history. The more Dipper explores them, the more he discovers that the mysteries are tied to his family and involve an otherworldly entity named Bill Cipher (Hirsch). Gravity Falls was the beginning of a new era of cartoons for Disney , and inspired future projects like Amphibia and The Owl House . The show's success came from its ability to juggle a compelling mystery that rewarded attention to detail, hilarious comedy, and solid character work. Gravity Falls Season 2 took all of this even further when it revealed exactly who wrote the journal and what happened to them, before ending on its own terms rather than continuing into seasonal rot. 4 'Adventure Time' (2010–2019) Adventure Time characters standing together on a cropped poster. Image via Cartoon Network The land of Ooo is a crazy fantasy land divided into themed kingdoms like candy, breakfast, and slime, which are beset by many dangers. Fortunately, it has protection in the form of two heroes: Finn the human ( Jeremy Shada ), an energetic adventurer, and Jake the dog ( John DiMaggio ), a shapeshifting dog and Finn's adopted brother. Their adventures bring them in contact with many fantastical characters, including the scientifically-minded Princess Bubblegum (Hynden Walch), the princess-stealing Ice King ( Tom Kenny ), and a carefree vampire named Marceline ( Olivia Olson ). Adventure Time began as a Dungeons & Dragons- style adventure show, with plenty of quests, random humor, and creative monsters. However, it quickly matured alongside its audience, with later seasons touching on abstract and metaphysical concepts like life, death, the purpose of existence, and more, without losing its original premise. This helped broaden the show's viewer base, and later spawned the spinoffs Adventure Time: Distant Lands and Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake , which continued the later seasons' trend of pushing the characters into more mature situations. 3 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' (2005–2008) Aang air-gliding with a large smile in Avatar: The Last Airbender. Image via Nickelodeon As the Fire Nation prepared for a war of conquest against the entire world, they eradicated the Air Nomads in an attempt to kill the Avatar, the only being who could master all four elements. 100 years later, the Avatar, a young boy named Aang ( Zach Tyler Eisen ), is found frozen in ice at the South Pole by Water Tribe siblings Katara ( Mae Whitman ) and Sokka ( Jack De Sena ). They decide to travel with Aang to help him master the other three elements, while avoiding pursuit by Zuko ( Dante Basco ), the disgraced prince of the Fire Nation, who seeks to capture Aang and return home with honor. Avatar: The Last Airbender has gone down as one of the greatest fantasy shows for kids and adults thanks to its brilliant writing, lovable characters, and immersive worldbuilding. The show was not afraid to tackle hard issues for kids, like the horrors of war, imperialism, free choice, and the morality of pacifism, and each of its characters has their worldview challenged during the journey that forces them to change, not always for the better. Season 1 was pretty good at setting up the world as the group traveled to the North Pole, but Season 2 introduced more characters who quickly became fan favorites, while Season 3 brought the characters into the heart of the Fire Nation itself. 2 'Batman: The Animated Series' (1992–1995) Batman's shadow standing atop a rooftop in front of buildings in Batman The Animated Series. Image via Warner Bros. Animation Gotham City is a haven of crime and corruption, making it difficult for its citizens to feel safe at night. Fortunately, when the sun goes down, Gotham is protected by its Dark Knight, Batman (Conroy). Aided by his ward, Robin ( Loren Lester ), his butler Alfred ( Clive Revill and Efrem Zimbalist Jr. ), and Police Commissioner Gordon ( Bob Hastings ), Batman regularly faces off against both small-time gangsters and powerful supercriminals, including the Joker ( Mark Hamill ), The Penguin ( Paul Williams ), Poison Ivy ( Diane Pershing ), and Ra's al Ghul ( David Warner ). Batman: The Animated Series broke new ground for superhero shows with its mature storytelling , and shaped an entire generation's perspective of these characters to the point that DC Comics made adjustments to certain characters to match the show's versions, and adopted the character of Harley Quinn ( Arleen Sorkin ). People fell in love with its dark atmosphere and willingness to explore why the villains act the way they do, making them sympathetic without justifying their actions. The show's later season saw a change to its art style to better fit with Superman: The Animated Series , which was a bit hit-and-miss, but many of the episodes remained just as powerful as ones from the early seasons. 1 'BoJack Horseman' (2014–2020) Princess Carolyn (Amy Sedaris) having dinner with BoJack Horseman (Will Arnett) in Season 1, Episode 1 of BoJack Horseman. Image via Netflix In the 1990s, BoJack Horseman ( Will Arnett ) starred in the hit sitcom Horsin' Around, but has since fallen into a rut full of alcohol, drugs, sex, and nihilism. He decides to publish his memoirs to get back into the public eye and teams up with ghostwriter Diane Nguyen ( Alison Brie ) to get it written. Along the way, BoJack has various humorous and reflective adventures with Diane, his roommate Todd ( Aaron Paul ), his longtime agent Princess Carolyn ( Amy Sedaris ), and his former sitcom rival Mr. Peanutbutter ( Paul F. Tompkins ). BoJack Horseman 's first season starts a little rocky, but by the time it ends, you can't wait to jump into Season 2 and see where things will develop. From there, the writing gets sharper and funnier, resulting in a show that encourages the audience to take a deep, hard look at themselves and their flaws through its characters. It's also got a lot of effective commentary regarding the Hollywood system and what it does to people, especially young actors, as well as the cycle of abuse. bojack-horseman-poster.jpg Like Follow Followed BoJack Horseman Drama Animation Comedy Release Date 2014 - 2020-00-00 Network Netflix Cast See All Amy Sedaris Will Arnett Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming Showrunner Raphael Bob-Waksberg Genres Drama , Animation , Comedy Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. But once the series lost Oscar-winner Jessica Lange after the fourth season in 2014, subtitled Freak Show , the series slowly started losing steam. The last few seasons didn’t really enter the pop culture zeitgeist. But according to Deadline , for its upcoming 13th season, Murphy is pulling out all the stops. He’s bringing back series icon Jessica Lange, along with several notable actors from the show’s past, and even singer/ Wicked star, Ariana Grande. Ryan Murphy revealed the cast for the new season via an Instagram post on Halloween. The video lists off several names from American Horror Story’s regular stable of actors, with Jessica Lange’s name coming last. This addition was a huge surprise, because earlier this year, Lange was asked about a return to the series. She said, “Christ, no. I mean, I haven’t done it for more than 10 years, 12 years. So, no, I’m not doing it.” This is some Andrew Garfield/ Spider-Man: No Way Home levels of denial. After Lange’s name came up, a quote from AHS: Coven popped up on screen, saying “Surprise, bitch. I bet you thought you’d seen the last of me.” The rest of the cast includes Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett , Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe, and Leslie Grossman. FX Could this season be another continuation of AHS: Coven ? That season focused on a coven of witches based out of New Orleans. It remains a fan-favorite season, especially for LGBTQ fans. Although each season is usually a standalone story, 2018’s American Horror Story: Apocalypse brought the witches back from Coven . This meant resurrecting many dead characters. Most of the main Coven cast is back for season 13, so maybe this is Coven: Part 3 ? All we need is Lily Rabe, Taissa Farmiga, and Francis Conroy back, and it’s a complete set. We’ll have to wait and see what the premise and subtitle of season 13 is. But we imagine we’ll find out soon. If season 13 is indeed the final season, let’s hope they go out with a bang.
