Now You See Me: Now You Don’t star Isla Fisher says, 'I’m really desperate to visit India' Vinay MR Mishra / TNN / Nov 09, 2025, 11:00 IST Share AA + Text Size Small Medium Large Isla Fisher returns for the third installment of the 'Now You See Me' franchise, expressing her eagerness to visit India after two postponed trips. She highlights the seamless integration of new talent with the original cast, fostering a transgenerational appeal for audiences. Fisher also shared her immense pride in her co-stars, describing their bond as a close-knit family. Isla Fisher returns to the world of illusion and high-stakes trickery with Now You See Me: Now You Don’t , the third film in the blockbuster franchise that first introduced audiences to the mysterious Horsemen. In an exclusive conversation with Bombay Times, Isla talks about sharing the spotlight with a new generation of performers, revisiting the camaraderie of the earlier films, and why a trip to India has long been on her list. When asked about her plans to visit India, she quickly replies, “I’ve literally been vaccinated for India twice and both times gotten pregnant after getting the vaccines and therefore, not actually gone. But I’m really desperate to visit and I intend to go. It’s my next dream holiday.” LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 5: Isla Fisher attends the London photocall for Now You See Me: Now You Don't on November 5, 2025 in London, England. (Photo by Eamonn M. McCormack/Getty Images for Lionsgate) The upcoming film, which releases across PVR Inox Cinemas in India on November 14, brings together familiar faces like Jesse Eisenberg alongside three new actors who join the ensemble. Talking about the arrival of fresh talent and if that stirred any competitive nerves, Isla says, “We don’t have those kinds of egos. We’re performers and actors, and obviously, we’re insecure (laughs), but I feel there’s space for everyone. I, as a mother of an 18, 15, and a 10-year-old, want them (my kids) to identify with the characters in this franchise. So, to have these incredible fresh performers with the different energies and different takes — they’re just so relaxed about the magic, and it feels like the older Horsemen were a lot more sort of intense in some ways, which is ironic. So, I think that we just mix together really well. It just helps in being a transgenerational experience for audiences.” The actress, known for films like Confessions of a Shopaholic, Wedding Crashers and The Great Gatsby , lights up when speaking about her co-stars and the close bond they share, even after more than a decade. “I’m so proud of these guys, to work with them and to follow their careers and see them move forward. I am so proud of Jesse (Eisenberg). We all were sort of behind him when his movie came out. It’s really nice. It’s like a big family. Credit: John Russo for New Beauty / John Russo for New Beauty Isla Fisher: Aussie actress reflects on divorce and self-exploration in New Beauty magazine cover shoot Zach Margolius PerthNow 18 November 2025, 12:59pm Copy link Share story While some might argue Isla Fisher’s well-publicised divorce from Sacha Baron Cohen represented a blow to her personal life, the Perth-raised star has proven she’s never been more powerful, cue her recent cover shoot for New Beauty magazine. The mother of three, 49, took time out of her busy Now You See Me 3 publicity schedule to pose for the outlet and reflect on how she’s learned to balance work and life despite her public challenges. With her fiery red hair a feature, Fisher could be seen sporting several commanding outfits including her cover shot that pictured the actress in a pink blazer and matching sequined sheer frock. The actress could also be seen flaunting her enviable figure as she smiled in a bright red top, heels and stockings, with another image capturing the divorcee in a silver dress, expelling a roar as she rested her hands on her thighs. Fisher was shot by celebrity photographer John Russo, whose portfolio features A-list names Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Lopez, and Brad Pitt. Camera Icon The star talks mindfulness, rediscovery and the beauty rituals that keep her centered amid the chaos.⁠ Credit: John Russo for New Beauty / John Russo for New Beauty Speaking to the magazine, Fisher was asked how she’s navigated instability at home in recent times. “I’m not going to lie… it has been a really challenging time. I definitely feel like there’s something about the divorce club that anyone in it understands in a way other people don’t. It’s a different grief,” she said. “I feel like creating a new identity after your divorce is so fun, though. You get to reflect on your values and goals, explore new interests, focus on what you want and rebuild your sense of self.” Camera Icon Isla Fisher is glowing—inside and out. Credit: John Russo for New Beauty / John Russo for New Beauty She said she’s been able to re-discover relationships and interests that may have become distant over the years. “It’s a lot like that, reconnecting to maybe passions you had when you were a kid, but they fell by the wayside when you were raising a family,” Fisher continued. “All the relationships that you have in your life that were not necessarily the forefront of the way that you spend your time, because you’re married. Those relationships that are so supportive and brilliant and often really, really old get to retake centre stage. “I think that’s a really exciting thing. There are lots of positives that have come about from all this — like self-exploration and just trying to be kind to myself. I can just give myself grace whenever I like. That’s all I’m trying to do.” Camera Icon Isla Fisher poses for New Beauty. Credit: John Russo for New Beauty / John Russo for New Beauty Fisher and Cohen spent much of their 14-year marriage living in the UK, with their divorce finalised in July after splitting in late 2023. The mother said her kids have become accustomed to her regular travels away from home and have learned to deal with her repeat absences. “Now that my kids are a bit older, I can feel a little bit less guilty for going away for a week here or a week there,” she said. “I try to remember that I am lucky to get to travel and do these things.” Copy link Share story Tags: Influencers Entertainment TV You might like ‘One of my heroes’ Influencers Aussie actor’s hilarious Steve Irwin imitation earns praise SEE THE PICS Entertainment Robert Irwin spotted with rumoured new love interest Influencers ‘Absolutely smitten’: Aussie influencer shares family update News to your inbox Enter your email for the latest news and updates. Sign in to your MovieWeb account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The Western genre continues to endure, if not thrive, particularly in streaming, thanks to shows like Yellowstone and Outer Range . Netflix has seen success in Western TV, with titles like American Primeval and Territory finding acclaim. It is not surprising that Netflix aims to continue this trend by creating inventive and binge-worthy Western content on its platform with the Kurt Sutter (Sons of Anarchy, Mayans M.C.)–created show The Abandons . Moreover, the series is set to release in December 2025, ensuring the year ends on a high note for the Western TV fandom, with some already touting it as the perfect replacement for Yellowstone . The recent announcement of The Abandons has undoubtedly made an impression. Whether it's from the trailer that depicts a picturesque yet brutal Old West setting, the stage for a battle between a greedy land developer and a community, or the phenomenal casting of Gillian Anderson and Lena Headey, there is a lot to get excited about as we approach its release. Still, there are many details Western fans will be looking for before the series' release. Here, we will cover everything we know about The Abandons , including the cast, plot, and when it will be available to stream . What We Know About the Plot of 'The Abandons' Netflix Set in Washington Territory in 1854, in the fictional town of Jasper Hollow, The Abandons follows two different matriarchs from different backgrounds into conflict : Constance Van Ness (Gillian Anderson), a strong-willed philanthropist who will stop at nothing to continue to grow the mining business fortune she inherited from her husband, and Fiona Nolan (Lena Headey) a faith-driven woman who has made a family of outcasts and souls on the fringe of society, who stands firm against pressure to leave the cattle ranch she built in silver-rich Jasper Hollow under pressure from the Van Ness family. The two families become violently intertwined over a long-hidden secret, land ownership, and a star-crossed romance. In an interview with Tudum , executive producer Christopher Keyser explained that the first chapter of the series delves into a heated rivalry. “This first chapter of The Abandons is a classic American story — the frontier, two families both at war and in love with each other, [and] a battle over who owns the land and who makes the rules” In the same article, Keyser expressed excitement for the project and the twists and turns it will take audiences through, led by its phenomenal cast: “In the middle of murder and revenge and a bit of illicit romance, we get to explore questions we never seem to get away from: What makes a family? How do you stay good in a bad world? And would you change who you are and what you believe in to protect what you love? But in this case, we do it all through the eyes of Lena Headey and Gillian Anderson, as two widowed matriarchs battling to survive. And that … is really something to watch.” Whether the show will have subsequent seasons remains unconfirmed. However, the first season promises nail-biting, addictive action and drama, making it a perfect replacement for fans feeling the void left by the end of Yellowstone . 'The Abandons' Comes With a Phenomenal Cast and Crew Netflix The Abandons is created by Kurt Sutter, who has amassed an impressive career in TV, having previously worked on The Shield , Sons of Anarchy , The Bastard Executioner , and Mayans M.C . However, Sutter exited the project weeks before it wrapped ( via Entertainment Weekly ) — neither Netflix nor Sutter commented on the exit. Sutter is credited with the show's inaugural episode, with Otto Bathurst and Rob Askins taking over for the rest of the series; there is officially no showrunner. While there were issues behind the scenes, Sutter's involvement ideally sets the groundwork to carry the series forward. Notably, director Otto Bathurst has worked on several series, including Black Mirror , His Dark Materials , and Halo , and brings his expertise to carry the inaugural season past its first episode. What will stand out for most is the lead cast of The Abandons , with Lena Headey as Fiona Nolan and Gillian Anderson as Constance Van Ness . Fan favorite Gillian Anderson entered pop culture through her role as Dana Scully in The X-Files , but has remained a consistent force in TV and film, with notable roles in Sex Education and Tron: Ares . Lena Headey, to most, is best known for her role in Game of Thrones as Cersei Lannister . This is the first time Nolan and Anderson will be working together, and the two as opposing forces is a welcome prospect. The series is also backed by a phenomenal supporting cast, including familiar faces from Netflix staples such as Marc Menchaca ( Ozark ) and Katelyn Wells ( Ginny & Georgia ), while actors from past Sutter-created shows also appear: Brían F. O’Byrne ( The Bastard Executioner ), Clayton Cardenas ( Mayans M.C. ), and Michael Ornstein ( Sons of Anarchy ). Complete cast list of The Abandons : Lena Headey as Fiona Nolan Gillian Anderson as Constance Van Ness Brían F. O’Byrne as Walter Paxton Clayton Cardenas as Quentin Serra Elle-Máijá Tailfeathers as Oma Serra Haig Sutherland as Pastor Collier Jack Doolan as Leslie Moran Jonathan Koensgen as Joseph Langley Katelyn Wells as Samara Alderton Marc Menchaca as Sheriff Hayworth Michael Greyeyes as Jack Cree Michiel Huisman as Roache Michael Ornstein as Issac Marstein Patton Oswalt as Mayor Nibley Sarah Grace White as Kiki When and How To Watch Netflix's 'The Abandons' Netflix The Abandons will stream exclusively on Netflix and will be available on December 4, 2025. There will be 10 episodes, all available on the same day . Netflix subscribers are certainly going to have their hands full of content in December. The platform is bringing holiday movies and series, including the Netflix original Christmas series Man vs. Baby starring Rowan Atkinson. Additionally, fans will be anticipating the final episodes of Stranger Things alongside the return of favorites like Emily in Paris for its fifth season. Yet, The Abandons is perfectly placed at the start of the month, perfect for a binge session before getting two wrapped up in seasonal viewings. During her time on SNL, McKinnon always came up with the most hilarious sketch ideas. She worked on the show for a decade and left viewers with numerous comically memorable moments. Now, in a podcast appearance with Amy Poehler, she reveals how she almost kissed every cast member during her final sketch of the show. Kate McKinnon’s initial pitch for SNL last episode involved kissing every cast member Kate McKinnon recently spoke to Amy Poehler on the latter’s Good Hang podcast. Soon after talking about trim carpentry and making furniture, Poehler asked McKinnon about her last show on SNL. The host recalled how she remembered McKinnon’s final sketch as feeling compelling and moving. However, McKinnon then went on to explain that it wasn’t her pitch. “My pitch was that I did this character Sheila Sovage, the barfly. And my pitch was that I would tongue every single person in the cast in line,” McKinnon shared. As Poehler began to crack up, McKinnon said she thought the “alien thing was a little more meaningful and had a better tone” and hence they went with that. When McKinnon then mentioned how everyone narrownly missed sucking her face, Poehler said it would have been “a goodbye tonguing.” When referring to “the alien thing,” McKinnon was speaking about her final sketch in which she appeared as Colleen Rafferty. This character was known for coming across aliens and always having bad, but funny, encounters with them. On the other hand, the other subjects who met an alien always described a blissful experience. Towards the end of the sketch, during her final show, McKinnon as Rafferty exited the set, waving goodbye to everyone and finally boarding the ship with the aliens. At the time, McKinnon held the record of the longest time a woman had been part of the show. Furthermore, as a performer on SNL, she won two Emmys back-to-back in 2016 and 2017. However, one story she recently shared might just take the cake. Talking with fellow alum Kate McKinnon on her Good Hang podcast, Poehler revealed that a guest host actually fell asleep. Funnily enough, that was right in the middle of a sketch rehearsal. The moment had both comedians cracking up as they reminisced about the beautiful, sleep-deprived madness of life at Saturday Night Live. Amy Poehler recalls one SNL host ‘fell asleep’ during dress rehearsal for a sketch Talking about the ups and downs of SNL’s nonstop creative grind on Good Hang Podcast, Amy Poehler and Kate McKinnon couldn’t help laughing about the sketches that tanked. “Did you ever go on the server and rewatch sketches that bombed?” Poehler asked. “We used to sit there together,” she said to watch their failed dress rehearsals. “Just to process it and remind ourselves that everybody bombs,” the 54-year-old added. Kate McKinnon burst out laughing as she shared one of her favorite behind-the-scenes moments. She said during a sketch, someone just stopped, sat down on stage, and basically gave up. “There were a few hits that we would watch over and over again,” McKinnon admitted. “There was one rehearsal where a person — I won’t say who — simply stopped doing the sketch and sat down on the stage. That was a fun watch,” the 41-year-old shared. Poehler also shared her own hilarious behind-the-scenes story from her SNL days. She remembered when a guest host actually fell asleep right in the middle of a dress rehearsal. McKinnon replied that it made sense with how late everyone stayed up, and the Golden Globe Award-winner agreed. Earlier this month, Amy Poehler hit a significant milestone with SNL, stepping back in as host for the first time in over ten years, just in time for the show’s 50th anniversary. She said being back in Studio 8H made her nostalgic for her days on the cast. Even though Poehler and McKinnon never worked on SNL at the same time — the former wrapped in 2008 while the latter joined in 2012 — the two have worked together on other projects. The two have since teamed up several times, including during the SNL 50th anniversary celebration. Kate McKinnon’s goal is to be able to ‘survive the apocalypse for four days’ The Saturday Night Live star, 41, has swapped city life for a self-sufficient existence on a “homestead”, and made the admission about her aim while discussing her new rural lifestyle while appearing on Good Hang, the podcast hosted by her former co-star Amy Poehler . During the episode, Kate spoke about leaving New York City after two decades to reconnect with nature, saying: “I belong on the homestead.” Kate also reflected on her lifelong fascination with the natural world, describing how it began in childhood. She added: “I loved bugs and science and making nature crafts. I remember making little bits of mud and putting them places. “Every time we went to a seafood restaurant, I would say, ‘Mom, can I take the empty clam muscle and lobster shells home with me and put them in the bath tub?’ “And after rinsing them of marinara sauce, she would let me put them in the bathtub and I would get in with them and just enjoy that.” When Amy asked about her motivations for living away from the city, Kate admitted her decision was partly rooted in a fear of the future. She said: “I think the reason I’ve done it is that I believe very much that we are doomed. “My goal is surviving the apocalypse (for) four days. If I can make it to four, oh mama, I will have achieved something.” The Ghostbusters actress described how she now spends her time growing food and woodworking on her property. She said: “I think it’s in my genes because my grandfather was a woodworker, my father was an architect. “I love the practicality of, you can manipulate this material and then you can spend time in it. How crazy is that? “You can sit on it. I love to sit on things, I do… to say I will sleep on what I did today.” Kate added she has already built her own table but admitted that the result was far from perfect. She said: “What you do, just kind of put it up inside the home anyways and I have absolutely decreased the property value of the house with my shoddy work.” Kate also told Amy she intends to add to her growing list of survival skills. Just as Americans are prepping their Thanksgiving turkey, Saturday Night Live has brought back one of its most beloved Thanksgiving traditions. On Tuesday, Nov. 25, SNL posted the beloved sketch ‘Back Home Ballers’, serving up just the right nostalgic treat for the holiday season. It’s “that time of the year again”, SNL captioned the video shared on its social media handles. Back Home Ballers The 2014 rap parody ‘Back Home Ballers’ is one of the beloved sketches that humourously captures the essence of adult children returning to their parents’ home for the holiday season. Kate McKinnon , Cecily Strong, Sasheer Zamata, Vanessa Bayer, Leslie Jones, Aidy Bryant, and guest host Cameron Diaz perform a hip-hop song about the mundane reality of going home to their parents’ house for Thanksgiving and enjoying the royal treatment. The video begins with a van pulling up in front of a suburban house. The number plate reads “YRGIRLS”, and seven women step out, introducing themselves and how they are treated by their parents during the holiday season. The sketch captures perfectly relatable moments that would strike a chord with anyone who’s back home for the holidays. From getting princess treatment, avoiding household chores, and having the luxury of getting their laundry done by someone else, the song celebrates the privileges grown-ups enjoy when they return home for the Thanksgiving season. The most iconic song ever Eleven years after its debut, ‘Back Home Ballers’ remains the undisputed Thanksgiving banger. When SNL dropped the video, it sent social media into a frenzy. Fans flooded the comments with effusive praise. One Instagram user said the sketch is her favourite: “My favorite forever.” Another agreed: “One of my favorite sketches of all time.” A third shared the same sentiments and added, “No disrespect to the new class who are wonderful, but this was prime/iconic ladies-on-SNL time. ” “This will forever be iconic,” another declared. Another fan confessed, “This is the best!! I still mourn the loss of these ladies!!!” Some gushed about the Wi-Fi password — iconic, after all. Fans of Aidy said, “Missed Lil Baby Aidy.” X is flooded with memes of Aidy’s striking alphabetic necklace. “How I miss lil baby Aidy, also Kate and Vanessa,” another added. Maya Dehlin Spach/Getty Images/John Nacion/PMC While SNL50: The Anniversary Special was stacked with special guest stars, Steven Spielberg didn’t make the final show. Following the special’s ‘ Close Encounters ‘ sketch, Mikey Day revealed that he “originally had Steven Spielberg in it” but ended up having to remove the 3x Oscar-winning director’s appearance, resulting in himself “spiraling into an awkward abyss” with Spielberg. “Everyone loves Steven Spielberg. I love this man so much. He’s so important to me and so many people,” he raved on The Tonight Show . “So we had Steven Spielberg come in at the end of the sketch playing himself. He’s like, ‘Hey, I have experience in this subject matter, and I’d like to make a movie based on your life.'” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Late Night TV ‘SNL50’: Meryl Streep Joins Kate McKinnon In ‘Close Encounter’ As Pedro Pascal & Woody Harrelson Crack Up News Nikki Glaser Roasts ‘SNL’ Cast In Expletive-Filled Promo Although the Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977) director was game for the cameo and was even at rehearsal, Day explained that the show was running long and everyone was forced to cut time from their sketches. “And we’re like, ‘I think we have to cut Steven Spielberg,’ because it was an added thing! You know what I mean?” Day told Jimmy Fallon. “I don’t even like talking about it! It makes me uncomfortable. Dude, I don’t like that this happened. I hate it. It’s an awful thing.” Aidy Bryant as Dr. Tyler, Jon Hamm as General Fairfax, Meryl Streep as Colleen Rafferty Sr., Kate McKinnon as Colleen Rafferty, Pedro Pascal as Kermit and Woody Harrelson during the ‘Close Encounter’ sketch on ‘SNL50: The Anniversary Special’ (Chris Haston/ NBC ) Day went on to recount “another awkward moment” at an event honoring SNL creator Lorne Michaels the next night, after relaying to Spielberg’s assistant that his part was cut, noting the Fabelmans director seemed to be under the impression “that the whole sketch had been cut.” “And I have awkwardness with Steven Spielberg because we had to cut him out of our sketch,” he said. “So I briefly talked to him and then he goes, ‘Yeah, the whole sketch was cut.’ I know that it wasn’t, because I would’ve heard, but instead of going, ‘Oh, I don’t think that’s right,’ I just went, ‘Oh no! The whole thing was cut? Nooo!'” Day continued, “A normal person would’ve gone, ‘Oh really? I don’t think so. Yeah, I think you might’ve heard wrong.’ But I just went, ‘Oh no, it was cut? Nooo!’ It was so awful.” While Spielberg was cut from the sketch, Kate McKinnon reprised her role as Colleen Rafferty in the sketch, which also featured appearances from Meryl Streep, Pedro Pascal, Woody Harrelson and Jon Hamm, as well as fellow SNL alum Aidy Bryant. Benedict Cumberbatch and Olivia Colman's "fun" film confirms UK streaming date Just in time for Christmas… Searchlight Pictures Daniel Goldstraw Published: Wednesday, 29 October 2025 at 5:35 pm Subscribe to Radio Times: 10 weeks for £10, including the Christmas edition Share on facebook Share on twitter Share on pinterest Share on reddit Email to a friend Two months on from its release in cinemas, a streaming release date has been confirmed for the comedy film The Roses, starring Benedict Cumberbatch and Olivia Colman. Ad The film, which hit cinemas in August, will be available to watch on Disney Plus from 3rd December this year – so not too long to wait at all. The Roses is a savage and star-filled reimagining of the 1989 classic The War of the Roses, itself based on the novel of the same name by Warren Adler. It starred Cumberbatch and Colman as the seemingly perfect couple, Ivy and Theo, both of whom appear successful and happy in their day-to-day lives. However, their relationship suddenly goes into freefall after Theo’s career nosedives and Ivy’s own ambitions take off, in what has been described as “a story of real life gone spectacularly wrong". Directed by Jay Roach, the film also boasted a starry supporting cast including Andy Samberg, Ncuti Gatwa, Kate McKinnon, Zoë Chao, Hala Finley, Jamie Demetriou and Sunita Mani. Andy Samberg and Benedict Cumberbatch in The Roses. Searchlight Pictures It has largely been well received by critics, with the Hollywood Reporter stating that "Cumberbatch and Coleman are terrific" and has been certified as Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes, with 65 per cent of 187 critics' reviews being positive . In our own review, we gave the film three stars out of five, finding it to be fun but toothless , arguing that its two leads perhaps failed to fully portray the bitterness that comes to the fore as the film progresses. Described as a satirical black comedy, it will hitting the streaming service just in time for Christmas. The Roses will be available to stream on Disney+ from 3rd December. According to Rick Riordan, who authored the books and serves as an executive producer on the series, the manifestation of the goddess will change. McKinnon’s casting turned heads when it was announced in October, and according to Riordan, he and the team on the show talked “a lot” about who would be right for the part. Speaking to TheWrap in a wide-ranging discussion ahead of Season 2, Riordan explained that it was important to both him and his fans that one aspect of the goddess remain true. “Her appearance, her manifestation of ultimate beauty, changes depending on who is beholding that beauty. Because beauty is different for everybody,” he noted. “It’s very subjective. So she doesn’t look like just one person. And you know, I will tell you that we honor that in the third season.” “So, while Kate is incredible, and maybe a very unexpected and fun sort of manifestation where we spend most of our time with, that’s not the only manifestation,” he continued. Does that mean McKinnon will be sharing the part with another actress, or even actresses? Will she be in prosthetics of some sort? Riordan wouldn’t hint at anything else. “I’ve probably already said too much,” he admitted with a laugh. McKinnon will guest star in the third season of the show, which is currently in production in Vancouver, and her character “must be sure that Percy Jackson respects the power and importance of love before she agrees to offer aid on his quest.” Season 2 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” premieres this December, and follows the events of the second book in Riordan’s series, “The Sea of Monsters.” Season 3 will likewise adapt the events of book 3, “The Titan’s Curse.” Season 2 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” premieres on Disney+ on Dec. 10. By Justin Harp November 21, 2025 TOP STORIES Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Searchlight Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Tap Here To Add Us Weekly As A Trusted Source Add as a preferred source on Google Benedict Cumberbatch and Olivia Colman lead an all-star cast in the 2025 comedy The Roses . In the director Jay Roach ’s movie, Theo (Cumberbatch) and Ivy Rose’s (Colman) thin veneer of a happy marriage crumbles over control of their family home. Theo becomes envious of his wife’s success as a budding restaurateur when he loses his job at a prestigious architectural firm and suddenly becomes a stay-at-home parent. Both of their lives are at a crossroads as Theo decides to file for divorce, leading to bth Roses resorting to the lowest of lows to take each other down. Their divorce boils down to who gets to keep their family home — and their friends and loved ones are all forced to choose sides. The Roses features a remarkable international cast, including Saturday Night Live alums Kate McKinnon and Andy Samberg , Academy Award winner Allison Janney and former Doctor Who star Ncuti Gatwa . I don’t like it,” The Favourite actress, 51, said during the Tuesday, September 16, episode of Amy Poehler’s “Good Hang” podcast, admitting that she is “most afraid” of having to “show any skin” or “pretending to have sex […] Keep scrolling for more information about The Roses and its cast. Who Is in ‘The Roses’? Benedict Cumberbatch and Olivia Colman star in The Roses as Theo and Ivy Rose, whose nasty divorce battle centers around who gets to keep their family home. “[They fight over the house] because they’re both invested in it, you know, massively,” Cumberbatch told NPR . Longtime friends Cumberbatch and Colman spend most of The Rose fighting relentlessly on screen, though they assured NPR that they are as close as ever in real life. “When you get to work with a friend as brilliant and fabulous as Olivia, but also the trust, the immediacy of how you can go further, faster, the shorthand,” Cumberbatch said. “But also she’s so, so, so good that you up your game.” In a joint interview with ABC News , Cumberbatch described Colman as a “ridiculously charming human being” and a “loyal” friend. “He’s the kindest, funniest, sweetest,” Colman said of her costar. “Also, [he doesn’t] know how lovely [he is]. There’s a lovely humility to [him].” Ivy and Theo’s messy breakup spirals completely out of control in The Roses , forcing their friends and family to pick sides. Andy Samberg has a supporting role as Theo’s divorce lawyer Barry, while Kate McKinnon plays Barry’s wife, Amy. Searchlight Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Doctor Who star Ncuti Gatwa appears in The Roses as Jeffrey, the front-house manager at Ivy’s restaurant, while Allison Janney is cast as Ivy’s high-priced divorce lawyer Eleanor. “[ The Rose s is] a tale about two people who really got a kick out of each other, and could still if they could just find their way back to each other, and ignore what their expectations were for their life. Some of which were gendered, some of which were not gendered,” McKinnon told Refinery29 . “I believe in this couple, even though things are not going well for them at present.” Mr. Robot ’s Sunita Mani , Venom: The Last Dance actress Hala Finley and Nightbitch star ​​Zoë Chao also appear in The Roses . What Is ‘The Roses’ Based On? The Roses is based on author Warren Adler ’s 1981 novel The War of the Roses . Danny DeVito previously directed a 1989 movie version of The War of the Roses , with Michael Douglas and Kathleen Turner in the leading roles. Screenwriter Tony McNamara used the novel and previous film adaptation as a jumping off point but doesn’t consider The Roses to be a direct remake. “Danny’s movie is so great and I was like, ‘Well, we can’t do that again,’” McNamara told The Los Angeles Times . “That was about two people tearing each other apart as they get divorced, but this was more like: How do two people who desperately want to stay married stay married despite not having the skill set to do so?” Colman also differentiated between The Roses and its predecessor, describing her version as “its own beast.” Thank You! With this in mind, is it possible that the Fab Four of paranormal investigations have been busting ghosts for decades without our knowledge? According to Dan Aykroyd , who plays Dr. Ray Stantz in the beloved Ghostbusters franchise, his character’s cameo in 1995’s Casper is the real deal. Aykroyd, who co-created the Ghostbusters franchise with Harold Ramis, spoke about his brief part in the family-friendly haunted house film, starring Christina Ricci and Bill Pullman, saying he considers the cameo part of Ghostbusters lore. “I think so, given the fact that [Steven] Spielberg asked for me and said, ‘Come and do this,’ and that they built me in there,” said Aykroyd on the Talking Strange podcast. “Of course, it’s a beautiful nod to what we were doing with Ivan [Reitman] and everybody. While trying to rid the spooky place of ghosts, Carrigan calls the Ghostbusters to investigate. Aykroyd’s Dr. Ray Stantz arrives to represent the group, but is scared off by what he finds inside. “Who you gonna call?” he begins, referencing the Ghostbusters’ theme song. “Someone else.” Dan Aykroyd’s Dr. Ray Stantz is part of the original Ghostbusters group, which also includes Bill Murray, Ernie Hudson, and Harold Ramis, who serves as the other Horseman of the paranormal apocalypse. Moreover, Casper wouldn’t be Aykroyd’s only Ghostbusters-related cameo. If you remember, he played a cab driver in the 2016 female-led Ghostbusters reboot, starring Kristin Wiig, Kate McKinnon, Leslie Jones, and Melissa McCarthy. Credit: Will Heath/NBC/NBCU Photo Bank via Getty Kate McKinnon always leaves the audience laughing. Her original idea of how to do that when she exited Saturday Night Live in 2022, after a decade in the show's cast, would have been very tongue-forward if it had aired. "My pitch was that I did this character Sheila Sovage, the barfly," McKinnon explained to Amy Poehler on Tuesday's episode of the Good Hang podcast . "And my pitch was that I would tongue every single person in the cast in a line, and I thought, ultimately, that the alien thing was a little more meaningful and had a better tone. So, we went with that." Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter . She added, "So everyone narrowly missed sucking my face." Poehler, who was an SNL cast member herself from 2001 to 2008, quipped that it would have been "a goodbye tonguing." McKinnon told a similar story in August 2022, noting that COVID restrictions helped shut that down . Instead, she played another of her recurring characters in her final moments in the cast: Colleen Rafferty, a woman who always has a comically bad encounter with aliens she meets; meanwhile, the others being studied, who also came face-to-face with an extraterrestrial being, describe bliss. This time, Miss Rafferty agreed to go with the aliens permanently. Fans saw her boarding a spaceship and waving goodbye. Kate McKinnon hosts 'Saturday Night Live' in 2023. Will Heath/NBC via Getty "Well, Earth, I love ya," McKinnon said, as she appeared to he holding back tears. "Thanks for letting me stay a while." When she left SNL , McKinnon held the record for the longest a woman had been on the cast. Looking back, she noted that the experience had been "very emotional," because "it was everything to me, and those people are everything to me." Known for her impressions of Hillary Clinton, Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, Kellyanne Conway, and many others, McKinnon was nominated for nine Emmys — two of which she won — during her decade on the show. So, I did, I loved it, I had the best decade, and then I was just like, my body was tired, and I felt like it was time." Since leaving the SNL cast, McKinnon has returned to host SNL and has appeared in movies such as Barbie and The Roses . Watch the full conversation above. Activate your Online Access Now Article content In a report to be discussed at today’s regular council meeting, Ellen Fry, the city’s integrity commissioner, concludes the mayor violated the code of conduct on two occasions, first “by trying to intimidate” someone “by applying pressure at her place of work,” and in another instance by treating members of the public disrespectfully with the use of the term “wackadoodle.” While the province’s Municipal Act allows council to suspend the mayor’s pay as a penalty for code of conduct violations, and the code of conduct allows council to remove him from committees, Fry’s report recommends only that council issue Wren a reprimand. City council’s regular meeting takes place today at 5:30 p.m. While the motion on the agenda simply calls on council to receive the integrity commissioner’s report, members are expected to vote on its recommendations. Article content In a statement emailed to local media Monday night, the complainant, Bill McKinnon, urges council to “impose the maximum available sanction under Ontario law – suspension of remuneration for up to 90 days.” In a prepared statement, Wren said he accepts the integrity commissioner’s report, adding that the report in part vindicates him, but he also expresses regret for comments made in a moment of “ poor judgment .” Bill McKinnon took over the organization of last year’s Brockville Santa Claus Parade with his wife, Kate, after Brockville’s two Rotary clubs were no longer able to continue organizing the popular event . Article content Fry’s report notes that McKinnon’s complaint made eight allegations, four of which she deemed worthy of investigation under council’s code of conduct or the province’s Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. The first allegation is that Wren “improperly influenced city staff” to prevent McKinnon from organizing the parade for a second year. The second allegation was that the mayor “treated members of the public improperly” in an Aug. 29 phone call to Gina Rose Cristello of Solid Rock Realty, and by referring to “wackadoodles from Facebook” in a call with McKinnon on Aug. 25. McKinnon also alleged the mayor demonstrated bias “by improperly benefiting the Rotary Club and the role of his brother-in-law Dave Paul in the Rotary Club.” Advertisement 5 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content And the fourth allegation Fry investigated was that Wren “made false statements” in a social media post. The mayor asserted the former parade organizers “now claim to face thousands of dollars in city fees….There were no such extra fees last year and there would not have been this year either.” The mayor also said “the suggestion that (he) demanded public recognition if council waived fees is a bald faced lie.” Article content The accusation that Wren improperly influenced staff stems from a disagreement between McKinnon and the mayor over the city’s decision not to grant McKinnon a fee waiver in relation to the 2025 Santa Claus Parade. The report notes McKinnon posted on social media about the disagreement, and Wren felt the posts “were embarrassing the city.” Advertisement 6 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content Meanwhile, Fry continues, the city had already decided to take the management of the parade in-house, rather than continue with the McKinnons or another outside group, something the city announced two days after Wren and McKinnon spoke on the phone. “Mr. McKinnon believes that because of the timing of the city’s decision in relation to his discussion with Mayor Wren, Mayor Wren must have inappropriately pressured staff to reject the application of his organization,” notes the report. However, the report adds, both Wren and city manager Sandra MacDonald “state that the decision to manage the 2025 parade in-house was a decision made independently by staff, without any involvement of Mayor Wren or council, and that … it was made before Mayor Wren spoke to Mr. McKinnon on August 25. Mr. McKinnon has not provided any information that contradicts this.” Advertisement 7 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content Fry also notes she has not found any information from other sources that would support McKinnon’s belief, and so dismisses that complaint. Bill McKinnon, then one of the organizers of Brockville’s Santa Claus Parade, speaks to city council on Tuesday, Sept. 24, 2024. Photo by RONALD ZAJAC / The Brockville Recorder and Times The complaint about improper treatment of the public relates to a call Wren made on Aug. 29, to the real estate firm where Kate McKinnon works, which the mayor said aimed “to put a stop to social media posts by Mr. McKinnon’s wife that he viewed as reputationally damaging and containing misinformation.” Instead of speaking to Kate McKinnon, notes Fry, Wren raised the issue with one of her colleagues. “The fact that Mayor Wren spoke to the colleague of Mr. McKinnon’s wife rather than speaking to Mr. McKinnon’s wife directly would reasonably be interpreted as an attempt to intimidate Mr. McKinnon’s wife by applying pressure at her place of work,” Fry concludes. Advertisement 8 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content The integrity commissioner also takes issue with a colourful term Wren used in another call. “In his conversation with Mr. McKinnon on Aug. 25, Mayor Wren expressed concern that Mr. McKinnon’s social media posting would lead to him and city staff having to deal with the ‘wackadoodles from Facebook.’ “‘Wackadoodles’ is generally understood to be a derogatory term, and given the fact that the conversation between Mayor Wren and Mr. McKinnon concerned city business, this was not a situation where the term was used in a private conversation. Consequently, I consider that using this term violated the requirement in section 7.0 of the Code of Conduct to treat members of public with respect.” Wren told the commissioner his regrettable language happened during a “frustrating and tiring period of days that he was experiencing in dealing with the impact of a serious apartment fire in Brockville .” Advertisement 9 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content Fry goes on to note she did not investigate the claim regarding the Rotarians and Dave Paul, because Wren “did not play a part in the decision to manage the 2025 parade in-house.” And on the matter of the mayor making false statements, Fry concludes that Wren was incorrect in his comment about fees, but he believed his information to be correct. She does not reach a conclusion on the “bald-faced lie” comment, citing a lack of evidence. Fry does not recommend any penalty over the “wackadoodles” comment, citing Wren’s expression of regret. She does recommend a reprimand over his conversation with Kate McKinnon’s colleague concluding “it was inappropriate that Mayor Wren took this approach rather than speaking to Mr. McKinnon’s wife directly.” Advertisement 10 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content In his statement, Wren says he accepts the integrity commissioner’s report, adding it confirms he did not misuse his office to influence staff decisions. “I have deep respect for the role of city staff and consistently refrain from interfering in matters that are theirs to decide,” the mayor adds. “The report clearly finds that the complainant levelled accusations that are unfounded and without merit.” Wren also notes that Fry’s report addresses his “response to deeply offensive comments directed towards (him). “I acknowledge that my reaction represented a moment of poor judgment. I regret this and accept the criticism,” the mayor’s statement adds. “While navigating opposing views is part of public service, the rise in personal attacks and harassment makes it increasingly difficult to maintain composure in every moment.” This story has been updated to add new information. November 02, 2025 Add Cracked to Google Matt Solomon Back in 1975, Lorne Michaels laid down a few rules for his new show, Saturday Night . One pillar was that his program would be everything the popular Carol Burnett Show was not. The prime time variety show “lacked subtlety and nuance; it was too broad, too bourgeois, and too smug—especially when the performers broke out laughing in mid-sketch, doubling up at the hilarity of themselves,” according to Saturday Night: A Backstage History of Saturday Night Live . Lorne demanded “more integrity and respect for the writing here,” dismissing corny sketch ideas as, “That’s Carol Burnett .” Burnett was rightly offended when word got back to her. “I don’t know what I did to upset that man, but I’m so sorry,” Burnett told The New Yorker earlier this year. Not that she’s ever been asked, but Burnett would refuse to host SNL if an offer came her way. “I would not be interested. That’s all I can say.” But Lorne Michaels wasn’t wrong. As a young upstart comedy show featuring a cast of twentysomething comedians, the last thing early Saturday Night should have done was emulate the status quo. By bringing National Lampoon’s “burn it all down” mentality to late-night, Saturday Night established a counterculture comedy show for a younger generation. That longevity meant a couple of things. First, its hip guests of the time — Paul Simon, Steve Martin , Tom Hanks — eventually became the standard bearers of mainstream culture. Its audience aged with the show; a 20-year-old viewer in 1975 is now 70, so SNL’s signature catchphrases wouldn’t be out of place in AARP Magazine. A show that lasts for fifty years inevitably becomes the thing it set out to avoid: The definition of establishment, mainstream comedy. Somewhere along the way, Lorne must have decided the things he hated about The Carol Burnett Show weren’t so bad after all. Today’s SNL definitely isn’t devoted to “sublety and nuance” — this season’s best sketch featured Ashley Padilla and her uncontrollable farting . Advertisement Harvey Korman and Tim Conway were too smug and self-satisfied when they cracked up at their own jokes? Then how does SNL’s producer feel about the fact that the biggest breakout sketches of the past few years — Lisa from Temecula, Beavis and Butthead, pretty much any of Kate McKinnon’s Close Encounters bits — went viral due to the performers breaking up? Saturday Night Live is its generation’s version of The Carol Burnett Show . Own it, Lorne, and be proud of it. There’s nothing wrong with defining comedy for a generation or two. But realize that if you’re the cool kid of yesteryear, you can’t be the cutting-edge comedy of today, no matter how many times you drop Gen Z catchphrases. Join Dazed Club on iOS and Android via telegraph.co.uk January 17, 2015 Fashion Incoming Tilda Swinton: the art of the everyday The Academy Award winner and Dazed cover star reflects on the emotional bonds we form with fashion after her poetic Pitti performance Share Link copied ✔️ January 17, 2015 Fashion Incoming Text Susanne Madsen Read More Music 7 musicians who had their secret identities exposed Art & Photography Candid photos from a Paris strip club locker room Art & Photography These photos trace a diasporic archive of transness Tilda Swinton, Dazed May 2010 Gallery / 8 images It’s not every day you line up at a cloakroom and hand over your ticket to Tilda Swinton , who hurries back towards the rails to fetch your stuff and delicately presents it to you. But that was what happened at Swinton and fashion historian Olivier Saillard’s Cloakroom performance in Florence this week, where the audience were invited to leave things throughout the play, which Tilda then contemplated and interacted with, from her licking a jacket to throwing herself full force on top of a coat and burying her face in a hood, in a gesture of bringing out the poetry in ‘ordinary’ clothes. Fashion churns out an endless stream of products – whether fast or high-end – and Saillard and Swinton’s performance asked us to press pause and appreciate the things we already own. As Olivier Saillard commented in his notes for the performance: “The collection takes life, built up on what’s acquired and not on novelty, wandering the opposite path to that which was constructed by fashion.” A Fondazione Pitti Discovery project staged in the gilded Saloncino at the Medici-commissioned Teatro della Pergola – the oldest opera house in Italy now focusing on drama productions – it is the third instalment of the duo’s Impossible Wardrobe (Swinton showcasing fashion archive pieces in a performance inspired by Saillard’s position as director of the Palais Galliera in Paris) and Eternity Dress (the making of a dress on Swinton’s body) and the result of a three-year collaboration. “We kind of completed a trilogy with this one,” Swinton said after the performance. “It’s a completion of that enquiry which is something about the soul of clothes. Maybe the interesting thing about clothes is that people live in them, and that there’s nothing else really to be said, and so it’s trying to trace that and concentrate on that, and to honour our clothes, rather than Coco Chanel or Napoleon or anybody else. Actually our clothes.” During the 90-minute performance, Swinton – in a graceful and demure long-sleeved black dress with black patent stilettos – continuously repeated the ritualistic act of approaching the audience’s garments and silently communicating with them, while Saillard then took each piece to hang on the rails along the wall. Dazed dropped off a fox stole, which Swinton laid to rest with a single stalk of wheat, and she put her ear to Dazed contributor Marta Represa’s coat to listen to it and whispered to another piece of outwear, “Oh, don’t be silly.” Afterwards, Swinton spoke of her approach to each item: “In the first instance there’s something about trying to resist the superficial attributes of something. I mean, it would be very easy to only go with something that’s brightly coloured in a brightly coloured way, or something that was very soft in a very soft way, so maybe [I try to] dislodge one’s expectations.” “Maybe the interesting thing about clothes is that people live in them, and that there’s nothing else really to be said.” – Tilda Swinton The performance was not without its amusing moments as Swinton used her impossibly elegant body to comical effect by positioning herself on top of things, and tried to place a coat on a table like it was a person sitting up. But there was also a strong sensual element to it, like the way she crawled on all fours under to table to sniff a man’s jacket and then caress it with her head like a cat. It elevated our everyday clothes – whether inconspicuous or precious - to special status, and underscored the innate stories and memories that our clothes carry. “One of the inspirations of this piece was the fact that for last two years I’ve been slowly going through my mother’s wardrobe,” Swinton said. “She died two years ago when we were making Impossible Wardrobe, and so it’s been very much a part of our inquiry, this whole question of clothes outliving us very, very often. The body’s gone, the clothes are still here. And there’s a tradition of people inheriting clothes. Certainly in Scotland people tend to wear their grandfather’s kilts. There’s a feeling that clothes are to be passed down from generation to generation. It’s only relatively recently that we have a fetish for newness.” In a way, the performance had its own overtones of the fetishisation of clothes, but in the sense of imbuing an object with magical powers rather than a more superficial one. “It’s not really about appearance at all. It’s about spirit, I suppose, and the life lived in these garments,” Swinton said. “The more I do the piece, the more I realise that it’s about making relationships. Something comes, you go ‘Ah! I can make a relationship with this’. And you know, we all have relationships with an old jersey that people have told us to throw out, but we’re not going to because you know what, we have a very strong relationship with that thing.” Watch Swinton perform in a striking original Dazed short by Glen Luchford, styled by Katy England: Share Link copied ✔️ More on these topics Fashion Incoming Fashion Week Autumn / Winter 2015 Menswear Tilda Swinton Olivier Salliard Expand your creative community and connect with 15,000 creatives from around the world. The really, really big news is the return of Tilda Swinton to the British stage after literally decades away, as she reprises her role in German playwright Manfred Karge’s Man to Man (Sep 5-Oct 24 2026). Set between the wars, the one-woman show concerns Ella Gericke, a German woman who adopts her late husband’s identity in order to hold on to his decently-paying job as a crane operator. Tilda Swinton was just 27 when it debuted at Edinburgh’s Traverse Theatre in 1987 (it transferred to the Court the following year), and her extraordinary, gender-bending performance cued her up cult big screen career. Following on from this year’s superb Court revival of the original production of Sarah Kane’s 4.48 Psychosis , this is another case of getting the old gang back together – director Stephen Unwin will take the helm for what is literally a reprisal of the original production. Photo: Royal Court Theatre Gary Oldman, Krapp’s Last Tape The other big celebrity name is Gary Oldman, who has been absent from the stage for even longer than Swinton – a whopping 37 years. Or he was until earlier in 2025, when he performed, directed and starred in Beckett’s high concept elegy Krapp’s Last Tape at Theatre Royal York. That gets a transfer to the Court (May 8-30 2026), which would be a good get under any circumstance but has a particular resonance at this address – it premiered here in 1958, and was revived there in 2006 as part of the theatre’s fiftieth anniversary celebrations, with none other than the great Harold Pinter performing the role of Krapp, an elderly man who listens back to the megalomaniacal rantings of his old self with mounting horror. Photograph: Courtesy Julieta Cervantes Sadie Sink in John Proctor Is the Villain Away from the star name revivals, there’s one more obvious jewel in the season crown in the shape of the Court bagging the UK premiere of Kimberley Belflower’s Broadway smash John Proctor is the Villain (Mar 20-Apr 25 2026), a genre-defiant, post-#MeToo riff on The Crucible that was the toast of New York this year. We’re getting Danya Taymor’s Broadway production, although casting is TBA – the US version originally starred Stranger Things ’ Sadie Sink – I’d imagine a homegrown cast for this this is more likely but it’s still damn exciting (Broadway production pictured but don’t hold your breath for Sink). Away from the showstoppers you have a pretty damn exciting regular Royal Court season. The above plays are naturally in the larger Downstairs theatre, as will be Luke Norris’s new hospital-set romantic drama Guess How Much I Love You? (Jan 18-Feb 21 2026), starring Rosie Sheehy and Robert Aramayo and directed by Jeremy Herrin. That opens 2026. Later, Downstairs will host a Lyndsey Turner’s UK premiere production of top US playwright Rajiv Jospeh’s Archduke (Jun 20-Jul 25 2026), about the assassination of Franz Ferdinand. The final Downstairs show of the years will be rising star Ryan Calais Cameron’s The Afronauts (Nov 14-Dec 19 2026), which tells the true story of the landlocked African country of Zambia’s attempts to join the actual ’60s space race. In contrast to all the glittering names Downstairs, the smaller Upstairs theatre will play host to four productions found via the Royal Court‘s open script submission scheme – that is to say the playwrights submitted their scripts to be considered by the theatre, they weren’t commissioned. These will be Jack Nicholls’s The Shitheads (Feb 6-Mar 14 2026, about prehistoric cannibalism); Georgie Dettmer ’s Are You Watching ? (May 29-Jul 4 2026, about digital voyeurism) ; Joy Nesbitt ’s Blood of my Blood (Oct 1-Nov 7 2026, in which a woman attempts to conjure her ancestors) ; and Rhys Warrington’s Monument (Dec 3 2026-Jan 23 2027, Welsh community politics). In addition, there will be a co-production with Berlin's Maxim Gorki Theatre: Yousef Sweid and Isabella Sedlak ’s Between The River and The Sea (Apr 15-May 9 2026), which is billed as ‘a personal story of family, fear, and imagining a future beyond borders’. Tickets for all shows in the Royal Court seventieth anniversary season go on sale at noon on Nov 4. The best new London theatre shows to book for in 2025 and 2026. In 1930s Germany, a woman puts on her dead husband’s trousers and never takes them off. As the world around her changes, she endures war and dictatorship, hunger and humiliation – always fighting to stay alive. More than 30 years after she first brought the role to life, Tilda Swinton makes a long-awaited return to stage as Ella/Max in Manfred Karge ’s Man to Man - the role she originated in the acclaimed 1988 UK premiere at the Traverse Theatre and Royal Court. Prior to the New York run in Spring 2027, the production will transfer to the Berliner Ensemble for a limited run in Germany. The previously announced multi-year exclusive ‘first look’ agreement will see Brian and Dayna Lee working with the Royal Court to develop the future life of productions originating in the Court’s Jerwood Theatre Downstairs. The partnership will increase investment in ambitious new work on the Royal Court's main stage while growing pathways for new plays to reach wider national and international audiences. The other projects Brian and Dayna are producing with the Royal Court this season include the world premiere of Guess How Much I Love You? by Luke Norris , The Shitheads by Jack Nicholls, and Archduke by Rajiv Joseph . NVK / Nate Koch , Jenna Ready, Joanna Pisano will serve as general managers for the New York production of Man to Man. Brian and Dayna Lee are a Canadian born, New York based husband-and-wife team and founders of AF Creative Media, a three-time Tony Award and two-time Olivier Award winning production company. They were recently included in Variety’s Broadway “10 to Watch” for the 2025-2026 Broadway season. Their first collaboration with the Royal Court was Mark Rosenblatt ’s Giant, directed by Nicholas Hytner and starring John Lithgow as Roald Dahl . The production, which won multiple Olivier Awards, including Best New Play, enjoyed sold out runs at the Royal Court’s Jerwood Theatre Downstairs in 2024 and broke capacity and box office records at Harold Pinter Theatre in London’s West End in 2025, now set to transfer to Broadway in 2026. Brian and Dayna Lee ’s other credits include Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre’s Fiddler on The Roof, which received a record-breaking 13 Olivier nominations before transferring to the Barbican. mmeszoros@news-herald.com | The News-Herald PUBLISHED: October 28, 2025 at 6:15 PM EDT | UPDATED: October 28, 2025 at 6:18 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Edward Berger was due for a mediocre hand. The filmmaker has been on a hot streak with his last two directorial efforts, 2022’s German-language adaptation of “All Quiet on the Western Front” and last year’s “Conclave,” both nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture. We expect no such honor for “Ballad of a Small Player,” a reasonably ambitious film that’s a bit more effective as a character study of a gambling addict than a psychological thriller and that never quite gets on a hot streak itself. Landing this week on Netflix after a brief limited theatrical run, the film stars Colin Farrell as Lord Doyle, who, as he puts it in the film’s opening narration, is “a high roller on a slippery slope, a gambler with a pair of lucky gloves washed up on the shores of Macau, the gambling capital of the universe.” Related Articles ‘The Thing With Feathers’ review: Bold examination of grief frustrates ‘Zootopia 2’ review: Sequel has animal magnetism lacking in original Winter movie preview: Holiday fare, this, that, the other — and an ‘Avatar’ ‘Wicked: For Good’ review: More cheers for Chu as he completes adaptation ‘Train Dreams’ review: Edgerton helps make thoughtful ride inviting The name’s fake, of course — “Here, I can be whoever I want to be,” he says — but the debt he’s amassing in Asia’s glitzy and glamorous answer to Las Vegas is quite real. Wearing his distinctive yellow gloves, he is on a bad run playing the punto banco variety of baccarat, in which, as he tells us, the house has only a slight mathematical edge over the player. We can tell from an early shot of his suite in the high-class Wynn Palace that he’s living in luxury but not living well. Under the door, into his messy accommodations — home to empty bottles of booze but decidedly lacking in cash — comes an envelope. The delivery is soon followed by a meeting with a casino manager, who insists he pay the 350,000-plus in Hong Kong dollars he owes or the police will become involved. He bargains for a bit more time but can no longer gamble there. Although he refuses Lord Doyle a complimentary limo, a sympathetic valet advises him he may still be able to get credit at the more modest Rainbow Casino, so after grabbing an umbrella on this rainy evening, he ambles off for that establishment. There, he encounters the mysterious Dao Ming (Fala Chen), a casino employee who, yes, despite all the signs that it’s a bad idea, offers him credit. Predictably, the cards continue to work against him. Worse, Lord Doyle is being hunted by a private investigator, the icy-cold Cynthia Blithe (Tilda Swinton), representing a party also wanting money from him. Tilda Swinton portrays a dogged private investigator in "Ballad of a Small Player." (Courtesy of Netflix) As the story proceeds, set against the backdrop of the Festival of the Hungry Ghost, Dao Ming floats in and out of his life, with Lord Doyle believing a run of good luck will begin at any moment and wanting to share his entirely theoretical winnings with her. Perhaps it’s supposed to be, but it’s rather obvious what truly is happening along Lord Doyle’s journey as he attempts to change his luck — or find another way out of his dire situation. Fala Chen appears in a scene from "Ballad of a Small Player." (Courtesy of Netflix) As a viewer, it’s difficult to fully embrace Lord Doyle, despite some colorful elements to the character. We can’t help but wonder if Farrell felt the same way, as the actor — on a hot streak himself of late with excellent performances in the series “The Penguin” and t he underappreciated recent film “A Big Bold Beautiful Journey” — never quite finds his footing in the role. Colin Farrell's Lord Doyle draws attention with his playing in a scene from "Ballad of a Small Player." (Courtesy of Netflix) “Ballad of a Small Player” is based on the 2014 novel of the same name by Lawrence Osborne, with screenwriter Rowan Joffé (“The Informer”) responsible for the adaptation. Berger doesn’t have as much to work with here as with his previous two films, which are quite different from one another but are both excellently made. Given the quality of the visuals of those two films, it should come as no surprise that “Ballad,” too, is a looker. Berger works again with “Western Front” cinematographer James Friend, who makes art of both the casino settings and the rain-drenched streets of Macau. The film’s final stretch, while not revelatory, is somewhat more satisfying than much of what comes before it, but it’s not enough reason to give this film a strong recommendation. In the punto banco variety of baccarat, a player is dealt two cards, with the best hand adding up to nine. Berger is holding a three and a two, but we’ll bet on a stronger play from him next time. ‘Ballad of a Small Player’ Where: Netflix. When: Oct. 29. Rated: R for language and suicide. Runtime: 1 hour, 42 minutes. Stars (of four): 2. Netflix Debuts Colin Farrell’s New Psychological Thriller Bassyonni ago 27 days The latest Netflix release, “Ballad of a Small Player,” is poised to be a significant entry in the award season lineup. Directed by Edward Berger, an Academy Award winner known for “All Quiet on the Western Front,” this psychological thriller has high expectations attached to it. Key Elements of the Film “Ballad of a Small Player” features an impressive cast led by Colin Farrell, who plays the dual roles of Lord Doyle and Mr. Reilly. Tilda Swinton stars as Cynthia Blithe, a private investigator pursuing Reilly for theft. The film’s score, composed by Academy Award-winner Volker Bertelmann, adds a thrilling backdrop. However, it faces challenges in delivering on its initial promise. Plot Overview The film begins with a gripping premise. In the trailer, Farrell’s character is introduced as a thief on the run, setting the stage for a fast-paced chase. Yet, the actual storytelling unfolds at a slower pace. Key plot twists, like Reilly’s true identity, are revealed far later than expected, which disrupts the film’s tension and flow. Character Dynamics Colin Farrell as Lord Doyle/Mr. Reilly: His performance is the standout aspect, showcasing a dynamic transformation between his two identities. Tilda Swinton as Cynthia Blithe: Her role as a relentless investigator is introduced late, confusing the plot’s build-up. Dao Ming (Fala Chen): Introduced as a potential ally, her character’s rapid familiarity with Doyle feels unearned despite their supposed first encounter. Critique of Storytelling The film suffers from a struggle in tone, oscillating between a psychological thriller and a tightly wound action narrative. While there are moments of intensity, particularly during a pivotal baccarat game in Macau, the storytelling lacks coherence. Despite Farrell’s compelling performance, the film’s overall execution may leave viewers wanting more. Final Thoughts “Ballad of a Small Player” premiered on Netflix and is available for streaming. Although it carries the weight of talent in both the cast and crew, it ultimately may not meet the lofty expectations set by its promotional materials. Tilda Swinton and Gary Oldman return to London stage after 30 years , The Times Tilda Swinton will be reprising her 1988 role in Manfred Karge’s Man to Man ROYAL COURT THEATRE Jessica Sharkey Tuesday October 28 2025, 7.15pm , The Times Today's Quizle Q: Test your knowledge Tilda Swinton is set to return to the stage for the first time in three decades, reprising her 1988 role in Manfred Karge’s Man to Man as part of the Royal Court Theatre’s 70th anniversary season. The actress will return to the production, in which a woman from 1930s Germany impersonates her dead husband, as part of the 2026 season in which Sir Gary Oldman will also star in and direct a revival of Samuel Beckett’s Krapp’s Last Tape . Swinton, 64, will be reunited with Stephen Unwin, the play’s original director, when the Man to Man reprisal runs at Jerwood Theatre Downstairs in central London from September 5 to October 24 before it transfers to the Berliner Ensemble and later a New York run in spring 2027. Swinton in the 1988 production of Man to Man ALAMY Unwin said: “I’ve developed and changed in countless ways since we first staged the play in the 1980s, but it has shaped many of my creative choices ever since.” David Byrne, who is in his third season as artistic director at the Royal Court, said the year-long programme in 2026 would be “the most thrilling season we can imagine” and a “legendary, year-long party” to commemorate 70 years. Advertisement Oldman, 67, last performed at the Royal Court 39 years ago in Carly Churchill’s Serious Money . The production, running from May 8 to May 30, follows Oldman’s performances of the play earlier this year at York Theatre Royal. Each night will open with Godot’s To-Do List , a Beckett-inspired short by Leo Simpe-Asante, winner of the inaugural 2025 Royal Court Young Playwrights Award. Sir Gary Oldman said he was “very honoured” to be starring in the revival ROYAL COURT THEATRE Oldman said: “I’m very excited to be returning to the Royal Court with Krapp’s Last Tape and to share the stage with Leo’s wonderful play Godot’s To Do-List . I’m very honoured and proud to be a part of it.” • I assumed Gary Oldman was a self-obsessed thespian — I was so wrong The production, in which an old man listen to recordings of his younger self, has been performed by acclaimed actors such as Sir John Hurt and Sir Michael Gambon. Advertisement The year will open with the world premiere of Luke Norris’s Guess How Much I Love You and close with Ryan Calais Cameron’s The Afronauts , a play about Zambia’s 1960s space race ambitions, which was described by Byrne as a “masterpiece”. • Tilda Swinton: I still talk to trees Other productions through the season include The Shitheads by Jack Nicholls, Monument by Rhys Warrington, John Proctor Is the Villain by Kimberly Belflower, Between the River and the Sea by Yousef Sweid and Isabella Sedlak, Are You Watching? by Georgie Dettmer, Archduke by Rajiv Joseph, and Blood of My Blood by Joy Nesbitt. Oldman and Swinton in 2011. Both have won academy awards ALAMY Will Young, executive director, said: “Our 70th anniversary isn’t just about the past — it’s a moment to direct every bit of new thinking and resource into the pipeline for the next 70 years. “Collectively, these new projects and partners not only expand our ambitions on stage, but also represent an additional quarter of a million pounds which the Royal Court will invest every year in the future of playwriting, all dedicated to supporting new writers and developing new plays.” Advertisement The theatre also announced a collaboration with BBC Radio 4 and Mark Ravenhill, who made his name with his play Shopping and F***ing , who will curate adaptations of Royal Court plays spanning seven decades of BBC archives. “It’s always been part of what the Royal Court can do for new work … we want to be a place where world-class talent comes.” Addressing concerns over West End “celebrity casting,” Byrne said: “In [the Royal Court’s] very first season George Devine talked Peggy Ashcroft into doing a Brecht, which was a huge departure; we’ve had Olivier in The Entertainer ; when Max Wall came and did Ubu here, he was the biggest musical hall star in the world and the set was designed by David Hockney. Announcing the 2026 season, Byrne told the Guardian: “With anniversaries you need to encapsulate something that is both of the past, of the moment and the promise. All those things need to sit in equilibrium.” The Royal Court has passed through a lot of turbulence in recent years ALAMY Stage shows it can still draw the brightest stars Clive Davis, chief theatre critic Advertisement Is Tilda Swinton about to revive fond memories of a lost masterpiece? Some of the reviews for her 1988 Royal Court performance of Man to Man by the Berliner Ensemble veteran Manfred Karge (sometimes dubbed “the Brandenberg Beckett”) were less than complimentary. One reviewer described the piece as “a rambling mixture of banal reflections”; another dismissed it as a “peculiarly depressing load of old pseudo-Brechtian rubbish”. But the fact that actors as starry as Swinton and Gary Oldman are joining the 70th anniversary season at the Royal Court is a sign that — at a time when AI and CGI are the hot topics in Hollywood, and movie executives fret about dwindling audiences — theatre still has real cachet. The stage is still the place where A-listers leave behind the trappings of celebrity and stand naked, metaphorically speaking at least, in front of an audience. Swinton is not alone in wanting to prove herself on the stage AMY SUSSMAN/GETTY IMAGES If truth be told, the Royal Court has passed through a lot of turbulence in the past five years or so. Vicky Featherstone’s tenure as artistic director dwindled into a series of right-on duds. While David Byrne’s reign has delivered at least one undisputed classic in the form of Giant — Mark Rosenblatt’s portrait of Roald Dahl as an unabashed antisemite — there have been flops too. • Read more from Clive Davis But the Court’s reputation as the home of Look Back in Anger and other convention-busting works of yesteryear means it still has a special place in the theatre constellation. And Swinton and Oldman aren’t alone in wanting to prove themselves on the stage. Four decades after he dazzled audiences with his Henry V , Kenneth Branagh is returning to the RSC next year to appear in The Tempest and Chekhov’s The Cherry Orchard . Wearing a black t-shirt layered with a pair of tailored, loose-fitting trousers, the upcoming actress looked effortlessly chic at the glitzy event. She layered her black ensemble under a long black fur coat and slipped into a pair of leather flats. To complete her red carpet look, the nepo baby toted around her belongings in a large black handbag. But, can you guess which Hollywood star is her mother? Her mother is an Academy Award-winning star and one of Britain's finest acting talents - but do you know who she is? That's right it is Honor Swinton Byrne, whose mother is Academy Award-winning Tilda Swinton, 65 Honor Swinton Byrne's mother is Academy Award- winning actress Tilda Swinton, 65. Tilda and her ex, the late playwright John Byrne are also parents to 28-year-old Xavier Swinton Byrne, who is Honor's twin brother. As the daughter of actress Tilda, Honor has already enjoyed some high-profile roles. Now, she is set for success after landing a role in the new Prime Video miniseries A Very Royal Scandal. The actress, who is set to play the role of Princess Beatrice in the new series, told British Vogue that she had 'buggered up' her audition for the role. She told the publication: 'I was so nervous. I didn't think I looked like her. I was like, I don't know - I'm not really what they're looking for and really kind of b*****ed up, b*****ed up that audition.' Right after her audition, she met her boyfriend at a nearby pub for a pint and told him through tears 'It's okay I didn't want it anyway'. However, just a few days later, she received a phone call saying she had landed the role. Be the first to comment Be one of the first to comment Comments Did YOU guess who it was? Her first starring role was in The Souvenir, a semi-autobiographical film directed by Joanna Hogg in which she stars as Julie, a film school student who embarks on a relationship with an older man. She also starred in the final season of The Crown as a student named Lola Airdale-Cavendish-Kincaid, a clever stand-in for the aristocratic women Prince William was linked to before dating Kate Middleton. Honor, who starred in The Souvenir alongside her mother, admitted that she 'was considered' for the role due to her connections but has since landed other roles for her talent. She told The Times: 'I feel like it’s very important to own it [nepotism]. I completely admit and am grateful for the fact that I was considered for The Souvenir because of my connections.' 'But at the same time, I continue to act and get jobs because I have skill. I’m still doing it.' Honor explained how she was cast by director Joanna, who is a friend of her mother's while working as a florist’s assistant in Inverness. The beauty gushed that it wasn't daunting starring opposite her famous mother but actually 'really fun'. As well as her acting and modelling career, Honor completed a four-year psychology degree at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh. Honor's brother Xavier is also in the movie business but works with the props department. Tilda and Honor's father John split up after 14 years in 2005 but continued to live together while Tilda worked on various blockbusters.
